# Management-Governance Module — NVT (Synthesis)

## Abstract

nVent is run by professional managers who have delivered what they promised and kept the books clean, but who own almost none of the company and have spent five years buying growth. Acquisitions absorbed $3,017.2m against $2,091m of free cash flow, funded partly by selling a 20.5%-margin segment, with no return target published on any deal. Pay rewards relative shareholder return and free cash flow — never return on capital — and directors and officers hold roughly 0.5%, all granted, none bought. The biggest flag is that serial-acquirer pattern; the biggest gap is a missing proxy, which caps the pay read at 50. Verdict: standard, mixed stewardship — competent operators, unproven capital allocators.

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** the acquisition engine has never been shown to earn its cost of capital. $3,017.2m deployed in four years produced an incremental return of **7.6%** (FY2022→FY2025), reported return on capital sat flat at **6.2–6.3%** right through the spending years and is **9.5% LTM** against peers at 13.3–13.6%, and goodwill plus intangibles now equal **117.6% of shareholders' equity** with tangible book value at **−$571.2m** [02-017, 02-018, 11 §12].
- **Strongest bull point (the steelman):** the per-share outcomes actually happened. Normalised diluted EPS went **$1.27 (FY2021) → $2.92 (LTM Jun-2026)**, book value per share $15.03 → $24.63, the diluted share count fell 3.4%, the buyback's biggest year was executed at an average **$52.73** into a drawdown and throttled to zero at $171, 32 consecutive quarterly dividends were paid with three raises and no cut, and indexed total shareholder return was 296.3 against 197.5 for the S&P MidCap 400 Industrials [02-010 to 02-016, 02-021].
- **Single killer risk specific to stewardship:** management is paid on relative TSR and free cash flow with **no return-on-capital gate anywhere in the disclosed design**, while committing $1.75bn + up to $550m to Maverick Power on a publicly stated test of *"accretive to adjusted EPS in the first year"* — a test a debt-funded deal passes while still earning less than the money costs [03-009, 03-032].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** zero impairments have ever been recorded on any deal; the Thermal Management disposal was executed at ~13.3× operating income for a $435.4m pre-tax gain; the Maverick release carries a stated multiple and a falsifiable accretion test, so RF-CAP-001 did not fire; and the accrual battery is clean (Beneish M −2.67 with **0 of 7** components in the manipulator zone, CFO/PAT 0.92–2.08×, effective tax rate 43.9% versus a 25.0% statutory rate). If the acquisitions were being written up rather than earning, none of that would read this way [02-005, 02-009, 11-014, 11-001, 11-010].

## 3. Reconciliation

Four material disagreements. In each, the more conservative reading is taken and the counter-reading is preserved rather than averaged away.

**1. The Pentair cross-link — is RF-NET-003 live? (07 and 12 say no; the checklist item sits Amber.)** `07` graded Pentair plc **Material concerns** as an entity, tested RF-NET-003 against it, and deliberately did not fire it — then left the judgment visible for this synthesis, stating that if `99` reads the linkage as live, the Material-equivalent band binds instead (People & network integrity max 50, Governance risk floor 55, no rating above Watchlist). `12` concurred and did not re-fire. **Adjudicated here: RF-NET-003 does NOT fire.** The trigger's own defined condition is a **live** hop-1 cross-link. On the cited facts the link is historic, not live: nVent separated from Pentair on 2018-04-30 by a pro-rata distribution to Pentair's own shareholders, there is no common control, no common directorship and **$0.0m flowing between the two companies** in any period tested [09 §10]; what survives is legacy equity-plan administration and a 2018 indenture. The alleged conduct sits in **2025–26, seven years after separation, in a Pool business nVent never owned**, and the posture is verbatim *"filed complaints, no ruling on any motion to dismiss found, no adjudication, no admission"* on plaintiff-firm notices — a tier-10 source. Firing an exposure floor on that would be an entity-level version of the namesake error the protocol exists to prevent, and would manufacture a cap against nVent for something another company is alleged to have done. **What would change it:** a court ruling on a motion to dismiss, an SEC action against Pentair, or evidence of a live control, directorship or trading relationship. Recorded, not dismissed.
**Immateriality check, stated so nobody has to re-derive it:** had the Material-equivalent band been applied, People & network integrity would fall 70 → 50 and Governance risk would floor at 55 (below the 60 already binding). The Governance Score would move from 60 to **57.7 → 58** — still the Watchlist band, still the same rating and the same verdict.

**2. The related-party floor — 09 (14) versus 00's declared cap (floor 40).** `00_governance-data-triage` declared "No related-party note → RPT & leakage risk floor 40; Confidence max 80." `09` examined that cap and argued it should not apply, because the RPT position is affirmatively **known and nil** on three independent legs — an audited note set with **no ASC 850 note where a material flow would force one**, the leases note's explicit denial of any related-party lease, and the proxy's *"we had no related person transactions during 2025"* against a self-imposed $50,000 threshold. `09` is right on the evidence and its point is a good one: floor-40 exists for a pool where the position is unknown, not one where it is proven nil. **Reconciled conservatively: the floor is applied anyway (RPT & leakage risk = 40, not 14), because two of the three legs are absence-of-evidence rather than affirmative disclosure and the third sits outside the frozen pool.** This costs nothing analytically and it is honest to say so: **Checklist Risk = max(40, 40, 29, 20) = 40 either way**, because contingent-liability risk already sits at 40. The disagreement does not move the Governance Score by a single point. `09`'s evidence-based read of **14** is reported alongside the floored figure, and the Confidence limb of the same cap row (max 80) binds.

**3. The proxy — absent from the pool (00, 03, 08) but retrieved from outside it (05, 07, 09, 12).** `00` recorded the DEF 14A as absent and declared the caps that follow. `05`, `07`, `09` and `12` each retrieved the 2026-03-31 proxy and the two AGM 8-Ks from EDGAR and answered A1, A2, A5, A6 and A10 from them — which is why checklist coverage is 86% rather than the sub-50% `00` warned about. `03` used outside-pool data too but explicitly held its own cap, writing *"it does not lift the cap."* **Reconciled: the caps stand.** Incentive alignment stays at 50 and Shareholder friendliness at 60, because the cap rows key on what the frozen evidence pool contains, and `05` itself declined to relax either. What the outside-pool retrieval legitimately buys is **coverage, not score relief** — and it is paid for in the Confidence Score, which is held at 74 partly because those governance answers came through a fetch layer rather than a checkpointed pool source [05-039].

**4. The Shareholder-friendliness number — 79 from 05's own scorecard versus 60 after the cap.** `05` scored board and shareholder rights at 79/100 on evidence that is genuinely good (88.9% independent, three 100%-independent committees, independent-only sessions at every meeting, a true majority-vote standard, no pill in force, the Irish frustrating-action ban). `04` separately established that no ownership or insider-transaction data exists in the pool, which triggers "Shareholder friendliness max 60." **Reconciled: 60 binds.** The two readings are not in conflict about facts — they measure different halves of the same score, and the half nobody could measure is the one about whether the people running the company have anything at risk. `05`'s 79 is reported so the master synthesizer can see what the board read alone would have supported.

**No disagreement** between `01` and `06` on candor (both flag the same untested-in-a-bad-quarter limitation), between `10` and `11` on the balance sheet (both name goodwill/intangible intensity as the live exposure), or between `07` and `09` on the network (both ran the A17-08 four-class test independently and both returned zero `disclosable-and-omitted`).

## 5. Stewardship Summary

**Have they delivered and created per-share value?** On operations, yes and it is checkable: adjusted EPS beat the top of their own guidance by 17.2% and 26.1% in consecutive quarters, the ~20% adjusted operating margin target was met at 20.2%, the $1.7bn Thermal Management sale was agreed and closed in six months, and normalised diluted EPS went $1.27 to $2.92 while the share count fell 3.4%. On capital, the record is unproven rather than bad: $3,017.2m of acquisitions — 158.3% of five years of free cash flow, funded partly by selling a 20.5%-operating-margin segment — carry **no published return target and no post-close return on any of the four deals**, and the incremental return on the money actually deployed was **7.6%** against peers at 13–16%, with reported return on capital (ROIC — the profit earned on each dollar invested) flat at 6.2–6.3% right through the spending years. The qualifier travels: most of the per-share gain came from an AI data-centre demand upswing and a well-timed disposal, not from demonstrated deal returns.

**Do incentives and ownership point at per-share value or at size?** At per-share value, on the metrics that are readable — three-year relative total shareholder return against the S&P 400 Industrials paying 0–200%, and free cash flow in the annual bonus. **Nothing readable pays for revenue, absolute EBITDA, headcount or deal count**, dilution is small (0.25–0.42% annual burn, 9.07% overhang), and the share count is falling. Two things pull the other way and both are specific: there is **no return-on-capital gate anywhere in the disclosed design** on a company earning 9.5% ROIC in the middle of a $1.75bn acquisition sold on first-year EPS accretion; and the **weights** behind those metrics are unreadable, because the proxy sits outside the pool. Skin in the game is thin — directors and officers hold roughly **0.5%**, every traceable share of it granted, **zero open-market purchases** anywhere in the record.

**Are minorities protected, and is management candid when results are bad?** Protection is real and mostly structural: one share one vote, no controller, no dual class, 8 of 9 directors independent, three 100%-independent committees, independent-only sessions at every meeting, a true majority-vote standard, no poison pill in force, the Irish ban on frustrating a bid, pledging and hedging contractually prohibited, **nil related-party transactions on three independent legs**, and all 16 AGM resolutions across two years carried on 93.91%–99.92% of votes. Against that: the CEO also chairs the board, and three dormant board-side levers stay alive that shareholders never voted on individually — unilateral power to adopt a pill, 20 million blank-cheque preferred shares whose voting terms the board sets alone, and a 15%/three-year business-combination freeze. On candor, everything testable reads well — the bad number comes before the mitigation, bought growth is separated from earned growth, stock-based compensation is left inside adjusted earnings, and a $25.8m GAAP benefit was **removed** from adjusted in Q2 FY26 — but the decisive test is unrun: both transcripts in the pool cover quarters that beat guidance, so **candor in a bad quarter is Insufficient Data, not proven**, and four "one-off" adjustment categories recur every single year, holding adjusted EPS 28.8% above GAAP with 87% of that gap being the amortisation cost of the acquisition engine itself.

**The single most important reason to trust — or not trust — this team.** Trust them with the operation: eight years of stable leadership, one CFO change handled as a lateral move with the auditor and chief accounting officer both continuous through it, clean books on every accrual, cash and revenue measure, an unqualified opinion on both the accounts and the internal controls, and not one person on a 21-name register carrying a criminal matter, regulator order, sanctions match or undisclosed directorship. Withhold trust on the capital: they have spent three billion dollars of other people's money on four companies, have never published what any of it earned, are paid on nothing that measures whether it earned anything, own almost none of the company themselves, and are about to do it again with borrowed money.

## 6. What Would Change The Stewardship Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Strengthen It | What Would Weaken It | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Standard / mixed** (Governance Score 60; Rating Watchlist; Gate PASS) | (a) A **published post-close return** on ECM, Trachte and EPG showing they earned above the cost of capital — this single item does more than anything else, because it is the specific evidence the serial-acquirer cap exists to demand. (b) A **return-on-capital gate** added to the incentive plan. (c) **Separation of Chair and CEO**, or a Lead Director charter with independent agenda-setting power. (d) **Open-market insider buying** — any at all, since there has been none. (e) The **audit-fee ratio** published and inside 25%, lifting the AuditAssurance cap from 65. (f) A transcript of a genuine miss showing the same candor the beats showed — which would lift Disclosure candor off its "provisional and cycle-conditioned" label. (g) ROIC sustained above the peer band rather than 3.7–6 points below it | (a) **Another material acquisition before the current ones prove out**, especially debt-funded — this would harden RF-CAP-004 from a High flag into a pattern with compounding evidence. (b) A **goodwill impairment**, which would confess overpayment on a $4,469.6m goodwill-and-intangible base already at 117.6% of equity. (c) The **bonds/LC line compounding past $102.0m** with the note paragraph still unchanged — a disclosure-conduct finding, not just an exposure one. (d) Any **person on the register moving to Material concerns or Disqualifying**, which for a controller/CEO/CFO/chair would fail the gate outright. (e) A **restatement, a modified opinion, or an auditor resignation** — all currently clean and all Critical if they occurred. (f) Evidence that the **audit-fee ratio is at or above 100%**, which fires RF-AUD-004. (g) A **court ruling or SEC action** that turned the Pentair matter from an allegation into an adjudicated fact **and** evidence of a live link — both are needed, not either | **In priority order:** (1) the **DEF 14A** collected into the pool (CD&A, metric weights, summary compensation, beneficial ownership, related-person transactions, audit fees — lifts three separate caps at once); (2) the **FY2025 Form 10-K** (audited FY2025, contingency note, post-divestiture Exhibit 21, second CAM, ICFR scope for EPG); (3) **Form 4 and Schedule 13D/13G filings** (insider behaviour, ownership verification, RF-MKT-001/002 testability); (4) **segment economics for ECM, Trachte and EPG** post-close; (5) the **Q3 FY2024 earnings transcript** (the one bad quarter); (6) **PCAOB Form AP** for the nVent engagement (signing partner identity and discipline sweep) |

## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **Stewardship verdict: Standard / mixed.** Strongest single piece of evidence: $3,017.2m of acquisitions in four years = **158.3% of five years of free cash flow**, with **no published return target or post-close return on any of the four deals**, an incremental return on deployed capital of **7.6%** against peers at 13–16%, and a 20.5%-operating-margin segment sold to help pay for it. Competent operators; unproven capital allocators.
- **NON-NEGOTIABLE GATE: PASS**, with 154 of 179 registry items answered (86.0%). All four conditions tested and none met: no hard disqualifier, zero Critical red flags, zero Disqualifying grades on any controller/CEO/CFO/chair, and zero material undisclosed legal matters (0 of 10 found dockets absent from filings; 0 of 53 network subjects `disclosable-and-omitted`).
- **Capital allocation — what the number means:** per-share value WAS created ($1.27 → $2.92 normalised diluted EPS, book value $15.03 → $24.63, share count −3.4%, TSR 296.3 vs 197.5), but **the mechanism was an end-market surge and a well-timed disposal, not demonstrated deal returns** — that qualifier must survive into the thesis. The buyback is the genuinely good decision here: $591.3m at 4.7× the stock-comp charge, the biggest year executed at **$52.73** into a drawdown and throttled to **zero at $171**. That is price discipline visible in the filings.
- **Incentives and ownership — do they point at minority holders?** Partly. The disclosed metrics are per-share and cash-based (relative TSR, free cash flow) and **nothing readable pays for size**. But there is **no return-on-capital gate anywhere** on a team earning 9.5% ROIC mid-way through a $1.75bn deal justified on first-year EPS accretion, the metric **weights are unreadable**, and insiders own ≈**0.5%**, all granted, with **zero open-market purchases** ever found. Alignment here is asserted by policy, not evidenced by stake.
- **The people read:** 21 persons swept — **20 Clean, 1 Minor concerns, 0 Material, 0 Disqualifying**. The riskiest is Lead Director Susan M. Cameron, and the basis travels: *no adverse record against her personally; the grade reflects her Tupperware chairmanship through that company's restatement and Chapter 11, both now ended.* She is not a controller or KMP, so nothing is capped by it. **No §24 Filter 1 signal is open** — `business-model/01` routed none and none surfaced.
- **The checklist read:** 86.0% coverage — 110 Green, 41 Amber, **3 Red** (combined Chair/CEO · contingent-liability trend up 9.5-fold behind unchanged wording · Dechow F-score 1.92), 18 Not Applicable, 7 Insufficient Data. **The binding Checklist Risk is 40**, and it is a **tie between RPT & leakage risk and contingent-liability risk** — but the two are not equivalent: the RPT 40 is a *conservatively applied floor over an evidence-based read of 14*, while the contingent-liability 40 is `10`'s *own earned score*. Treat contingent-liability risk as the substantive binding constraint.
- **Biggest governance risk / red flag:** **RF-CAP-004, High** — the serial-acquirer pattern, which caps Capital allocation at 50 and floors Governance risk at 60. Four further High flags: RF-DISC-002, RF-ACC-001, RF-CL-001, RF-FIN-003. **Zero Critical.**
- **Hard disqualifier from `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`:** none — reported verbatim: *"No verdict-lock. The synthesizer is free to score this business on its merits; nothing in this scan overrides other scores."*
- **§24 rejector filters:** **Filter 4 (serial acquirer) TRIPPED** → Capital allocation max 50, Governance risk floor 60, RF-CAP-004, conviction cap. Filter 1 (integrity), Filter 2 (turnaround) and Filter 6 (unaligned owner) all tested on cited evidence and **not tripped**. Filters 3 (leverage) and 5 (fast-changing industry) belong to balance-sheet-survival and business-model respectively, but note for the roll-up: leverage is **1.15× net debt/EBITDA on the strict §15 basis** today and **~2.43× pro-forma Maverick**, having touched 3.00× at FY2024 and been rescued by a divestiture rather than repayment.
- **Partial-data caps that applied, and what each limits:** *(i)* no proxy in the frozen pool → **Incentive alignment capped 57 → 50** and **Overall usefulness capped at 70** — the pay *weights* are the specific thing nobody can test; *(ii)* no ownership or insider data → **Shareholder friendliness capped 79 → 60** — note `05`'s board-and-rights read alone supported 79, so the cap is about unmeasured skin in the game, not a weak board; *(iii)* no auditor-fee disclosure → **Audit & assurance capped 69 → 65**, and **RF-AUD-004 stands NOT CLEARED, UNTESTED — never read it as clean**; *(iv)* no related-party note → RPT risk floored to 40 over an evidence-based 14 (immaterial to the composite, §3); *(v)* declared breadth overflow → **People & network integrity capped 88 → 70**, with 31 named hop-1 entities and ~130 subsidiaries at scoped depth only; *(vi)* **sweep coverage-limited on three named axes** — 8 of 21 persons unscreened for sanctions, six directors' criminal/insolvency axes not run at Tier-C depth, and Russian-language sources for LLC nVent Rus `unreachable_database`. Confidence Score held at **74**.
- **Biggest missing data point — the single highest-value next request: the DEF 14A (2026-03-31, and the 2025 proxy) collected into the evidence pool.** One document lifts three caps at once — it carries the compensation discussion and metric weights, the beneficial-ownership table, the related-person-transaction disclosure, and the audit vs non-audit fee table. `07` separately nominates Form 4 / 13D-13G filings; those rank second because the proxy answers more of the open items.
- **Explicit handoff:** **this module supersedes the `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance` quick-read.** Treat THIS module's governance verdict, scores and red flags as the **primary governance read**. `business-model/11` could not test pay design at all and scored the affected rows at a conservative default; that hole is now filled to the extent the evidence allows and explicitly capped where it is not. Where the two differ, this module wins.

## 8. Simple Summary

- **Have they done what they said?** Mostly yes, and in 2026 they beat their own numbers badly — adjusted profit per share came in 17.2% and 26.1% above the top of their own forecast two quarters running. But that is execution inside a data-centre boom, not proof they can forecast: they under-called their own year by 25.5% in five months.
- **Has capital created value per share?** Yes on the scoreboard — profit per share went from $1.27 to $2.92 and the share count fell — but the buying itself is unproven. They spent $3,017.2m on four companies, more than five years of spare cash, and have never published what any of it earned. The money they spent earned about 7.6%; rivals earn 13–16%.
- **What does the pay actually reward?** Beating a peer index on share-price return, and generating cash. Nothing pays for revenue, size or doing deals — which is genuinely good. But **nothing measures whether the deals earn anything either**, and the next one is $1.75bn on borrowed money.
- **How much do insiders own, and are they buying?** About **0.5%** — almost nothing — and every share of it was given to them, not bought. **No insider has ever been found buying stock on the open market.** They do sell, but the ordinary way, after results, and the quarter after the last sales was twice as good.
- **Are small shareholders protected?** Largely yes: one share one vote, no controlling owner, 8 of 9 directors independent, no related-party deals at all, no pledged shares, and every shareholder vote passed with 94%+ support. Two things to watch: the chief executive also chairs the board, and the board can issue 20 million preference shares and adopt a takeover defence without asking anyone.
- **Is management honest when results are bad?** Probably — but it has not been tested. Every bad number they do disclose comes with the cause and a fixable plan. The problem is that the only two recordings in the evidence are of good quarters; their one real miss has no transcript. Also, four kinds of "one-off" cost recur every single year.
- **Any hard disqualifier?** **No.** The disqualifier scan found nothing, no person on a 21-name register has a criminal record, regulator order or sanctions match, the auditor's opinions are clean, and there has been no restatement in five years.
- **Is this module useful?** Yes — 86% of the governance checklist was answered and the gate passed with evidence. It is weakest exactly where the missing proxy bites: how much of the pay each metric drives, and what the auditor is paid.

# Governance Data Triage — NVT

**Evidence binding (MODULE_PIPELINE Step 1.5).** `NOSTRA_FROZEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT` is set and the complete quartet resolved (`NOSTRA_FROZEN_POOL_DATA_PATH` = `/Users/admin/nostra-prod/data/NVT`, `NOSTRA_FROZEN_POOL_OUT_DIR`, `NOSTRA_FROZEN_POOL_GENERATION` = `6db32848…1aecd1e6`, `NOSTRA_FROZEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT`). All reads went through that exact generation's `manifest.json`, `corpus.txt`, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json` and its `extract` references. The extractor was NOT re-run; live `data/NVT/` and `analyses/NVT_2026-09-07/_pool_extracts/` were NOT read. `data/NVT/` below is a citation label only.

**Extraction health.** `manifest.totals`: 15 sources, 2 workbooks, 20 tabs, 33 extracts written, **0 failures**. Every source carries `status: "ok"`. No `fail`, no `fallback-text`, no `missing-dependency`, no `gdrive-pointer`. So nothing in this pool is hollow — what is missing is missing because it was never collected, not because extraction broke.

**Two filename traps that a filename-only inventory would fall into (fix F23).** Periods below are read from INSIDE each document, never from the file's sync date.
1. **`nVent Electric plc, 2026.pdf` is NOT a 2026 annual report.** It is the **Q1 FY2026 Form 10-Q** (quarterly period ended March 31, 2026, signed May 1, 2026 by Gary L. Corona) — the same filing as `nVent Electric plc, Q1 2026.pdf`. The pool holds 15 files but **14 distinct documents**; these two are different PDF renderings of one 10-Q (151,205 vs 165,957 extracted chars).
2. **`nVent Electric plc, 2026 rev.pdf` is NOT a company annual report either.** It is a **Form 11-K** — the annual report of the *nVent Management Company Retirement Savings and Investment Plan* for the plan year ended December 31, 2025. It is an employee-benefit-plan filing, not a company filing.

**The single fact that shapes this whole triage.** The pool's only company annual filing is the **FY2024 Form 10-K** (year ended 2024-12-31, filed 2025-02-18). Its **Items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 — directors and corporate governance, executive compensation, security ownership, related-person transactions, and principal accounting fees — are ALL incorporated by reference to the "Proxy Statement for our 2025 annual general meeting", and that proxy is not in the pool.** The governance disclosure this module exists to read was deliberately placed in a document nobody collected.

**Lineage LEAD (not a finding).** The claimed origin (Federal-Hoffman, **1988**) and the "over 100 years" brand-history claim both predate the entity's incorporation date (**2017-05-30**). Under A17-02 that is a lead, not a flag, **and on the face of the pool it looks like the benign case**: the company states the lineage explicitly, names the parent it inherited it from (Pentair), names the 2015 ERICO acquisition Pentair made, and dates the separation. A truthfully-cited group or parent history is expressly not an A17-02 red condition. `07` runs the D-2 test to confirm or reconcile it; **this triage asserts no predecessor entity exists or is concealed** — that conclusion is `07`'s to make once lineage evidence supports it. The tax-residency split is a second D-2/D-5 input: organised in Ireland, "centrally managed and controlled" in the UK, UK tax resident, US management office in Minneapolis, plus a Luxembourg/Netherlands/Switzerland financing chain visible in Exhibit 21.

**Instruction to later agents on regime (Hard Rule).** This is a **US/SEC + Irish-company-law** filer. Do **not** mark India/SEBI instruments — shareholding-pattern filings, promoter pledge/encumbrance disclosures, MR-3 secretarial audit, CARO annexure, SAST/PIT disclosures, scrutinizer reports — as "missing data". They are **genuinely Not Applicable** to this regime. Likewise, "promoter" has no meaning here: nVent is a **widely held professional-management company with no controlling shareholder disclosed in the pool**, so every A3 promoter-holding, promoter-pledge and promoter-group item is answered as *Not Applicable (no promoter/controller under this regime)*, **not** as a red flag and **not** silently Green. Conversely, the genuinely missing US instruments are **DEF 14A, Form 4, Schedule 13D/13G, and the FY2025 10-K** — those are real gaps and are scored as such.

## 6. Sufficiency Verdict

- **Verdict: Partial**

- **Reason:** The filings are present, current at the interim level and clean in extraction (15/15 sources `ok`, 0 failures), and both management track record and multi-year capital allocation are fully assessable — but the FY2024 10-K routes **all five governance items (10–14) to a proxy statement that is not in the pool**, so compensation, beneficial ownership, board independence, related-party transactions and auditor fees have no source at all.

- **Specialists that can run:**
  - **Run substantially unimpaired:** management track record (01) · capital allocation (02) · candor and disclosure quality (06) · audit quality (08, minus the fee items) · contingent liabilities (10) · accounting forensics (11)
  - **Run with the entity-side intact but the person side thin:** people dossiers and network discovery (07) — the seed roster of 21 persons and 155 entities in §5E is unusually complete, every D-1…D-5 anchor is present, and the entity-discovery recipes have full starting material; what is missing is any filing-side biography for the current CFO and any independence/committee data for the 9 directors
  - **Run capped and largely as "Not Available with reason":** incentives and compensation (03) · ownership and insider behavior (04) · board and shareholder rights (05)
  - **Runs on its own external sweep, not on this pool:** regulatory/legal and compliance (12) — the pool contributes only the two contingencies notes and one legal-proceedings item

- **Hard disqualifier already flagged by `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`?** **No.** That scan's §3 Verdict-Lock Signal records: *"No verdict-lock. The synthesizer is free to score this business on its merits; nothing in this scan overrides other scores."* No Governance-risk floor is inherited, and no verdict cap flows from disqualifier deference. `12_red-flags-sweep` separately carries two disclosed-item flags at 52 and 55 (inverted scale) that this module should read and re-test, not re-adjudicate.

- **Active partial-data caps:**
  - No proxy / compensation disclosure → **Incentive alignment max 50; Overall usefulness max 70** (agents 03, 99)
  - No ownership / insider-transaction data → **Shareholder friendliness max 60** (agents 04, 99)
  - No board disclosure beyond the signature-page roster → **board independence and shareholder-rights read not assessable**; A1 and A2 items answered Not Available with reason (agents 05, 99)
  - No auditor-fee / audit-detail disclosure → **A4-06 and A4-07 Not Available with reason; Audit & assurance quality max 65; Confidence Score max 80** (agents 08, 99)
  - No related-party note → **RPT quantification not assessable; RPT & leakage risk floor 40; Confidence Score max 80** (agents 09, 99). The absence is itself an **Amber** disclosure finding — carried with its qualifier: a US filer routinely locates RPT disclosure in the proxy, so this is a pool-collection gap, not demonstrated company opacity
  - **Watch the checklist-coverage cap.** A large share of A1, A2, A3, A6, A10, A12 and A15 will land as Not Available. If the assembled registry coverage falls below 50%, `99` must additionally apply **Data quality max 60 and Confidence Score max 60** — a checklist mostly made of "Not Available" is not a governance read. `99` counts coverage and applies this; triage flags it as the live risk it is.
  - Agents 07 and 12 declare their own external-sweep coverage and apply the coverage-limited caps themselves. Triage applies none on their behalf and does **not** presume the sweep is unavailable.

- **Critical missing items:**
  - **The Proxy Statement (DEF 14A) for the 2025 AGM (held 2025-05-16), and the 2026 proxy** — carries Items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 in full: director nominees and independence, corporate governance matters, committee reports, Compensation Discussion & Analysis, executive compensation tables, security ownership, related-person-transaction policies, insider-trading policy, and audit vs non-audit fees
  - **The FY2025 Form 10-K** — no audited FY2025 financials, no FY2025 auditor's report or CAM, no post-Thermal-divestiture Exhibit 21, and no confirmation of whether FY2024's judgment-driven tax items recurred
  - **Ownership and insider filings** — Schedule 13D/13G (who owns the company) and Form 4 (whether insiders are buying or selling). Zero of both
  - **Any 8-K series** — including whatever disclosed the CFO transition from Sara E. Zawoyski to Gary L. Corona, and 8-K Item 5.07 AGM voting results
  - **Any shareholder letter** — the promise-vs-delivery test must run on guidance and transcripts instead
  - Minor: no rating-agency reports, no proxy-advisor reports, and no dated as-of on the three CIQ RTF exports

- **Single highest-value missing document:** **the DEF 14A proxy statement.** One document restores compensation design and metrics (agent 03, currently capped at 50), beneficial ownership and control (agent 04, capped at 60), board independence, committees, tenure, attendance and voting outcomes (agent 05, currently not assessable), related-party transactions (agent 09, currently a floor-40 unknown), and audit vs non-audit fees (agent 08, A4-06/07). No other single document in any regime would lift five caps at once.

# Management & Track Record — NVT

**Jurisdiction & regime.** nVent Electric plc is incorporated in Ireland, head-officed in London, and files as a **US SEC domestic filer** on the NYSE (Commission file 001-38265), reporting under US GAAP in USD with a fiscal year ending 31 December [FY24 10-K, cover page]. So the US form names — 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A — are the correct local documents here (CLAUDE.md §27). All pool sources are in English; no translation issue arises and no language-based gap is recorded.

**Evidence binding: frozen.** Every pool read resolved through extract generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6` (`manifest.json`, `corpus.txt`, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json`, per-document extracts). Live `data/NVT/` was not read; `data/NVT/` below is a citation label only.

**Two real data limits, named up front.**
1. **No proxy statement (DEF 14A) is in the pool.** The FY24 10-K incorporates Part III Items 10–14 by reference to the 2025 proxy [FY24 10-K, Item 10]. So director bios, the CEO-succession policy, and pay design are unread in this run. That is a genuine gap for board and pay work (agents 03 and 05); it does not block the officer-tenure read, because the 10-K carries its own "Information About Our Executive Officers" table in Part I.
2. **No FY2025 10-K and no 8-Ks are in the pool** [business-model/00_data-triage.md §3, via 01_disqualifier-scan]. The pool's officer table is therefore **as of 31-Dec-2024**, and it predates a leadership reorganisation that the 2026 filings clearly reflect (a different person signs the CFO certifications). Per the module's web rule, the web is used **only** to confirm executive background, appointment dates and tenure, and every such input is labelled web-sourced and unverified. No character judgment is drawn from the web.

**Partial-data cap: not applied to the core test.** Checkable prior promises exist in quantity — dated quarterly and full-year guidance, dated mid-term targets, a dated divestiture commitment — so the "no prior promises" cap does **not** apply here.

There is no promoter block, and the company's own filed policy **prohibits** employees and their family members from pledging company shares [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 19 — Insider Trading Policy]. ## 2. Management Stability

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Senior departures (last 3 years)** | **No senior executive is identifiable as having left the company.** Every one of the eight officers named in the FY2024 10-K table is still traceable to a role at nVent today, either in the pool's own 2026 filings (Wozniak, Corona, Wacker) or via the March-2025 announcement (Zawoyski, van der Kolk). What happened in March 2025 was a **reorganisation, not attrition**: four moves announced on one date (2025-03-11) with staged effective dates — Zawoyski internally promoted from CFO to President of Systems Protection (the ~67%-of-revenue segment), van der Kolk moved into a newly created President EMEA & APAC role, and two external hires, Corona (CFO) and Coleman (President, Electrical Connections). Three of ten senior seats changed hands in a single month, which is a large single-step refresh; the mitigating fact is that two of the three were internal people moving up or across, not out | FY24 10-K, Part I — Executive Officers; Q1/Q2 FY26 10-Q signature pages and certifications; *web-sourced (unverified):* nVent press release 2025-03-11 via MarketScreener / tEDmag |
| **CFO turnover** | **One CFO change in eight years** — Zawoyski (2019–2025) → Corona (2025-03-31). That is **well inside** the module's warning band, which fires on serial exits at one role (for example three CFOs in four years). Two features argue against reading this as a warning: (a) the outgoing CFO did not leave — she took a P&L job running the larger segment, which is the shape of a promotion, not a departure; (b) the Chief Accounting Officer, Wacker, has been continuously in post since 2018 and still signs the accounts, so the accounting seat did **not** turn over alongside the CFO seat. The gatekeeper-cluster pattern (CFO plus auditor or company secretary leaving inside 12 months) does **not** apply: Deloitte & Touche LLP has audited nVent since 2017 and is still the auditor [FY24 10-K, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, 2025-02-18], and the General Counsel/Secretary is unchanged since 2018. **Caveat:** no 8-K covering the CFO transition is in the pool, so the reason given and the exact terms are web-sourced, not filing-verified | FY24 10-K, Part I; Q1 FY26 10-Q, Ex. 31.2, 2026-05-01; *web-sourced (unverified):* nVent press release 2025-03-11 |
| **Chief Accounting Officer succession — announced, then reversed** | On **2026-06-17** nVent disclosed that CAO Randolph Wacker would retire on 2026-09-01, with Tyler Krutzig to succeed him. On **2026-08-14** the board reversed that: Wacker "decided to stay with the Company" and was re-appointed SVP & Chief Accounting Officer effective 2026-09-01, the same date his retirement was to take effect; Krutzig stays as Assistant Corporate Controller. Net effect is continuity in the accounting seat. The **process** wobble is real and worth one line: a named successor to the top accounting officer was announced and unwound inside two months. Nothing in the pool or the disclosure ties it to an accounting problem — internal controls were reported effective with no change to internal control over financial reporting in the most recent quarter [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Item 4] — so this is graded **Amber on process, not Red**, and it does not trip RF-MGT-001/002 (no CFO, secretary or compliance-officer resignation occurred) | *Web-sourced (unverified):* nVent Form 8-K reported 2026-08-14 (via StockTitan) and the 2026-06-17 predecessor announcement; corroborated in the pool by Wacker's signature as CAO on the Q2 FY26 10-Q, 2026-07-31 |
| **CEO succession / continuity** | Wozniak has been CEO since the 2018 spin — **~8.4 years, the entire life of the company as a separate business** — and has been Chair since 2023. **No CEO-succession policy is readable in this run** because the proxy is absent; that item (A1-13) belongs to agent 05 and is recorded here as Insufficient Data rather than assumed either way. What the data *does* show is a visible internal bench: the CFO seat was filled in one step while the incumbent moved to run the largest segment, and the segment/regional layer is fully named | FY24 10-K, Part I; FY24 10-K, Item 10 (Part III incorporated by reference to the proxy — not in pool) |

**Warning check, stated plainly.** The module asks specifically for frequent CFO turnover and unexplained departures. Neither is present. One CFO change in eight years, with the predecessor retained inside the company and the Chief Accounting Officer and auditor both continuous, is the opposite of the pattern the flag exists to catch. **No red flag is raised on management stability.**

## 3. Stated Strategy & Targets

Management's stated plan is to narrow nVent to a "connection and protection" electrical company and point it at fast-growing end markets — data centres and electric utilities above all — funding that with internal investment plus bolt-on acquisitions, while selling what does not fit. The portfolio moves back this up rather than merely describing it: Thermal Management sold, and ECM (2023), Trachte (2024), Avail's Electrical Products Group (2025) and Maverick Power (agreed 2026) bought [FY24 10-K, Item 1 — History and Development; Q1 FY26 10-Q, Note — Electrical Products Group Acquisition; "nVent to Acquire Maverick Power" release, 2026-08-24]. The share of sales in the infrastructure end market has gone from **12% at the 2018 spin, to 45% in 2025, to nearly 60% in the first half of 2026** [2026 William Blair deck, 2026-06-03, slides 6–7; Q2 FY26 transcript, 2026-07-31, prepared remarks].

**The explicit, checkable targets.** At its **March 2026 Investor Day** nVent launched **2028 Value Creation Targets** — restated at the William Blair conference on 2026-06-03 [2026 William Blair deck, slide 18; corroborated on the call: "We significantly raised our mid-term financial targets at our Investor Day in March", Q1 FY26 transcript, 2026-05-01, prepared remarks (CFO Corona)]:

| 2028 target | New level | Deck's stated change vs the previous target | **Previous target (derived by subtraction — arithmetic shown)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organic sales growth (growth excluding acquisitions and currency) | **+10–13% a year** | +6.5 pts | 10−6.5 to 13−6.5 = **+3.5–6.5%** |
| Inorganic sales growth (growth bought through acquisitions) | **>3 pts** | +2 pts | **>1 pt** |
| Adjusted operating margin — "return on sales" (ROS), operating profit as a share of sales, on the company's own adjusted basis | **~22%** | +2 pts | **~20%** |
| Adjusted EPS growth (excluding future acquisitions) | **+17–20%** | +9.5 pts | **+7.5–10.5%** |
| Free-cash-flow conversion (free cash flow as a share of adjusted net profit) | **~95%** | **−5 pts** | **~100%** |

The subtraction is mine, from the deck's own stated deltas, and is labelled as such — the prior target table itself is not in the pool. Note the shape: **four targets raised, one cut.** The one cut is cash conversion.

Near-term, the company also guides quarterly. Current standing guidance, given 2026-07-31: FY2026 reported sales growth **+37–39%**, organic **+32–34%**, adjusted EPS **$5.00–5.10**, capex **~$130m**, free-cash-flow conversion **90–95%**, tariff cost **~$100m** to be offset by price and productivity; Q3 FY2026 sales growth **+32–35%** and adjusted EPS **$1.35–1.38** [Q2 FY26 transcript, prepared remarks; `CIQ Estimates→Guidance`, guidance date 2026-07-31]. Leverage policy is stated as a **2.0–2.5x net-debt-to-EBITDA target range**; the company sat at **1.2x** at 2026-06-30 [Q2 FY26 transcript, prepared remarks].

**The honest read on the guidance record — both sides of it.** Management has beaten every guide it has set in 2026, by 17% and then 26% above the top of the range, and it has raised the year twice. That is real delivery and it is filed, not asserted. But the same record says the company's own February-2026 forecast was **25.5% too low at the midpoint within five months**, and its organic-growth guide moved from +10–13% to +32–34% over two calls. Beating a number you set ninety days ago inside an unusually strong demand upswing is evidence of operating execution; it is **weak** evidence of forecasting discipline, and the two should not be conflated. The base rate makes the point: in the four years before this, full-year adjusted-EPS surprise was **+0.5%, +1.0%, −0.4% and +0.6%** — that is a company whose full-year guide normally converges almost exactly. The 2026 pattern is the end market moving, not management's forecasting getting better. Both readings must survive together.

**A cross-module note, not a score.** Four material acquisitions in four years — ECM ~$1.1bn (2023), Trachte $687.5m (2024), EPG $979.6m (2025), Maverick $1.75bn + up to $550m (agreed 2026) — against FY2025 revenue of $3,893.1m, is a **serial-acquirer pattern** on its face and engages CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 4. Sizing that pattern, its per-share outcome, and any RF-CAP-004 flag belong to `02_capital-allocation-scorecard`; this agent records the pattern and **routes it**, and does not double-score it. Two facts that agent will need from here: the deals have so far been funded from cash and disposal proceeds rather than stretched debt — net leverage was **1.2x at 2026-06-30 against a stated 2.0–2.5x target range** — and returns on capital, while rising (**ROIC 6.7% in 2021 → 7.2% in 2025 → 9.5% LTM to 2026-06-30**), remain **below** peers' third-party-computed 13.3–13.6% [`ciq_facts.json` `multi_year_trajectory`; business-model/08_competitive-map.md §2d].

## 4A. Turnaround & Integrity Tests (CLAUDE.md §24, Filters 1 & 2)

| Test | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Is the thesis a turnaround (struggling business + new management / new plan)? | **No.** This fails the turnaround definition on both halves. The business was not struggling: operating cash flow was positive in each of the last four years (+$394.6m FY2022, +$528.1m FY2023, +$643.1m FY2024, +$465.2m FY2025), the auditor's opinions are unqualified, and there is no going-concern language anywhere in the corpus. And the management is not new: the CEO has run the company for its entire ~8.4-year life as a separate business, and the plan being executed (narrow the portfolio, aim it at infrastructure) has been running since at least 2019, visible in a dated deal sequence, not in a freshly announced programme. **Classification: a company-specific thesis carried by an end-market cycle — not a governance-turnaround** | business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md rows 1 and 8; FY24 10-K, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, 2025-02-18; 2026 William Blair deck, slide 7 |

Read against it, gross margin has gone the other way — 38% (2021) → 40% (2024) → **37% LTM** — so the margin improvement is at the EBITDA line, not the gross line, and that contradicting series is named rather than averaged away (CLAUDE.md §3) | `ciq_facts.json` `multi_year_trajectory` and `margin_trend` — CIQ vendor export, tier 5 |

(not evidence) | **No — and the distinction is enforced here.** The William Blair deck's own framing ("Strong Track Record", "Proven Acquisition Track Record", "confident in our plans") is company marketing language and is given **zero** weight in this report. Every kept promise scored above is a dated guide or commitment matched to a filed or transcript-verified outcome. The CEO's Honeywell/Pentair résumé and the CFO's Medtronic/General Mills résumé are recorded as background only and **support no conclusion about future delivery** | 2026 William Blair deck, slides 15, 17, 19; this report §4 |

Nothing in the filings, the two FY26 transcripts, the decks, or the vendor exports raises an allegation against the controller or senior management." **Turnaround rule (Filter 2) — outcome.** The filter does **not** trip. No turnaround base-rate penalty is applied and no Management Quality cap at 60 is triggered. **But the reason it does not trip is worth stating precisely, because the adjacent risk is real and belongs somewhere:** what is unproven here is not management's competence, it is the **durability of the demand** they are executing into. Organic growth of +34% and +47% in two consecutive quarters, driven by AI data-centre capital spending, is not a base rate anyone should extrapolate, and the promise-vs-delivery record above was earned almost entirely inside that upswing. The correct classification is **company-specific with a heavy sector/technology-cycle overlay** (§14), and the cycle-dependence question routes to the master synthesizer, not to a management penalty here. Scoring this agent penalises what management controls: it is not paid extra for the cycle, and it is not docked for it either.

**Integrity rule (Filter 1) — outcome.** Nothing to chase, nothing unresolved, nothing suppressed. **No `RF-MGT-005`.** Person-level integrity beyond the résumé — registry sweeps, litigation, disqualification checks on each named individual — is owned by `07_people-integrity-dossiers` and is deliberately not duplicated here; if that agent's sweep could not run, its own coverage caps apply, not this one's.

## 5. Management Read

nVent is run by a CEO who has been in the seat for the company's entire ~8.4-year independent life and a senior team whose median time at the company is about 8.4 years, refreshed in one deliberate step in March 2025 rather than churned — the only CFO change in eight years moved the incumbent sideways into running the biggest segment rather than out of the door, and the Chief Accounting Officer and the auditor both stayed put through it, so the gatekeeper-exit pattern that this test exists to catch is simply absent. On promises, the record is **mostly kept and, in 2026, beaten hard**: adjusted EPS came in 17.2% and 26.1% above the top of the guided range in two consecutive quarters, the ~20% adjusted operating margin target was met at 20.2% in 2025, the $1.7bn Thermal Management sale was agreed and closed within six months, and a specific segment-margin recovery promised in May was delivered in July — set against one clear miss (Q3 FY2024, −22.2% on adjusted EPS), one year of organic growth below the then-standing target (+2.4% in FY2024), and a cash-conversion target quietly cut from ~100% to ~95% while every other target was raised.

The single biggest management signal is **positive but must be read with its qualifier attached**: this team beats the numbers it sets, and it has also been badly wrong about those numbers in the conservative direction — the FY2026 EPS midpoint rose 25.5% in five months — which means the delivery on show is operating execution inside an extraordinary AI data-centre demand upswing, not demonstrated forecasting skill. In the four years before this cycle, full-year adjusted-EPS surprise ran +0.5%, +1.0%, −0.4%, +0.6%; that, not 2026, is the base rate for how well they forecast. The one thing to watch, and it is a watch item rather than a warning: four material acquisitions in four years against a $3.9bn revenue base, executed by a team whose returns on capital (9.5% LTM) still sit several points below the peers it is buying alongside.

## Management Quality Score

| Component | Score | Max Score | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Stability and tenure | **17** | 20 | CEO in post ~8.4 years, the full independent life of the company; median senior-team tenure 8.4 years at the company and 5.0 years in role; **one** CFO change in eight years, with the predecessor retained as a segment president and both the CAO (since 2018) and the auditor (Deloitte since 2017) continuous through it — no gatekeeper-exit cluster [rows 01-001, 01-004, 01-006, 01-007]. Held below full marks for two things: three of ten senior seats changed in one month (March 2025), and the CAO succession was announced 2026-06-17 then reversed 2026-08-14 [row 01-008] |
| Promise-vs-delivery | **22** | 30 | **Kept:** Q1 FY26 adjusted EPS +17.2% and Q2 FY26 +26.1% above the top of their own guided ranges [01-010, 01-011]; ~20% adjusted operating margin target met at 20.2% in 2025 [01-013]; $1.7bn Thermal Management sale agreed 2024-07-31 and closed 2025-01-30 [01-016]; the May-2026 segment-margin recovery promise delivered in July [01-018]; the tariff-offset promise delivered two quarters running [01-019]. **Against:** FY2024 organic growth 2.4%, below the then-standing 3.5–6.5% band, with one segment shrinking organically [01-014]; the one clear miss, Q3 FY2024 adjusted EPS −22.2% [01-020]; the cash-conversion target cut from ~100% to ~95% while four others were raised [01-015]; and the FY2026 guide itself was 25.5% too low at the midpoint within five months, against a four-year base rate of near-exact full-year guides [01-012]. The M&A "exceeded expectations" claims carry partial credit only, because no published target exists to test them against [01-017] |
| Execution record | **20** | 25 | Sales +53% in each of Q1 and Q2 FY2026 (organic +34% and +47%); adjusted operating income +53% and +61%; return on sales 20.0% then 21.9%; free cash flow +21% then +125% year on year; net leverage 1.2x at 2026-06-30 against a stated 2.0–2.5x target range, after funding a $979.6m acquisition from cash; capacity delivered (Blaine, Minnesota plant in production from Q1 FY26) [Q1 and Q2 FY26 transcripts, prepared remarks]. Discounted for three named facts: ROIC of 9.5% LTM is still **below** peers' 13.3–13.6% and was flat at 6.2–6.7% for four years pre-cycle; gross margin fell 38% (2021) → 37% (LTM) even as EBITDA margin rose 20% → 22%; and the two headline quarters sit inside one AI data-centre demand upswing [01-025, `ciq_facts.json` `margin_trend` / `multi_year_trajectory`] |
| Succession / depth | **11** | 15 | A named, credentialed second level exists and was tested once in real time: the CFO seat was refilled in a single step (external hire) while the incumbent moved to run the 67%-of-revenue segment, and a division president was hired from 3M into the other segment [01-005]. Held down because **no CEO-succession policy is readable** — the proxy is absent — the CEO also chairs the board, and the CAO succession was announced and then unwound inside two months [01-008, 01-026] |
| Transparency around misses | **7** | 10 | Misses and cost increases are disclosed with numbers rather than adjectives: Electrical Connections ROS down 390 bps year on year in Q1 FY26 with the cause named, the tariff estimate raised from ~$80m to ~$100m openly, and the guidance-implied Q4 sequential decline defended under direct analyst challenge rather than deflected [Q1 and Q2 FY26 transcripts; earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md §3]. Held down because the 25.5% under-forecast of its own year has never been framed as a forecasting error, and the prepared remarks lean heavily on "outstanding / tremendous / record". Note this component is deliberately narrow — the full candor read is owned by `06_candor-and-disclosure-quality` |
| **Total** | **77** | **100** | Band 61–80 = "strong / low risk" (MODULE_RULES Scoring Rules). Traceable to rows 01-001 through 01-026 |

**Caps checked and none applied.** The turnaround cap (Management quality max 60) does not apply — Filter 2 does not trip [01-022]. The unresolved-integrity cap (Management quality max 60) does not apply — nothing was routed and no `RF-MGT-005` is emitted [01-023]. The "no prior promises/guidance" partial-data cap does not apply — dated guidance and dated mid-term targets exist and were tested [01-009]. The absent proxy caps `03` (incentive alignment) and `05` (shareholder friendliness), not this score.

**One thing this score does NOT claim.** 77/100 is a judgment on stewardship of what management controls — tenure, stability, doing what they said, and running the operation. It is **not** a claim about how durable the demand behind the 2026 numbers is, and it must not be read as one. That question is the master synthesizer's.

# Capital-Allocation Scorecard — NVT

**Reporting currency: USD.** All figures in USD millions unless stated. nVent Electric plc is incorporated in Ireland, tax-resident in the UK, and files as a **US SEC domestic filer** on the NYSE (Commission file 001-38265) under US GAAP with a 31-December fiscal year [FY2024 10-K, cover page]. The correct local documents are therefore US forms — 10-K, 10-Q, DEF 14A (CLAUDE.md §27). Every pool source is in English; no translation issue arises and no language-based gap is recorded.

**Evidence binding.** All pool reads resolved through frozen extract generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6` (`manifest.json`, per-document extracts, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json`). Live `data/NVT/` was not read; `data/NVT/` below is a citation label only.

**Two data limits, named up front, and what they do to this scorecard.**
1. **The FY2025 Form 10-K is not in the pool.** FY2025 *annual* cash-flow lines (acquisitions $975.7m, buybacks $253.1m, dividends $130.4m, debt repaid $873.3m) come from the Capital IQ workbook — a tier-5 vendor export (§4), not a filing. Where a filing covers the same fact it is used instead and cited as the filing: the H1 2025 comparatives in the Q2 FY26 10-Q independently confirm buybacks of $253.1m, dividends of $65.7m, acquisitions of $971.6m and debt repayments of $866.3m [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, six months ended 2025-06-30]. Confidence on the vendor-only rows is capped at 3.
2. **No proxy statement (DEF 14A).** That does not bind this agent — capital allocation is read from cash-flow statements, equity statements and the repurchase/dividend notes, all of which are present. It does mean the **compensation link** to capital-allocation metrics is agent `03`'s to answer, not answered here.

**Multi-year history IS available** (five fiscal years, FY2021–FY2025, plus H1 FY2026 from filings), so the MODULE_RULES "no multi-year capital-allocation history → cap 65" rule does **not** apply. A different cap does apply, and it is stated in §5 and in the score table.

**Basis note (§15).** FCF = CFO − total capex. Two CFO bases exist in the evidence and they are **not** interchangeable:
- **Continuing-operations CFO (the filing's own basis)** — used as primary here, because the company's own free-cash-flow reconciliation is struck on it [FY2024 10-K, MD&A "Other financial measures"; earnings/01_historical-financials.md §Reporting basis].
- **Total-company CFO (Capital IQ basis)** — includes discontinued operations. FY2025 total-company CFO of $465.2m is stated *after* a −$183.8m discontinued-operations outflow, most plausibly the tax on the Thermal Management gain [CIQ Financials→Cash Flow, "Net Cash From Discontinued Ops.", FY2025]. Leading with $465.2m would understate the recurring cash the operations throw off, so the normalised continuing-ops figure ($649.0m, implied by the filed FY2025 FCF of $555.7m plus $93.3m capex) leads, and the total-company figure is shown alongside, labelled.

## 1. Uses of Capital (FY2021–FY2025, five years)

Percentages are against **cumulative continuing-operations CFO of $2,218.8m** and **cumulative continuing-operations FCF of $1,905.9m** (CFO $2,218.8m − capex $312.9m). On the Capital IQ total-company basis, cumulative CFO is $2,404.3m and FCF $2,091.4m — both shown so no reader mixes them.

**What the table says in one line.** Acquisitions alone absorbed **158.3%** of everything the business generated after capex over five years. **Serial-acquirer + opportunity-cost test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 4) — the filter TRIPS.**

Four material deals in four years — ECM ~$1,100m (2023), Trachte $687.5m (2024), EPG $979.6m (2025), Maverick $1,750m + up to $550m (agreed 2026) — against FY2025 revenue of $3,893.1m. Cumulative cash acquisitions of $3,017.2m over FY2021–FY2025 were **158.3% of five-year free cash flow**; add Maverick and the four-year committed deal total reaches roughly **$4.5bn**. Most M&A destroys value, and that base rate — not the company's own narrative — is the yardstick here.

The **opportunity cost** is not hypothetical. A whole reporting segment earning a 20.5% operating margin was sold, and the proceeds went straight into EPG, of which **89.4% of the purchase price** is goodwill and intangibles. Group-wide, goodwill ($2,676.3m) plus other intangibles ($1,793.3m) now total **$4,469.6m — 62.5% of $7,146.3m of total assets and more than the $3,986.9m of total equity**, leaving tangible book value at **−$482.7m** [CIQ Financials→Balance Sheet, 2026-06-30]. And the ECM deal's tracking basis has been removed by a segment re-cut: the segment it was bought into no longer exists as a reported line.

**Two things that argue the other way, named rather than averaged away (CLAUDE.md §3).** First, **no goodwill or intangible impairment has ever been recorded** — "no impairment expense recorded in 2024, 2023 or 2022 related to goodwill" and none on identifiable intangibles [FY2024 10-K, Note 2 and Note 5 accounting-policy notes]. There is no accounting confession of overpayment yet. Second, the Maverick release is **not** bare synergy language: it states a multiple (11.5×/10.5×), a revenue base, and a falsifiable first-year accretion test. That is more disclosure than the previous three deals carried, and it is why **RF-CAP-001 ("large acquisition with vague rationale") is NOT triggered** — the rationale is thin on returns but it is numerically checkable. What is still missing across all four deals is any **return-on-invested-capital target or post-close return disclosure**, which is why no deal in the table can be scored "delivered" on evidence.

**Verdict on the filter:** serial-acquirer pattern **confirmed on the deal count, the cash intensity relative to internally generated cash, and the funding source (a divested segment)**. It is at the milder end of the band on one dimension — the deals are not "near or above the company's own value" ($4.5bn of deals against a $27,703.6m market capitalisation at a $171.16 share price [CIQ Financials→Key Stats, Current Capitalization]) and three of four were funded from disposal proceeds and cash rather than stretched debt. That mitigates severity; it does not switch the filter off. **RF-CAP-004 fires at High severity**, the M&A-discipline component is capped, and the module Score Cap Rule "Serial-acquirer pattern → Capital allocation max 50" is applied to the total in §5.

**RF-CAP-002 test ("buybacks not reducing share count") — NOT triggered over the period.** The share count is down 2.5% on the outstanding basis and 3.4% on the weighted-diluted basis, and buybacks ran at 4.7× the SBC charge. The H1 FY2026 stub, where a $50.4m repurchase was more than offset by equity-comp issuance, is recorded **Amber with a follow-up**, not Red: $50.4m against a 161.7m share base is 0.2% of the company and one half-year is not a pattern.

**Authorization hygiene.** Two live board authorizations, each dollar-capped and time-limited, each disclosed with monthly purchase detail in Item 5 / Item 2 of every filing: the 2024 Authorization ($500.0m, 2024-07-23 to 2027-07-22, $96.5m remaining at 2026-06-30) and the 2026 Authorization ($500.0m, 2026-07-23 to 2029-07-22, board-approved 2026-05-16) [FY2024 10-K, Note 14; Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15]. Under Irish law, buybacks and dividends can only be paid out of "distributable reserves" on the parent's statutory balance sheet — **$2.4bn at 2024-12-31, down from $2.7bn at 2023-12-31** [FY2024 10-K, MD&A "Share repurchases / Dividends"]. That balance is a real, jurisdiction-specific constraint on future distributions and is falling; it is not a GAAP number and does not appear in the retained-earnings line.

**The number that disagrees, adjudicated by name (CLAUDE.md §3).** The 22.6% incremental return over the last 18 months is the headline management would want. It should not be read as proof the acquisitions work, for three reasons that are all in this report's own tables. **First, the denominator is artificially small:** the Thermal Management sale returned $1,586.8m of cash that paid down $873.3m of debt and bought EPG, so invested capital rose only $1,079.0m while EBIT jumped — the ratio flatters because capital was *recycled*, not just added. **Second, the numerator is cycle-driven:** LTM revenue is up 46.2% year on year and organic growth ran +34% and +47% in two consecutive quarters on AI data-centre demand [`ciq_facts.json` `multi_year_trajectory`; management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md §4]. **Third, the longer window contradicts it:** over FY2022→FY2025 — the years the ECM, Trachte and EPG money actually went out — incremental return was **7.6%**, and the vendor-computed ROIC sat flat at 6.2–6.3% right through FY2022–FY2024. Two windows, two answers, and the longer one covers the spending. The honest read is that **the acquisition programme has not yet been shown to earn a return above any plausible cost of capital across a full window; the recent number is real but is measured inside an extraordinary demand upswing and after a disposal shrank the capital base.**

## 4A. Distribution Conduct (A10-05)

| Test | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism rationale stated (dividend vs buyback, who benefits)? | **Yes — a stated, repeated framework, though not an explicit dividend-versus-buyback economics comparison.** Management publishes a capital-allocation slide (Slide 9) and states the ordering verbatim on consecutive calls: "Our capital allocation priority is growth, and that starts with reinvesting in the business by funding capacity expansion, innovation and the capabilities required to win in high-growth verticals… while maintaining the balance sheet flexibility to consistently return capital to shareholders," followed by the actual amounts — "Through the first half of the year, we returned $118 million to shareholders, including share repurchases of $50 million, and we have increased our quarterly dividend by 5%." Leverage policy is stated as a **2.0–2.5× net-debt-to-EBITDA target range**, against 1.2× actual at 2026-06-30. *(The company's own phrase for this is "disciplined capital allocation"; it is quoted here as management's words and is not adopted as this report's judgment — the per-share outcomes in §5 are.)* **What is absent:** any statement of why buyback rather than dividend at a given price, and any per-share value test | Q2 FY26 earnings call, 2026-07-31, prepared remarks (CFO Corona); Q1 FY26 earnings call, 2026-05-01, prepared remarks |
| Promoter participation in any buyback (tender/open-market) | **Not applicable — no promoter or controlling shareholder exists**, and the mechanism forecloses the abuse in any case. nVent is a 2018 spin-out of Pentair with a **single class of ordinary shares**, 161,857,939 outstanding at 2026-06-30, 11,711 holders of record at 2024-12-31, and $12.6bn of market value held by **non-affiliates** at 2024-06-28. Every repurchase in the record was **open-market under a dollar-capped board authorization — there has been no tender offer**, so no shareholder can be selectively bought out. Monthly purchase detail (share count, average price, programme-versus-tax-withholding split) is published in Item 5 / Item 2 of every 10-K and 10-Q | FY2024 10-K, cover page and ITEM 5; Q2 FY26 10-Q, cover page and ITEM 2; FY2024 10-K, Note 14; Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15 |
| Buyback timing vs promoter pledge / stake changes | **Not applicable — pledging is prohibited by the company's own filed policy.** "Company personnel, their Family Members and anyone else… are prohibited from… pledging Company Securities as collateral for a loan," alongside a hedging ban and a ban on standing/limit orders. There is therefore no pledge to time a buyback around. Insider *transaction* data is separately unavailable in this pool (`insider_net_activity` and `insider_open_market` both `status: missing`) and belongs to agent `04`; that gap does not affect this test, because the pledge prohibition is filed and the buybacks were open-market | FY2024 10-K, Exhibit 19 — Insider Trading Policy, "Specific Prohibition Regarding Special Transactions, Including Hedging and Pledging"; `<GENERATION_ROOT>/ciq_facts.json` |

**A10-05 verdict: Green.** The mechanism is open-market repurchase under a disclosed, dollar-capped, time-limited board authorization plus a uniform per-share dividend — both of which pay every holder of the single share class on identical terms. There is no controller, no tender, no pledge, and the monthly execution detail is filed. The framework rationale is stated and repeated. The one thing missing from the green band's spirit — an articulated reason for choosing buyback over dividend at a given price — is noted as the follow-up, not as a downgrade.

## 5. Capital-Allocation Read

Over five years nVent put **$3,017.2m into buying other companies — 158.3% of everything the business generated after capex** — and $312.9m, one-ninth of that, into its own plants; the gap was funded by $610.8m of net new debt and by selling a segment that was earning a **20.5% operating margin** on $622.7m of sales, which is the textbook shape of selling the geese to buy a hen. The **best** use of capital was the buyback: $591.3m spent at 4.7× the stock-comp charge, cutting the diluted share count 3.4%, with the largest single year ($253.1m) executed at an average of **$52.73** into the H1-2025 drawdown and the buying deliberately throttled to $50.4m at ~$126 and then to zero as the shares ran to $171.16 — that is price conduct visible in the filings, not a claim. The **worst** was the acquisition programme: four material deals in four years, not one of them carrying a published return target or a post-close return disclosure, 89.4% of the EPG price landing in goodwill and intangibles, group intangibles now 62.5% of assets against negative tangible book, and an incremental return on the money actually deployed of **7.6% over FY2022–FY2025** against peers computed at 13–16% — the 22.6% incremental return of the last 18 months is real but is measured after a disposal shrank the capital base and inside a demand upswing that produced +47% organic growth in a single quarter.

**The single biggest capital-allocation signal: the serial-acquirer pattern (RF-CAP-004), and specifically that the next deal is the first one to be funded with fresh debt.** Maverick Power at $1,750m plus up to $550m of earnout, funded with cash on hand and new borrowing under a Bank of America bridge, would take a balance sheet currently at 1.24× net debt/EBITDA toward the top of management's own stated 2.0–2.5× range — while the three deals already done still have no disclosed return to show for them.

**Conclusion: MIXED.** Per-share value has been created — normalised diluted EPS went $1.27 (FY2021) → $2.12 (FY2025) → $2.92 (LTM Jun-2026), book value per share $15.03 → $24.63, share count down 2.5%, dividend never cut and raised three times, indexed total shareholder return 296.3 at end-2024 against 197.5 for the S&P MidCap 400 Industrials — but the mechanism that produced most of it was an end-market surge and a well-timed disposal, not demonstrated returns on the $3bn of acquisitions, and the returns evidence that does exist puts nVent 3.7–6 points below its named peers on return on capital, a gap that has persisted five years.

**Source conflicts, shown rather than smoothed.** (1) FY2022/FY2023 buyback dollars differ between the equity statement ($63.3m / $58.8m) and the cash-flow statement ($65.9m / $60.8m) — a settlement-timing difference; the equity-statement figure is used for the price calculation because it is the one paired with the share count in the same table, and both are shown. (2) `ciq_facts.json` reports net debt/EBITDA of 1.28× on the CIQ vendor net-debt basis while the CIQ Ratios tab reports 1.24×; both are shown and neither is presented as the filing's own number. (3) CIQ places the $1,584.5m Thermal Management inflow in "Other Investing Activities" with its "Divestitures" row empty; the filing's own figure ($1,586.8m net cash proceeds) is used and cited to the filing.

## management-governance / 03_incentives-and-compensation.md

_Source: `03_incentives-and-compensation.md`_

# Incentives & Compensation — NVT

**Jurisdiction & regime.** nVent Electric plc is incorporated in Ireland, head-officed in London, and files as a **US SEC domestic filer** on the NYSE (Commission file 001-38265), reporting under US GAAP in **USD**, fiscal year ending **31 December** [FY24 10-K, cover page]. The correct compensation documents here are therefore the US ones — DEF 14A (proxy) for pay design and magnitude, 10-K for plan accounting and the compensatory exhibits. India's Companies Act Sec 197 caps and SEBI LODR Reg 17(6)(e) promoter-pay gates **do not apply to this issuer**; the local equivalent gate is the Dodd-Frank §951 advisory say-on-pay vote plus the Item 402(v) pay-versus-performance disclosure. Every A6 band below is applied on that basis and says so. All sources are in English; no translation issue arises and no language-based gap is recorded (CLAUDE.md §27).

**Evidence binding: frozen.** Every pool read resolved through extract generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6` (`manifest.json`, `corpus.txt`, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json`, and its `extract` references). Live `data/NVT/` and `analyses/NVT_2026-09-07/_pool_extracts/` were **not** read. `data/NVT/…` below is a citation label only.

---

## PARTIAL-DATA CAP APPLIED — read this before the numbers

**No proxy statement (DEF 14A) is in the data pool.** The FY2024 10-K places Items 10–14 — including the entire Compensation Discussion & Analysis, the Summary Compensation Table, and the pay-ratio disclosure — outside the document, incorporated by reference to the "Proxy Statement for our 2025 annual general meeting" [FY24 10-K, Item 11, p.76; corroborated in `00_governance-data-triage.md`, §2]. That proxy was never collected. **The exact metric weights inside the annual bonus and the long-term incentive plan are therefore not readable from the pool, and no weight in this report is invented.**

Per `MODULE_RULES.md` Partial-Data Rules and Score Cap Rules, **Incentive alignment is capped at 50/100** and Overall usefulness at 70. The cap is applied on the pool basis and is **not** lifted by anything sourced from the web below.

**Three source classes are used, and they are never mixed.**
1. **Pool filings** (highest weight): the FY2024 10-K including its compensatory exhibits (the RSU, PSU and stock-option award agreements, the Non-Employee Director Compensation policy, the Insider Trading Policy), and the Q1/Q2 FY2026 10-Qs. These carry the plan *design* — vesting, performance condition, change-of-control triggers, recoupment, dilution.
2. **Outside-pool SEC filings, fetched from EDGAR and labelled web-sourced** (confidence 3–4): the 2025 AGM Form 8-K voting results (2025-05-16) and the pay-versus-performance XBRL data inside the DEF 14A filed 2026-03-31. These are primary documents, but they were not in the frozen pool and did not go through the extractor, so they are labelled and do not lift the cap.
3. **Third-party web aggregators** (confidence 2, unverified): the FY2024 CEO pay breakdown and the CEO-to-median ratio. These are used for benchmarking context only, flagged inline every time, and never carry a Green verdict on their own.

---

## 1. Compensation Structure

Reporting currency **USD**. Fiscal years end 31 December. Latest annual filing in the pool: **FY2024 10-K** (filed 2025-02-18). Latest interim: **Q2 FY2026 10-Q** (filed 2026-07-31).

| Executive | Base | Annual Bonus | Long-Term Incentive | Cash vs Equity Mix | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| **CEO — Beth A. Wozniak** (CEO since the 2018 spin from Pentair; also Chair since 2023) | **Not in pool.** *Web-sourced, unverified:* $1,045,114 (FY2024) | **Not in pool.** *Web-sourced, unverified:* $1,337,700 (FY2024) — a Management Incentive Plan award, which an SEC Summary Compensation Table would report under "non-equity incentive plan compensation", not "bonus" | **Not in pool.** *Web-sourced, unverified:* $7,000,022 (FY2024) = option awards $1,749,988 + stock awards $5,250,034 | *Web-sourced, unverified, FY2024:* **cash ≈ 25.9%** (salary 11.1% + incentive 14.2% + other 0.6%), **equity ≈ 74.1%**; **non-salary ≈ 88.3%** of the $9,440,866 total | Structure: FY24 10-K, Note 16 (Share-Based Compensation), p.71–73; Exhibit Index items 10.5, 10.15, 10.22–10.24. Amounts: *web-sourced (unverified)*, salary.com NVT executive-pay page, retrieved 2026-09-07 |
| **CFO — Gary L. Corona** (effective 2025-03-31) | Not in pool | Not in pool | Not in pool | Not assessable | FY24 10-K predates the appointment; Corona signs the Q1/Q2 FY26 certifications [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Ex.31.2, 2026-07-31]. `01_management-and-track-record.md`, §1 |

**Two arithmetic checks on the web-sourced CEO figures, because a number nobody can rebuild reads as invented (CLAUDE.md §15).**
- The five components sum exactly: 1,045,114 + 1,337,700 + 1,749,988 + 5,250,034 + 58,030 = **$9,440,866**.
- Inside the $7,000,022 of long-term incentive, options are **25.0%** and stock awards **75.0%** — which reconciles precisely with the separately web-reported target mix of **50% performance share units / 25% stock options / 25% restricted stock units**. Two independent web sources agreeing to the dollar on an internally consistent split raises confidence in the *shape* of the package. It does not make either one a filing.
- **A discrepancy that must be stated, not smoothed.** The pay-versus-performance data inside the DEF 14A filed 2026-03-31 reports the CEO's FY2024 Summary Compensation Table total as **$9,833,132** — $392,266 above the aggregator's $9,440,866. The gap is most likely a line the aggregator omits (change in pension value / deferred-compensation earnings). **Where the two disagree, this report uses the SEC figure** and treats the aggregator only for the component split.

**What the pool itself establishes about the structure.** The long-term incentive programme is a combination of **restricted stock units, performance share units and stock options** granted under the **nVent Electric plc 2018 Omnibus Incentive Plan**, which shareholders approved in 2018 and amended (to increase the authorised share count to 18.5 million) in 2020 [FY24 10-K, Note 16, p.71]. The annual bonus runs through the **nVent Electric plc Management Incentive Plan**, whose description is an exhibit incorporated by reference to an October-2023 10-Q and is **not in the pool** [FY24 10-K, Exhibit Index, item 10.5, p.79]. Severance sits in two instruments, both named in the exhibit index and **neither in the pool**: individual **Key Executive Employment and Severance Agreements** for Wozniak and the other named officers, and the **nVent Management Company Severance Plan for Executives** (effective 2019-03-01, amended and restated 2023-09-18) [FY24 10-K, Exhibit Index, items 10.6, 10.12, 10.15, 10.21].

**Company-wide equity cost, which IS in the pool.** Share-based compensation expense was **$27.3m in FY2024**, up from $21.8m (FY2023) and $23.3m (FY2022) — RSUs $14.0m, PSUs $7.9m, options $5.4m [FY24 10-K, Note 16, p.71]. That is **0.91%** of FY2024 revenue of $3,006.1m and **5.4%** of FY2024 operating cash flow from continuing operations of $501.0m [derived; revenue from CIQ Income Statement tab, FY2024 column — tier-5 vendor export; cash flow from FY24 10-K, MD&A free-cash-flow reconciliation, p.32]. In the first half of FY2026 the expense was **$23.1m**, against $20.1m a year earlier, with the company stating the step-up came from "substantive vesting at the grant date for certain retirement eligible employees" [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 14, p.22].
