## 2. Performance Metrics

| Plan | Metric | Weight | Per-Share/Returns or Size-Based? | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **Annual bonus** (Management Incentive Plan) | **Free cash flow** — stated by the company as "used as a criterion to measure and pay annual incentive compensation." nVent defines free cash flow as net cash from operating activities of continuing operations **minus** capital expenditures, matching the CLAUDE.md §15 definition | **Not disclosed in the pool** | **Per-share supporting / cash-based.** Free cash flow is the cash left after the business pays for its own equipment — the money available to pay dividends, buy back shares or repay debt. It is not a size metric | FY24 10-K, MD&A — "Other financial measures", p.32; **restated in the current filing**: Q2 FY26 10-Q, MD&A — "Other financial measures", p.30 |
| **Annual bonus** | Any other Management Incentive Plan measures and their weights | **Insufficient Data** | Cannot classify | FY24 10-K, Exhibit Index item 10.5 — description incorporated by reference to the Oct-2023 10-Q, not in pool |
| **Long-term incentive — performance share units (PSUs)** | **Three-year total shareholder return (TSR) relative to the S&P 400 Industrials**, with payout ranging **0% to 200%** of the target number of units based on nVent's TSR ranking (dividends assumed reinvested) against that index, over a three-year service period. This was the metric on the awards actually granted in **2022, 2023 and 2024** | *Web-sourced, unverified:* **50%** of the CEO's target long-term incentive value | **Per-share / returns-based.** Relative TSR is the return a shareholder actually earns — share-price change plus dividends — measured against a peer index, so it cannot be won by getting bigger alone | FY24 10-K, Note 16 — Performance share units, p.72 |
| **Long-term incentive — stock options** | No performance condition. Exercise price is set **equal to the market value of the shares on the grant date**; options vest one third a year over three years and expire ten years after grant | *Web-sourced, unverified:* **25%** | **Per-share (share-price linked).** Pays only if the share price rises above the grant-date price — but it is not indexed, so a rising market alone can pay it | FY24 10-K, Note 16 — Stock Options, p.72–73 |
| **Long-term incentive — restricted stock units** | No performance condition. Vest one third a year over three years, subject to continued employment; dividends accumulate and are paid on earned awards | *Web-sourced, unverified:* **25%** | **Neither.** A retention tool that gives share-price exposure; it pays out in full for simply staying | FY24 10-K, Note 16 — Restricted stock units, p.71 |
| **Non-employee directors** | Fixed cash retainers plus a **fixed-dollar-value** RSU grant vesting at the next annual general meeting. No options. No performance-conditioned pay | Fixed | **Not applicable — fixed, by design.** This is the intended structure for independent directors: it keeps them from being paid on the same short-term measures they are supposed to police | FY24 10-K, **Exhibit 10.14 — nVent Electric plc Non-Employee Director Compensation** |

### The two things that matter most in this section

**First: what IS disclosed is genuinely per-share, not size-based.** The only performance condition attached to any equity award in the last three grant years is *relative* total shareholder return — a per-share, market-relative measure that a company cannot clear by buying revenue. The annual bonus explicitly carries a free-cash-flow criterion, stated in the company's own current filing, not in a marketing document. Nothing readable in the pool pays management for revenue, absolute EBITDA, headcount, or deal count.

**Second, and this is the real gap: there is no return-on-capital metric anywhere in the disclosed design.** No ROIC, no ROCE, no return-on-invested-capital hurdle appears in Note 16, in any of the three filed award agreements, or in the free-cash-flow language. That matters here for a specific, dated reason:

- nVent's own return on invested capital is **9.54% (LTM to 30 June 2026)** — the profit it earns on each $100 of capital employed [CIQ Financials → Ratios tab, LTM 12 months Jun-30-2026 — tier-5 vendor export, as read in `business-model/08_competitive-map.md`, §2d].
- On **2026-08-24** nVent agreed to buy Maverick Power for **$1.75 billion**, plus **up to $550 million** of extra cash tied to performance in 2027 and 2028. The company's stated financial test in the announcement is that the deal will be **"accretive to adjusted EPS in the first year"** [`nVent-to-Acquire-Maverick-Power-2026.pdf`, press release, 2026-08-24]. No return-on-capital hurdle is disclosed.
- A large, partly debt-funded acquisition can raise earnings per share and lift relative TSR while earning **less than the cost of raising the money**. That is the classic gap between an EPS test and a returns test. **Nothing in nVent's disclosed pay design pushes back on it.**

**A third point, flagged rather than scored: the plan's authorised menu is far broader than the awards actually granted.** The filed PSU award agreement lists the measures the committee is permitted to choose from, and the list includes plainly size-based ones — "revenue growth; sales growth (including organic sales growth); … earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization; operating income; … market share" alongside the returns-based ones ("return on equity; return on investment; return on invested capital (including after-tax); total stockholder return") [FY24 10-K, **Exhibit 10.24 — Performance Share Unit Award Agreement**, footnote 1]. The committee has therefore *reserved the right* to pay on size without a further shareholder vote. It has not used that right in 2022, 2023 or 2024. Both facts belong in the record.

## 3A. Statutory & Code Pay Gates (A6-01, A6-02, A6-05, A6-06, A6-09)

**Regime note applied first (`MODULE_RULES.md`, Regime & structure nuance).** The registry's numeric bands for A6-01 and A6-02 are the India/SEBI defaults. nVent is Irish-incorporated and files as a US domestic issuer, so the Companies Act Sec 197 caps and the LODR Reg 17(6)(e) promoter-pay gates **have no legal application here**. They are recorded Not Applicable *with the reason*, and the equivalent local test — the say-on-pay advisory vote plus the pay-versus-performance disclosure, and the "pay rising while profit falls" limb of A6-01 which is regime-neutral — is run in their place and shown with its numbers.

| Test | Raw value | Band applied | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **A6-01 — Aggregate managerial pay vs the statutory cap** (India: Sec 197 — 11% aggregate; ≤5% single MD/WTD, ≤10% all executives, NEDs ≤1%/3%; loss years per Schedule V) | Statutory-cap limb: **no such cap exists in this regime**. Regime-neutral limb, run in its place — CEO reported pay as % of net income: FY2022 **1.98%** → FY2023 **1.57%** → FY2024 **2.96%** → FY2025 **1.94%**. Profit did **not** fall for two consecutive years: net income fell in FY2024 ($567.1m → $331.8m) and rose in FY2025 ($710.2m) | India Sec 197 bands **Not Applicable — Ireland/US regime**. Regime-neutral limb: Green = stable as % of profit and no cap breach; Red = pay rising while profit falls 2+ consecutive years | **Green** (on the applicable limb) | FY24 10-K, cover page (jurisdiction). Pay: DEF 14A PvP XBRL, *web-sourced, outside pool*. Net income: CIQ Income Statement tab, FY2022–FY2025 |
| **A6-02 — Promoter-executive pay vs the extra gates** (India: LODR Reg 17(6)(e) — ₹5cr or 2.5% of net profit individually, 5% aggregate) | LODR limb: **Not Applicable — nVent has no promoter and no controlling shareholder.** It is a widely held 2018 spin-out of Pentair with a single class of ordinary shares; $12.6bn of market value was held by non-affiliates at 2024-06-28. ## 4. Incentive Alignment Read

**What the pay actually rewards, on the evidence that exists: beating a peer index on total shareholder return, and generating free cash.** The only performance condition on any equity award granted in 2022, 2023 or 2024 is three-year relative TSR against the S&P 400 Industrials, paying 0–200% — and nVent beat that exact index by 98.8 index points over five years, so management was paid for clearing the bar it was actually set. The annual bonus carries free cash flow as a stated criterion in the company's own current filing. Nothing readable pays for revenue, absolute EBITDA, headcount or deal count; equity dilution is small (0.25–0.42% annual burn, 9.07% overhang) and the share count is falling, not rising; the clawback, the double-trigger, the absence of gross-ups, and the outright ban on hedging and pledging are all real and all filing-sourced; and shareholders backed the pay design with ~95.2% support.

**The single biggest incentive signal is what is missing rather than what is there: no return-on-capital measure appears anywhere in the disclosed design.** A company earning 9.54% on invested capital has just agreed to pay $1.75bn plus up to $550m more for Maverick Power, justified publicly as "accretive to adjusted EPS in the first year" — a test a debt-funded deal can pass while still earning less than the money costs. Relative TSR and EPS accretion will both reward that deal if the share price cooperates; nothing in the pay plan penalises it if the returns do not.

**Conclusion: mixed.** The metrics that are disclosed are returns/per-share-based, not size-based — that part is a genuine positive and is stated without hedging. What holds the verdict at mixed is threefold and specific: the weights behind those metrics are unreadable from the pool, so "how much" of the pay each metric drives cannot be tested; there is no capital-efficiency gate on a management team in the middle of its largest acquisition; and the two magnitude signals that do exist — CEO pay growing ~6 percentage points a year faster than per-share earnings, and a ~307× pay ratio — both sit above where a reader would want them while resting on sources too weak to grade Red. **Incentive alignment is scored 50/100 under the no-proxy cap; the uncapped read on the evidence assembled here is 57.**

# Ownership & Insider Behavior — NVT

**Evidence binding.** All pool reads went through the frozen extract generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6` (`manifest.json`, `corpus.txt`, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json` and its `extract` references). Live `data/NVT/` and `analyses/NVT_2026-09-07/_pool_extracts/` were not read; `data/NVT/` below is a citation label only. Reporting currency USD; fiscal year ends 31 December; US GAAP.

**Jurisdiction (CLAUDE.md §27, MODULE_RULES Jurisdiction-Aware Source Mapping).** nVent Electric plc is Irish-incorporated, NYSE-listed, and files as a **US domestic filer** (Form 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K / DEF 14A / Form 4 / 11-K, Commission file 001-38265), with an Irish Companies Act 2014 and Irish Takeover Rules overlay [FY24 10-K, cover page and Exhibit 4.7]. India/SEBI instruments — shareholding-pattern filings, promoter pledge/encumbrance disclosures, SAST/PIT disclosures, ASM/GSM surveillance lists — are **genuinely Not Applicable to this regime**, not missing data. The word "promoter" has no meaning here: there is no controlling shareholder disclosed anywhere in the pool. Where an A3 item tests a promoter construct that does not exist, it is answered Not Applicable with the reason; where the item has a real US/Irish equivalent (pledging, float, one-share-one-vote, stake-disclosure hygiene), that equivalent is applied and named.

**The gap that shapes this report.** The pool's only annual company filing is the **FY2024 Form 10-K**, and its Item 12 (Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management) is **incorporated by reference to the "Proxy Statement for our 2025 annual general meeting"** — a document that is not in the pool [FY24 10-K, Item 12]. There is no DEF 14A, no Schedule 13D/13G, no Form 4, and no Capital IQ ownership export (`ciq_facts.json`: `insider_net_activity`, `insider_open_market`, `top_institutional_holders`, `institutional_ownership_trend` all `status: missing`). Per the Partial-Data Rule, the ownership and insider-behavior read is capped, and the web was attempted for the beneficial-ownership and Form 4 record — everything so obtained is labelled web-sourced and unverified below.

**Red-flag gating (fix F20).** No RF-OWN or RF-MKT red flag in this report is fired on a web- or memory-sourced figure. Every red-flag decision below traces to a pool filing or is recorded as "not fired — no pool source". The web-sourced insider-transaction record is reported as labelled context only, and it caps the "recent insider behavior" component of the Ownership Alignment Score to Insufficient Data / Low confidence.

**Total insider ownership: approximately 0.5% of shares outstanding — a derived figure, not a filed one.** The arithmetic, shown so a reader can rebuild it (§15): the FY24 10-K cover page states aggregate market value of equity **held by non-affiliates** of **$12,611,244,553** at a closing price of **$76.61** on 2024-06-28 → **≈164.62 million non-affiliate shares**. FY2024 basic weighted-average ordinary shares outstanding were **165.5 million** [FY24 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations], and 165,022,146 shares were outstanding at 2024-12-31 [FY24 10-K, cover page]. The residual — shares the company itself classified as affiliate-held — is therefore **roughly 0.9 million shares, about 0.5%**. Two qualifiers travel with that number and must not be dropped: (a) the two inputs carry **different as-of dates** (a 2024-06-28 price and value against a full-year average share count), so this is an order-of-magnitude read, not a precise stake; (b) "affiliate" is the company's own determination for the cover-page test, which is not identical to the proxy's beneficial-ownership definition. What the arithmetic does establish, and the web cross-check independently supports at 0.33%, is that **insider ownership at nVent is well under 1% of the company** — roughly $150 million at the $171.16 share price, spread across a board and an executive team of at least eighteen people.

**Share count and its direction.** 165,022,146 shares outstanding at 2024-12-31 → 161,720,452 at 2026-03-31 → **161,857,939 at 2026-06-30** [FY24 10-K cover; Q1 FY26 10-Q cover; Q2 FY26 10-Q cover]. That is a **1.9% reduction over eighteen months**, achieved through buybacks of $253.1 million (4.8m shares) in H1 2025 and $50.4 million (0.4m shares) in H1 2026, against continuing equity-plan issuance [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note on Share repurchases]. Buyback capacity: $96.5 million remaining under the 2024 authorization at 2026-06-30, plus a fresh $500.0 million authorized on 2026-05-16 [Q2 FY26 10-Q].

**Dilution overhang (context for "granted, not bought").** At 2024-12-31 the 2018 Omnibus Incentive Plan carried **4,108,862 securities issuable** (3,250,661 options, 514,940 RSUs, 343,261 PSUs) at a **$30.64 weighted-average exercise price**, plus **10,866,980 shares remaining available** for future issuance — **14,975,842 shares, or 9.1% of the 165.0m then outstanding** [FY24 10-K, Item 12, equity compensation plan table]. Against a $171.16 share price, that option strike is deep in the money, which is exactly why the visible insider record is exercise-and-sell rather than purchase. (Grant design, burn rate and vesting terms are agent `03`'s item A6-04; they sit in the absent proxy and are not adjudicated here.)

## 2. Insider Transactions (last 12 months)

**Pool evidence first.** The pool contains **no Form 4 and no insider-transaction data of any kind**. What it does contain is the Item 408(a) trading-arrangement disclosure in each periodic filing, which is a genuine pool-sourced statement about insider trading conduct:

| Period | Pool disclosure | Source |
|---|---|---|

| Q2 2026 | Same — none adopted or terminated | Q2 FY26 10-Q, Part II Item 5 (Item 408(a)) |

So in every period the pool covers, **no insider put a new pre-set selling plan in place and none tore one up** — the latter being the signal that matters, because a terminated 10b5-1 plan ahead of news is a classic conduct flag. Q1 2025, Q2 2025, Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 are not covered by any filing in the pool.

**Net insider activity: net selling — on web-sourced evidence only, and therefore recorded as Insufficient Data for scoring purposes.** Two distinctions the report structure requires, kept separate:

1. **Open-market buys vs option exercises.** There are **no open-market purchases** in the visible record. Every acquisition is an option exercise at strikes of $20.22–$25.34 against a market price above $160 — a pay event, not a conviction event. Most exercises are same-day sales of the identical share count (Wozniak: 46,261 acquired, 46,261 disposed on 2026-08-05), which is a cashless exercise, not accumulation.
2. **Elective sales vs pre-set 10b5-1 sales vs tax withholding.** The pool's Item 408(a) disclosures say **no director or Section 16 officer had a 10b5-1 plan adopted or terminated** in Q4 2024, Q1 2026 or Q2 2026, which means the May and August 2026 sales are most likely **discretionary window trades, not pre-set plan sales**. That is a slightly weaker signal than plan-driven selling, because the timing was chosen. It is not, however, evidence of misconduct: the company's Insider Trading Policy opens the trading window "one full trading day after the public release of the Company's quarterly or annual financial results", requires **pre-clearance by the General Counsel for every director and Section 16 officer**, and the May 4–13 cluster falls precisely inside the window that opened after the 2026-05-01 Q1 release [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 19 — Insider Trading Policy]. The trades line up with the mechanism the company discloses, not against it.

**Did selling precede bad news? No — the opposite, on the evidence available.** The May 2026 sales cluster was followed by a Q2 print of **diluted EPS from continuing operations of $1.32 versus $0.65 a year earlier**, and net income from continuing operations of $215.8m versus $106.7m [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income]. Consensus EPS breadth for FY2026 was **6 up / 0 down over the last month** and revenue breadth **14 up / 0 down** [CIQ Estimates → Revisions]. **RF-MKT-001 (insider selling before a weak result) is NOT triggered** — and could not be triggered on this evidence in any case, because the transaction record is web-sourced (fix F20).

## 3. Pledging & Encumbrance

| Insider | Shares Pledged | % of Their Holding | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| All directors, executive officers, Company personnel and their Family Members | **0 — pledging is contractually prohibited** | **0%** | FY24 10-K, Exhibit 19 — nVent Electric plc Insider Trading Policy, "Specific Prohibition Regarding Special Transactions, Including Hedging and Pledging" |

**No pledging disclosed — and, better than that, pledging is banned by a filed company policy.** The exact language: "Company personnel and their Family Members are prohibited from holding Company Securities in a margin account or otherwise pledging Company Securities as collateral for a loan" [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 19]. The same clause prohibits hedging — prepaid variable forward contracts, equity swaps, collars, puts, calls, short sales — and prohibits standing and limit orders. The single carve-out is narrow and disclosed: "transactions designed to facilitate portfolio diversification, such as investments in exchange funds, are permitted for non-management directors but not other Company personnel." That is the one channel through which a non-management director could economically reduce exposure without an open-market sale; the pool discloses no such transaction.

**Tested against the graded thresholds, not a flat line (A3-02).** Warning line ≥25% of holding pledged: **not reached (0%)**. SAST-style detailed-declaration trigger — ≥50% of holding or ≥20% of total capital: **not reached (0%)**. Any quarter-on-quarter increase: **none (0% in every period covered)**. Pledge invocation, which would be Critical: **none**. Verdict Green, and it is a genuine Green rather than an absence-of-data Green, because it rests on a filed prohibition rather than on a silent disclosure.

**Cross-reference to the disqualifier scan.** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md` tested "pledged insider shares ÷ insiders' own holding = **0% vs the >50% threshold**", answered **N**, and cited the same Exhibit 19 prohibition. This report reaches the same conclusion from the same primary source and does not re-adjudicate it. `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` recorded promoter pledging as "Not applicable — Irish-incorporated, NYSE-listed company with a single class of ordinary shares and no promoter or controlling-shareholder construct", which is consistent.

The pool discloses **none issued**. This is a real minority-dilution power held by the board, and it is disclosed rather than hidden | FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4.7 |

Whether a lead independent director exists as the counterweight is **not disclosed anywhere in the pool** (it would sit in the absent proxy). Flagged here as context; A1-02/A1-03 belong to agent `05` | `management-governance/00_governance-data-triage.md`, §5E; FY24 10-K signature page |
| Controlling-owner objective alignment *(Filter 6)* | **No trip. Not government-controlled, not a listed subsidiary of a value-maximizing parent, not a sprawling unrelated conglomerate** — see the test below | FY24 10-K, cover page and Exhibit 4.7; CIQ Financials → Segments |

**Unaligned-owner test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 6).** All three structures are tested and none applies.

(a) **Government control** — no state or state entity holds any disclosed interest; the shareholder register the pool reveals is 11,711 holders of record with no bloc at or above 10% [FY24 10-K, Item 5 and cover page]. Not applicable.

(b) **Listed subsidiary of a parent** — nVent Electric plc is the **ultimate parent** of the group. Exhibit 21 lists 138 subsidiaries, all 100% owned except two minority stakes nVent itself holds *in* other companies (Iceotope Group Limited 5.2%, Torgoterm AD 19%), and no entity sits above the listed company [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 21; `00_governance-data-triage.md`, §5E entity roster]. There is no parent to steer economics toward, and no pyramid: the promoter-investment-company layer the A3-03 test looks for does not exist. Not applicable.

(c) **Sprawling unrelated-diversified conglomerate** — two reportable segments, **Systems Protection $2,593m (67%) and Electrical Connections $1,300m (33%)** of $3,893m FY2025 revenue, both in electrical connection and protection, with 81% of revenue in the Americas [CIQ Financials → Segments; `ciq_facts.json` `segments_revenue`, `geographic`]. That is a focused two-segment industrial, not unrelated diversification. Not applicable.

**Conclusion: RF-OWN-004 is NOT triggered, no shareholder-friendliness cap flows from Filter 6, and no value-trap note goes to the valuation module on ownership-alignment grounds.** The value-trap read this filter exists to catch — persistent cheapness under a misaligned owner — does not arise here, and the market is in any case not pricing this name cheaply (EV/LTM EBITDA 26.2x, P/LTM EPS 47.5x [`ciq_facts.json`]). The honest statement of the residual risk runs the other way: with no controlling owner and insider ownership under 1%, **nobody at this company has a personal balance-sheet reason to care about the share price**; alignment has to come from pay design, which sits in the absent proxy and which agent `03` could not test.

## 4B. Ownership-Structure Hygiene (A3-08, A3-09, A3-10)

| Test | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Promoter-group classification (any reclassification to "public"? persons-acting-in-concert complete?) | **Not Applicable — the construct does not exist in this regime.** There is no promoter or promoter group, no SEBI LODR Reg 31A reclassification mechanism, and no persons-acting-in-concert declaration to test. The US/Irish analogue — an affiliate determination — is made on the 10-K cover page and implies affiliate holdings of roughly 0.9m shares (~0.5%); no bloc is being parked or relabelled | FY24 10-K, cover page; `00_governance-data-triage.md`, regime instruction |
| Beneficial-ownership chain (ultimate owners identifiable? trusts/offshore layers?) | **No opacity evidenced; the register itself is not in the pool.** nVent Electric plc is the ultimate parent — no trust, offshore vehicle or holding layer sits above it [Exhibit 21, 138 subsidiaries, all below the listco]. Irish law gives the company an enforceable power to serve notice requiring any person to disclose their interest in its shares, with court-ordered restrictions (transfers void, voting suspended, dividends withheld) for non-response [Exhibit 4.7]. What is missing is the **beneficial-ownership table**, which lives in the absent proxy, and any 13G. That is a pool-collection gap, not company opacity — and per CLAUDE.md §27 a fact that is disclosed elsewhere is not opaque | FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4.7 and Exhibit 21; FY24 10-K, Item 12 (incorporated by reference) |
| Takeover-code disclosure hygiene (India: SAST Reg 29; here: Section 16 / 13D-G + Irish Takeover Rules) | **Mechanism compliant; the delinquency record itself unread.** The company states that "Reports of beneficial ownership filed by our directors and executive officers pursuant to Section 16(a) of the Exchange Act are also available on our website" [FY24 10-K, Available Information], and it made the required Item 408(a) trading-arrangement disclosure in all three periods the pool covers. Irish-side limits are disclosed and none is near: mandatory offer at **30%** of voting rights, Substantial Acquisition Rules capping stake-building speed, 1% accelerated disclosure in an offer period — against a largest disclosed holder of ~9.1%. **No holder is anywhere near the 75% ceiling the Indian band tests.** The one thing not verifiable: the "Delinquent Section 16(a) Reports" statement is a proxy caption, and the proxy is absent, so late-filing hygiene is not positively confirmed | FY24 10-K, Available Information; FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4.7; Q1 and Q2 FY26 10-Qs, Item 408(a) |

## 5. Ownership / Insider Read

**Skin in the game is thin and it was granted, not bought.** Directors and officers together hold roughly 0.5% of nVent — a figure derived from the 10-K cover page rather than read off a proxy, and cross-checked at 0.33% by an unverified web source — and every share of it that can be traced came out of the 2018 Omnibus Incentive Plan, where 14.98 million shares (9.1% of the company) sit issued or reserved at a $30.64 weighted-average option strike against a $171.16 market price. Not one open-market purchase by an insider appears in the pool or in the web record.

**The insider signal is net selling, but it is the ordinary kind and it cannot carry weight in scoring.** The visible pattern is cashless exercise-and-sell inside the post-results trading window the company's own policy defines, pre-cleared by the General Counsel, with no 10b5-1 plan adopted or terminated in any period the pool covers — and the May 2026 sales were followed by a Q2 that doubled EPS from continuing operations, so nothing here looks like selling ahead of bad news. Because that transaction record is web-sourced and not a pool filing, it fires no red flag and caps the recent-insider-behavior component to Insufficient Data (fix F20).

**The biggest risk to minority holders is not control abuse — it is that nobody is in control.** Pledging is contractually banned, hedging is banned, there is one share and one vote, no dual class, no bloc, no parent, and an Irish takeover regime that forbids the board from frustrating a bid. Against that: a combined Chair/CEO with no lead independent director disclosed anywhere in the pool, a board that may issue 20 million preferred shares — with voting rights of its own choosing — without asking shareholders, and insider ownership so small that no executive's own wealth is meaningfully tied to the share price except through the annual grant cycle. With the proxy absent, the pay design that would have to substitute for ownership alignment is unread in this run, and the honest verdict is that alignment here is **asserted by policy, not evidenced by stake**.

## management-governance / 05_board-and-shareholder-rights.md

_Source: `05_board-and-shareholder-rights.md`_

# Board & Shareholder Rights — NVT

**Jurisdiction:** Ireland-incorporated (Companies Act 2014), NYSE-listed US domestic filer (SEC file 001-38265, CIK 1720635). The proxy-equivalent is the **DEF 14A**; voting results are **8-K Item 5.07**; the constitutional document is the **Constitution / Articles of Association**, summarised in Exhibit 4.7 to the 10-K. Irish Takeover Rules apply on top of NYSE listing standards (CLAUDE.md §27).

**Evidence-scope note (read first).** The frozen data pool contains **no proxy statement** — the FY24 10-K incorporates Part III Items 10–14 by reference to a proxy that is not in the pool [FY24 10-K, Items 10–14]. Per this agent's partial-data rule, the board read would otherwise be "not assessable". It is assessable this run because the **primary proxy and both AGM voting 8-Ks were retrieved directly from SEC EDGAR**: `nVent DEF 14A filed 2026-03-31` (2026 AGM), `8-K Item 5.07 dated 2026-05-15`, and `8-K Item 5.07 dated 2025-05-16`. These are primary filings (CLAUDE.md §4 tier 4) read **outside the frozen pool** through a web-fetch layer, so every row built on them is labelled web-retrieved and carries **confidence 4, not 5**. Rows built on the pool's own 10-K/10-Q text carry confidence 5. Agent `07` independently read the same 2026 proxy; the two reads agree on the director roster, committee seats and the related-person-transaction statement, which is a real corroboration and is recorded as such. **The score cap that still binds is `04`'s, not mine:** no ownership or insider-transaction data exists in the pool, so the module-level *Shareholder friendliness max 60* cap stays live for `99` to apply. I do not apply the "no board disclosure" cap, and I state plainly why.

## 1. Board Composition

|---|---|---|
| Board size | **9 directors** from the close of the 2026 AGM (15 May 2026); 10 before it. Greg Scheu's term expired at that meeting and the board was deliberately reduced 10 → 9 | Web: nVent DEF 14A 2026-03-31, "Proposal 1 — Elect Director Nominees" (retrieved 2026-09-07) |
| Independent directors (%) — vs the applicable floor | **8 of 9 = 88.9% independent.** Only the CEO is non-independent. NYSE 303A.01 requires a majority; the applicable floor is therefore 50%, and the board runs at nearly nine-tenths. (The India ⅓ vs ½ chair test does not apply — this is a US/Irish filer. Its analogue does: where the chair is an executive, the tougher bar is ½, which is cleared by a wide margin) | Web: nVent DEF 14A 2026-03-31, "Corporate Governance Matters — Director Independence" |
| Chair / CEO split? Chair non-executive, non-promoter? Designated (not rotating)? | **NOT split. Beth A. Wozniak is both Chief Executive Officer (since 2018) and Chair of the Board (since 2023).** There is no promoter — nVent has been widely held since the 2018 Pentair spin-off. The counterweight is a **designated independent Lead Director, Susan M. Cameron**, with enumerated powers: presiding at executive sessions, calling meetings of the independent directors, approving board agendas with the Chair, reporting the CEO performance review, acting as shareholder liaison. The chair role is designated, not rotating | Web: nVent DEF 14A 2026-03-31, "Board Leadership Structure"; FY24 10-K, signature page ("Chief Executive Officer and Director") |

There is nothing here to mismatch: **the numerator is nil on both the flow and the stock basis**, so no peak-over-point-in-time hybrid can arise and no monitoring threshold built on a percentage is needed. The correct monitoring trigger is stated in currency, not in a ratio, below.

**Counterparty position — recorded and Not Applicable, not silently omitted.** nVent has **no related financial counterparty**: no group finance company, no captive NBFC, no affiliated treasury vehicle. Consequently the four facts this section would otherwise require — the company's own equity interest in such a counterparty, its regulatory supervision, the approved exposure cap and utilisation, and the independent-director / auditor review status — are **Not Applicable (no such entity exists)** rather than undisclosed. The vendor supply-chain graph is empty (`relationships.json`: 0 nodes, 0 edges, 0 relationship rows), so nothing contradicts the filings.

**The rights lens — who approved what.** nVent has a **written related-person-transaction policy** requiring disclosure and review by the **Governance and Sustainability Committee** of any transaction above **$50,000** involving a director, executive officer, or holder of more than 5% of the shares. That committee is **100% independent (Ducker chair; Burris, Cameron, Palmer)**, so the "only independent members vote" condition that India's LODR Reg 23(2)-(3) imposes is satisfied by construction rather than by exception. The proxy's own statement is unambiguous: **"We had no related person transactions during 2025. To our knowledge, no related person transactions are currently proposed."** Because none arose, no related-party resolution was put to shareholders, so there is **no majority-of-minority vote and no RPT dissent to read** — a true N/A, not a gap. Nothing in `07`'s registry-outward network sweep contradicts the statement: of 53 discovered subjects, **zero classify `disclosable-and-omitted`**.

**Disqualifier cross-reference.** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` tested each side on its own base: **related-party sales ÷ FY2024 revenue = 0% of $3,006.1m; related-party purchases ÷ total expenses = 0%**, against the >25% hard-disqualifier line. **Not tripped.** That scan's own caveat travels with the number and is repeated here: proxy-level person-transaction detail was unread *in the pool* — this run has now read it directly from EDGAR, and it says nil.

**Is economic value leaking to a controller?** There is no controller to leak to. All four material transactions of the last three years were **cash purchases from, or sales to, unrelated third parties**: ECM Industries ~$1.1bn (2023), Trachte ~$687.5m (2024), Avail Electrical Products Group ~$979.6m (closed 2025-05-01), Maverick Power $1.75bn plus up to $550m earn-out (announced 2026-08-24), and the Thermal Management divestiture to Brookfield-managed funds for $1.7bn (closed 2025-01-30). **The capital-allocation question these raise — $3,017m of acquisition spend FY2021–FY2025 against $2,091m of free cash flow, with a whole segment sold to help fund it — is real, and it belongs to `02` and to §24 Filter 4, not to this agent's leakage lens.** It is a spending-judgment risk, not a self-dealing one.

The 25,000 euro deferred shares (a €25,000 Irish plc minimum-capital formality) **carry no voting or dividend rights**. **But: 20,000,000 preferred shares are authorised and the Constitution entitles the board, without shareholder approval, to determine their terms — including voting.** None are stated issued. That is a live blank-cheque preferred authority | FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4.7, "Capital Structure" and "Voting" |
| Majority vs plurality director voting | **Majority — with a real fail rule** | *"The election of each director nominee … requires the affirmative vote of a majority of the votes cast,"* and *"A nominee who does not receive a majority of the votes cast in an uncontested election will not be elected to our Board."* Stronger than the plurality-plus-resignation-policy standard common in the US | Web: DEF 14A 2026-03-31, "Vote Required" |

Shareholder action by written consent is not disclosed as available; under Irish law it is not a practical minority mechanism | FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4.7, "Extraordinary General Meetings of Shareholders"; Web: DEF 14A 2026-03-31 |

The 10-K states plainly that this *"would be expected to have an anti-takeover effect … including discouraging attempts that might result in a premium over the market price."* A genuine board-side lever, disclosed candidly | FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4.7, "Interested Shareholder Provision" |

## 5. Minority-Shareholder Protection Read

The board is a real check, not a rubber stamp: 8 of 9 directors are independent, all three key committees are 100% independent with two designated financial experts, the independent directors met without management at **every** board and committee meeting in 2025, the 2025 evaluation was run by an outside third party with written assessments and one-to-one interviews, and there is no controller, no promoter, no dual-class share and **no related-person transaction at all in 2025** on the proxy's own statement — corroborated by the absence of any ASC 850 note in the audited financials and by `07`'s independent network sweep, which found zero `disclosable-and-omitted` subjects among 53. Rights are close to intact: one share one vote, annual election of every director on a majority standard that actually fails a loser, a 10% threshold to requisition a meeting, proxy access, no poison pill in force, and the Irish Takeover Rules' ban on frustrating action — which is a stronger real-world constraint on a defensive share issue than most US charters carry.

The two things that stop this being unqualified. First, **the CEO also chairs the board**, and the counterweight — a designated independent Lead Director with genuine enumerated powers — is a mitigation, not a substitute; the same person leads the body that reviews her succession, and no successor or emergency plan is disclosed. Second, the Constitution keeps three board-side levers alive that shareholders never voted for individually: **the power to adopt a poison pill without a shareholder vote, 20 million blank-cheque preferred shares whose terms (including voting) the board sets alone, and a Delaware-203-style 15% / three-year business-combination freeze** that the 10-K itself says would discourage a premium bid. None is in use; all are available. Add the softer items: the Lead Director carries a Minor-concerns grade from `07` on her Tupperware chairmanship through that company's restatement and Chapter 11; the audit-committee chair sits on four public boards and chairs a fifth company; and the company-secretary-equivalent seat has been without a publicly named permanent occupant since 2026-04-01.

**Conclusion: adequate — at the upper end of adequate, and short of strong protection only because of the combined Chair/CEO role and the dormant-but-unilateral board defenses.** `04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` runs in the same layer and its output does not exist as I write; on my own read there is **no structurally unaligned controlling owner** — nVent is widely held, not government-controlled, not a listed subsidiary of a value-maximising parent, and not a sprawling unrelated conglomerate (two segments in one industry) — so **RF-OWN-004 / §24 Filter 6 does not trip and the "no better than weak" floor does not apply**. If `04` finds a control bloc the filings do not show, that conclusion must be revisited. **The single biggest entrenchment risk to minority holders is not a current abuse but a standing capability: a board that can adopt a poison pill and set the terms of 20 million preferred shares on its own, chaired by the chief executive it is meant to supervise.**

## management-governance / 06_candor-and-disclosure-quality.md

_Source: `06_candor-and-disclosure-quality.md`_

# Candor & Disclosure Quality — NVT

**Jurisdiction & regime.** nVent Electric plc is incorporated in Ireland, head-officed in London, and files as a **US SEC domestic filer** on the NYSE (Commission file 001-38265), reporting under US GAAP in USD, fiscal year ending 31 December [FY24 10-K, cover page]. The US form names (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A) are therefore the correct local documents here (CLAUDE.md §27). Every pool document is in English; no translation issue arises, and **no language-based gap or opacity flag is recorded**.

**Evidence binding: frozen.** Every read resolved through extract generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6` (`manifest.json`, per-document extracts, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json`). Live `data/NVT/` was not read; `data/NVT/` below is a citation label only.

**Partial-data status — the important one, stated first.** The pool contains **two verbatim earnings-call transcripts** (Q1 FY26, 2026-05-01; Q2 FY26, 2026-07-31), so the module's "no transcripts" cap does **not** apply and tone and Q&A ARE assessable. But both of those quarters were blowouts: adjusted EPS beat the top of the guided range by 17.2% and 26.1% [earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md §6]. **The one clear miss in the record — Q3 FY2024, adjusted-EPS surprise −22.2% — has no transcript in this pool**, and there is no shareholder letter, no proxy (DEF 14A), no FY2025 10-K and no 8-Ks [management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md, header]. So the strongest form of the test this agent exists to run — *how do they talk when the print is genuinely bad?* — cannot be run on the genuinely bad print. It is run instead on the mildest available bad news (two segment-margin declines and one down organic year in the FY24 10-K MD&A), and that limitation is carried into the score, the confidence and the verdict rather than smoothed away.

**Cross-module inputs used.** `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` (available — non-GAAP and accrual cross-check performed), `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md` (available), `management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md` (available — the promise-vs-delivery record), `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md` (available — no integrity signal routed).

---

## 1. Owning the Misses

| Miss (from 01) | How It Was Communicated | Owned or Obscured? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Electrical Connections return on sales (operating profit as a share of sales) fell 390 basis points year on year to 24.4%, Q1 FY26** | Named in prepared remarks, in the CFO's own segment walk, with the number: "Return on sales of 24.4% was down 390 basis points year-over-year. The margin performance was impacted by higher than expected raw material inflation." Cause was then specified under questioning as "higher than expected inflation, primarily due to copper," with the actions taken (pricing, productivity) and a forward commitment ("we expect margins to improve in Q2 and for the balance of the year") | **Owned.** The decline was stated before the mitigation, with the size, the driver and a testable forward promise. Not buried in a footnote and not routed around by talking only about the company-level 20% ROS | Q1 FY26 transcript, 2026-05-01, prepared remarks and Q&A (Joe Ritchie exchange) |
| **The follow-through: Electrical Connections ROS still down 140 bps year on year in Q2 FY26 (27.3%)** | Again stated with the number first: "Return on sales of 27.3% was down 140 basis points year-over-year. The margin performance was impacted by inflation and mix, partially offset by improving price and volume. Importantly, margins improved sequentially back into the high 20s" | **Owned, with a framing tilt.** The year-on-year decline is disclosed first and accurately; the word "importantly" then steers the reader to the sequential recovery. That is emphasis, not concealment — both numbers are given | Q2 FY26 transcript, 2026-07-31, prepared remarks; corroborated in Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 13 (segment income $108.8m on sales $399.2m = 27.25%) |
| **FY2024 organic sales decline in Electrical & Fastening Solutions, −1.5%** — the year in which consolidated organic growth (+2.4%) fell below the then-standing +3.5–6.5% target band | Disclosed in the MD&A with a full decomposition rather than a summary: volume −1.7%, price +0.2%, organic −1.5%, acquisition +12.8%, currency 0.0%, total +11.3%. The segment margin decline (−1.1 pts to 30.0%) is shown in the same table, and the text names the offset explicitly — the reported increase "was primarily the result of sales of $136.3 million in 2024 as a result of the ECM Industries acquisition… partially offset by organic sales decline of approximately 1.5%" | **Owned.** This is the cleanest candor evidence in the pool: the filing separates bought growth from earned growth, in the year the earned growth was negative, and does not let the +11.3% headline stand alone | FY24 10-K, Item 7 MD&A — Electrical & Fastening Solutions, components of change in net sales |
| **The one large miss: Q3 FY2024 adjusted-EPS surprise −22.2%** (the only miss in the eight-quarter surprise history; FY2024 GAAP-EPS surprise −8%) | **Not assessable.** No Q3 FY2024 transcript, no FY2025 10-K, no 8-K and no shareholder letter covering that period exists in this pool | **Insufficient Data.** The single most informative candor test in the record cannot be performed. Recorded, not guessed | `CIQ Estimates→Surprise` via earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md §6; management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md §4 |
| **Free-cash-flow conversion: the one mid-term target cut** (~100% → ~95% at the March 2026 Investor Day, while organic growth, inorganic growth, adjusted operating margin and adjusted EPS growth were all raised) | Disclosed on the face of the target slide, labelled "−5 pts From previous target" — i.e. the cut is visible and quantified. But **no reason for the cut appears anywhere in the pool**: neither the William Blair deck nor either 2026 call explains why the cash target went down while four others went up, and no analyst asked | **Disclosed but unexplained.** Not hidden — labelled in the company's own deck — but the one bar that was lowered is also the one with no stated rationale. Amber | 2026 William Blair deck, 2026-06-03, slide 18; Q1 and Q2 FY26 transcripts (no mention) |
| **Backlog ticked down sequentially in Q2 FY26 (~$2.5bn)** — raised by two analysts | Answered directly and without deflection: "we had a strong quarter because we were executing on some of that backlog… we want to work it down… we're probably around the right level that we think we should be," plus the CFO's unprompted qualifier that "the backlog is mostly 12 months or less, and that hasn't extended out" | **Owned.** The soft datapoint was accepted rather than reframed, and the CFO volunteered a duration fact that cuts against the bullish reading | Q2 FY26 transcript, 2026-07-31, Q&A (Joe Ritchie; Nicole DeBlase; Vlad Bystricky) |

**Read across the row.** On every miss that *is* observable, management leads with the number and the direction, then the cause, then the fix. Nothing in this table shows a miss being routed around, renamed, or dissolved into an adjusted figure. The limitation is not what they did with the misses on show — it is that the misses on show are small.

## 2. Non-GAAP / Adjustment Aggressiveness

*Cross-checked against `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` (Earnings Quality Score 74/100). The figures below are that agent's; this agent applies the candor lens rather than recomputing them.*

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Recurring "one-off" addbacks** | **Four adjustment categories recur in every year on record**, which by definition makes them not one-off: intangible amortisation from acquisitions (50.3 / 69.5 / 94.7 / 147.1 in FY2022–FY2025; $165.2m LTM; $82.2m in H1 FY26 alone); acquisition transaction and integration costs (0.8 / 12.8 / 13.9 / 14.4; 7.5 in H1 FY26); restructuring and other (11.2 / 3.9 / 7.5 / 7.5; 10.9 in H1 FY26); and a pension/OPEB mark-to-market remeasurement the company performs **by policy every Q4** (+61.9 / −13.4 / +0.1 / +12.9). USD millions | earnings/06_earnings-quality.md §4 and §5, drawn from FY24 10-K Note 5 and the company's own reconciliations; Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 13 |
| **GAAP-to-adjusted gap (magnitude / trend)** | **FY2025: adjusted diluted EPS $3.35 vs GAAP continuing-operations EPS $2.60 — a gap of +28.8%.** At the operating line, +$169.0m of add-backs on $616.8m of GAAP operating income = **+27.4%**, and **87% of that ($147.1m) is acquisition intangible amortisation**. **H1 FY26: the gap narrows to +17.1%** ($2.54 adjusted vs $2.17 GAAP), but for a mechanical reason as much as a virtuous one — the amortisation add-back kept *growing* in dollars ($82.2m vs $64.1m in H1 FY25) while reported earnings grew faster still, so the same-sized adjustment is a smaller percentage | earnings/06_earnings-quality.md §7 |
| **Does the adjusted framing flatter reality?** | **Partly yes, and partly the opposite — both, and the second is unusual enough to state plainly.** *Flattering:* the headline adjusted number systematically excludes the amortisation cost of the acquisitions that are driving the growth — $2.77bn of deals in three years (ECM $1,120.1m, Trachte $677.7m, EPG $975.7m), with a fourth agreed (Maverick, $1.75bn + up to $550m). That cost keeps running for 8–20 years after each deal while the "organic-plus-acquired" growth stops being flattered. *Conservative, against interest:* **stock-based compensation is NOT adjusted out** — $37.5m (FY2025) and $23.1m (H1 FY26) stays inside adjusted earnings, which is a tighter definition than most US industrials use; and in Q2 FY26 the company **removed a $25.8m GAAP benefit** (IEEPA tariff reimbursements) from its own adjusted numbers, so H1 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $605.4m sits **below** GAAP-derived EBITDA of $612.8m. A company willing to publish an adjusted figure lower than its GAAP figure is not running the add-backs in one direction only | earnings/06_earnings-quality.md §4, §7, §10; Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 13 and Item 2 MD&A (Gross profit) |
| **One completeness gap on the IEEPA item** | The $25.8m reimbursement (≈ $0.12 of GAAP diluted EPS, ~9% of the quarter's $1.32) is disclosed in the 10-Q — in the segment note's definition, in the reconciliation table, and in the MD&A, which adds that it "was offset by other incremental tariffs compared to the prior year periods." It is **not mentioned once on the Q2 earnings call**, in prepared remarks or Q&A. Because it was excluded from adjusted, the omission does not flatter the headline adjusted EPS that management guides on; it does mean a listener working only from the call would not know a $25.8m item sat inside reported gross profit | Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 13, Item 2 MD&A; Q2 FY26 transcript, 2026-07-31 (absence) |

**Verdict on adjustments: aggressive in structure, conservative in conduct — and the structural problem is real enough to flag.** The recurring-adjustment test is failed on the facts: four categories labelled as excluded items appear in every single year, and adjusted EPS runs 29% above audited GAAP EPS. That triggers **RF-DISC-002**. What holds this short of a candor indictment is that every adjustment is disclosed line by line, reconciles exactly (496.4 + 82.2 + 10.9 + 7.5 − 25.8 = 571.2, tying to segment income of 644.9 less Enterprise and other of 73.7), SBC is left in, and the company removed a benefit rather than an expense. This is standard US-industrial non-GAAP practice with two above-average marks and one below-average one — not a company hiding a deteriorating business behind add-backs.

---

## 3. Disclosure Transparency

**Segment economics: disclosed, and the granularity has gone UP, not down.** From Q1 FY26 the 10-Q discloses, per segment and with restated prior-year comparatives, not just net sales and segment income but the significant expense categories beneath them — cost of goods sold, SG&A, and R&D (Q2 FY26 Systems Protection: sales $1,072.1m, COGS $707.5m, SG&A $99.8m, R&D $16.6m, segment income $248.2m; Electrical Connections: $399.2m / $227.1m / $57.3m / $6.0m / $108.8m) [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 13]. That lets an outsider compute a segment gross margin the company never quotes — and, as §4 below shows, the answer is less flattering than the commentary. A company that hands you the numbers to check it with is not obscuring. Revenue is additionally disaggregated by segment × vertical and by segment × geography, and backlog is disclosed with a stated definition ("all orders from external customers, which represent firm commitments, and are supported by a purchase order or other legitimate contract"; $749.3m at 2024-12-31) [FY24 10-K, Item 1 — Backlog of Orders by Segment; Item 1A].

**Two things did get less granular, and neither follows the deterioration pattern the rule exists to catch.** (a) Reportable segments went from three to two — because Thermal Management was sold on 2025-01-30, which is a disposal, not a reporting choice. (b) The revenue-by-vertical disaggregation went from four categories to three in Q1 FY26: the **Energy** vertical was folded away. Test it properly — Energy was **rising**, not deteriorating: $60.5m (FY2022) → $69.8m (FY2023) → $81.7m (FY2024), and it was 2.7% of FY2024 sales; the company stated the reason ("based on benchmarking of industry peers and for purposes of how we assess performance") and **restated the prior-year comparatives** so the series stays comparable, noting the change "had no impact on our consolidated financial results" [FY24 10-K, Note — Vertical net sales; Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 2]. A category dropped while growing, with comparatives restated, is the opposite of RF-MGT-003.

**The one genuine transparency gap is a KPI that only exists outside the filings.** "New Product Vitality" — quoted as **27% of sales, "up +7pp from last Investor Day"** [2026 William Blair deck, slide 6] — and its call-level companion, "new products contributed over 30 points to our sales growth" in Q2 (">20 points" in Q1) [Q2 FY26 transcript, prepared remarks; Q1 FY26 investor deck, Highlights], carry **no disclosed definition anywhere in the pool**: no stated window for what counts as "new," no reconciliation to any filed line, and no appearance in the 10-K or either 10-Q. That metric is used to attribute the majority of a 53%-growth quarter, and a reader cannot audit it. Separately and more mildly, nVent **names no competitor anywhere in its own filings** — the competition section is entirely generic [FY24 10-K, Item 1 — Competition; business-model/08_competitive-map.md, header], and management declined to break the $2bn data-centre revenue between liquid cooling and the rest ("certainly, we haven't broken that down yet") [Q2 FY26 transcript, Q&A — Jeff Hammond]. Neither is unusual for a US industrial; both are places where the reader is asked to take a number on trust.

---

## 4. Tone in Bad Times

**The honest headline: the worst period in this pool is not a bad period.** Both available transcripts cover quarters with 47–53% sales growth and record earnings, so the tone read is necessarily made on a bull-market sample. Within that sample, the tone is specific rather than promotional — inflation offsets are quantified to the dollar ("price plus productivity offset inflation of nearly $60 million, including approximately $40 million in tariff impact" in Q1; "more than $50 million… more than $30 million in tariff impact" in Q2), the all-in tariff burden was given on the spot when asked ("incremental is $80 million this year followed from $90 last year. So, $170 million all-in… the US tariff environment remains highly fluid"), and the raised tariff cost ($80m → $100m) was announced with its reason ("largely, this is driven by our significantly higher volume growth") rather than slipped in. The plainest tell is the refusal to speculate favourably: asked whether tariff relief might be coming, the CEO said only "We've kept to our current outlook, and I guess we'll wait and see."

**Q&A was mostly answered directly, with one exception that an analyst named on the record.** On the Q1 call Jeff Sprague of Vertical Research put it explicitly — "I think, somebody tap-danced around this a little bit. Right? But you clearly would have had factory inefficiencies in the quarter. You also would have had more inflation than you expected" — and the CFO's reply addressed neither factory inefficiencies nor the unexpected inflation, opening instead with "we were very pleased with the margin expansion that we saw in the quarter from Systems Protection." That is a deflection, and it is worth more than its size because it is the only hard question in the pool. A softer version appeared in Q2, when Jeff Sprague asked why the guide implies **sequentially declining** revenue in Q3 and more so in Q4: the CFO answered by switching metrics to the two-year stack ("we're going to significantly accelerate 50% in Q3 at the midpoint versus 46% growth in the first half") without addressing the sequential decline — though the CEO then answered it squarely ("this is just our planning, and we're being very prudent… as we ramp 2 new facilities").

**One place where the commentary is more flattering than the company's own segment data, and it should be named rather than averaged away (CLAUDE.md §3).** Management attributed Systems Protection's Q2 ROS gain to "strong volume and productivity" — "Return on sales of 23.2% increased 150 basis points year-over-year on strong volume and productivity" [Q2 FY26 transcript, prepared remarks]. Do the arithmetic from the segment note the company itself now publishes: Systems Protection **gross margin FELL 246 bps**, from 36.47% (230.5 ÷ 632.0) to 34.01% (364.6 ÷ 1,072.1). The ROS gain came entirely from operating leverage on fixed costs below the gross line — SG&A fell 363 bps as a share of sales (12.94% → 9.31%) and R&D 29 bps (1.84% → 1.55%). The build reconciles exactly: −246 + 363 + 29 = **+146 bps**, which is the "150 basis points" quoted [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 13 — derived]. The 10-Q's own MD&A *does* disclose the gross-margin drivers honestly (inflation, unfavourable product mix, capacity investment, partly offset by volume leverage and productivity), so the filing is candid and the call statement is not false — "productivity" is a genuine named offset. But a listener told the margin rose on "volume and productivity" would not know the gross line went backwards by 246 bps. **That is selective emphasis, not a contradiction: RF-DISC-001 is tested and does NOT trigger.**

---

## 5. Candor Read

**Conclusion: mixed, leaning candid — with the decisive test unrun.** On everything that can be checked, this management tells the truth in a checkable way: it puts the bad number before the mitigation (Electrical Connections ROS −390 bps, then the copper explanation, then a dated forward promise it went on to keep sequentially); it separates bought growth from earned growth in the one year earned growth was negative (FY2024 EFS: volume −1.7%, price +0.2%, organic −1.5%, acquisition +12.8%); it raised guidance three times while restating the prior range each time and disclosing the tariff cost going up with it; it leaves stock-based compensation inside adjusted earnings; and in Q2 FY26 it removed a $25.8m GAAP *benefit* from its own adjusted numbers, publishing adjusted EBITDA below GAAP EBITDA. It also now publishes segment cost lines detailed enough for an outsider to catch it framing a margin gain generously — which is what §4 above did.

The strongest evidence the other way is threefold and none of it is trivial: **four "one-off" adjustment categories recur in every single year on record**, holding adjusted EPS 28.8% above audited GAAP EPS in FY2025 with 87% of the gap being the amortisation cost of the acquisition engine itself; a headline growth-attribution KPI ("New Product Vitality," 27%; "new products contributed over 30 points to our sales growth") exists only in decks and calls with **no definition and no reconciliation to any filed number**; and the only genuinely hard analyst question in the pool drew a non-answer that the analyst himself labelled "tap-danced around."

**The single biggest candor signal is the one I could not test.** Both verbatim transcripts in this pool cover quarters that beat the top of guidance by 17.2% and 26.1%; the one real miss in the eight-quarter record — Q3 FY2024, −22.2% on adjusted EPS — has no transcript, no letter and no 8-K here. Candor is measured in bad times, and this company's bad time is missing from the evidence. No adverse integrity signal was routed from `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` (it states explicitly that none was found), so nothing compounds against the trust read under CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 1 — but nothing resolves the untested half of it either. Treat the candid read as **provisional and cycle-conditioned**, and re-test it on the first quarter this company misses.

**Red-flag tags emitted by this agent (standalone, per CLAUDE.md §13):**

RF-DISC-002 (recurring "one-off" / aggressive non-GAAP add-backs)

*Not triggered, tested and recorded:* RF-DISC-001 (commentary contradicting the numbers) — tested at §4 against the Systems Protection segment build; selective emphasis found, contradiction not found. RF-REG-002 (delayed results / material-disclosure timeliness) — no delay evidence in this pool; both FY26 10-Qs were filed the same day as their earnings calls and the FY24 10-K carries a 2025-02-18 audit report. **A7-01 timeliness is owned by `12_regulatory-legal-and-compliance`, not by this agent** — this is a reference, not an adjudication. Restatements (A7-02) are owned by `08_audit-and-assurance-quality`; this agent notes only that the FY26 vertical recategorisation states it "had no impact on our consolidated financial results" and is therefore not a restatement.

# People & Network Integrity Dossiers — NVT

**Run type:** full sweep, 2026-09-07. No prior-dated `07_people-integrity-dossiers.md` exists for this ticker (checked `analyses/NVT_*/management-governance/`), so this is a first run, not a delta-refresh.

**Coverage headline.** The external sweep RAN. Corporate registries (UK Companies House overseas-company register, Irish CRO number via the same record), SEC EDGAR (filings, DEF 14A, 8-K), the SEC Action Lookup for Individuals (SALI), OpenSanctions' consolidated sanctions/PEP screen, the company's own investor-relations governance pages, USPTO/proprietor brand evidence, and dated adverse-media queries were all reachable and were used. Two sources refused automated fetches — `www.nvent.com/en-us/*` (HTTP 403) and the Irish CRO mirror `vision-net.ie` (marketing page only, no record) — and the workarounds used are recorded in the Sweep Log. Nothing here is a filings-only profile presented as a clearance.

**Jurisdiction.** US/SEC domestic filer (Form 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K / DEF 14A / Form 4 / 11-K), Commission file 001-38265, listed NYSE: NVT. Issuer incorporated in **Ireland** (CRO number **605257**), UK-tax-resident, principal executive offices in London, US management office in Minneapolis. India/SEBI instruments (DIN, MCA, SEBI orders, wilful-defaulter lists, shareholding-pattern pledge columns) are **genuinely Not Applicable** to this regime and are recorded as such, never as missing data. All documents are in English; no translation was required and no language-based gap is recorded (CLAUDE.md §27).

### 0.4 The loop, in one line each — this block IS checklist item A17-01

- **Phase 1 recipes that ran:** D-1 (company self-disclosure fetch — run, PARTIAL: `www.nvent.com/en-us/about-us` returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so the self-disclosed history was taken from the company's own `investors.nvent.com` governance pages, its own nVent HOFFMAN 75th-anniversary heritage page, its own March-2025 leadership press release, and the "History and Development" narrative in its own 10-K); D-2 (founding-year vs incorporation test); D-3 (registry previous-names field — **this produced a hit**); D-4 (brand/trademark proprietor); D-5 (registered-address cluster); D-8 (past/resigned directorships); D-9 (co-director network).
- **Phase 2 (the founder loop) RAN**, on 25 hop-1 entities. Founders identified distinct from current boards where they exist: Tom Currier (Maverick Power, founded 2020); Harry Hoffman (Hoffman Enclosures, founded October 1945, the origin of the HOFFMAN brand nVent still trades under); Pentair plc as nVent's own past controller. Pentair's own 1966 founders were not verified within budget and are recorded as Insufficient Data on Scope-Boundary row S2, not asserted.
- **Hop reached:** 2.
- **Termination rule:** `breadth_budget`. The hop-1 candidate set is ~56 entities; the protocol admits 25 to a full Phase-2 sweep. Every candidate got the scoped pass (registry status + Adverse-Keyword Battery) **before** the selection, so the priority-2 ordering key ("carries an adverse hit from its scoped pass") was actually computable. The 31 named overflow entities and the Exhibit 21 block are on the Scope-Boundary Register in Section 5 with reason `breadth_budget`, and the declared-overflow score cap is applied.
- **Forcing rule satisfied:** every subject above carries an enumerated discovery method. No free text. No subject left scope without a Scope-Boundary row.

**A17-02 read.** The founding-year gap (claims of 1988 and "over 100 years" against a 2017-05-30 incorporation) is the classic D-2 lead, and it **reconciles cleanly**. The company names the parent it inherited the history from (Pentair), names the two acquisitions that carried the brands (Federal-Hoffman 1988, ERICO 2015), dates the separation, and repeats all of it in its audited annual filing. A truthfully-cited group history is expressly the Green case, not the red one. The one genuinely undisclosed item — the 4-day-old former name "nVent Electric Limited" — is a formation-stage private-to-plc re-registration of the same legal entity, and is classified `not-disclosable` under the A17-08 test in Section 4. **No RF-NET-001.**

## 3B. Lineage & Phoenix Read (A17-02, A17-03)

**Does a predecessor exist?** Yes, and the company names it itself. nVent Electric plc was incorporated in Ireland on 2017-05-30 as the vehicle for **Pentair plc's** separation of its Electrical business, completed 2018-04-30 by distributing one nVent share for every Pentair share (record date 2018-04-17); nVent began trading on 2018-05-01. Behind Pentair sit two brand-lineage entities the company also names: **Federal-Hoffman Corporation** (Pentair's 1988 acquisition, source of the HOFFMAN brand, itself founded by Harry Hoffman in October 1945) and **ERICO Global Company** (Pentair's 2015 acquisition, now nVent's Electrical Connections business). The registry adds one thing the filings do not: the company carried the name **"nVent Electric Limited" from 2017-10-12 to 2017-11-03**, a 22-day private-to-plc re-registration during formation.

**Did the predecessor fail?** **No.** Pentair plc is solvent and still listed. Federal-Hoffman was acquired as a going concern by a listed buyer in 1988. ERICO was acquired as a going concern in 2015 and is now a consolidated nVent subsidiary. No insolvency, liquidation, strike-off or resolution process was found on any of the three.

**Did assets, brands, staff, address, products or customers continue into the current entity?** Yes — the entire Electrical business of Pentair did, brands included. **On what disclosed legal basis and for what consideration?** A **pro-rata spin-off to Pentair's own shareholders** under a separation and distribution, disclosed in nVent's Form 10-12B registration statement, its 8-Ks of April–May 2018, and repeated in every annual report since. That is the textbook clean case: continuity through a formal, disclosed process, with the "consideration" being shares delivered to the predecessor's own shareholders rather than assets moved to an insider at a discount. **No related party re-bought failed assets. No RF-NET-002.**

**Are the marks still shared with a live unrelated user?** No. The nVent, CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE marks are owned or licensed by **nVent Services GmbH**, a wholly-owned Swiss subsidiary on nVent's own Exhibit 21. The RAYCHEM and Thermal marks left the group with the Thermal Management divestiture on 2025-01-30 — a disclosed sale, not a shared-brand ambiguity. The D-4 corroboration test therefore never engages, because there is no live unrelated proprietor to corroborate.

**The one live lineage fact the synthesis must carry:** the predecessor is clean on lineage but **not clean on its current record** — Pentair plc is a defendant in 2026 securities-fraud class actions covering 2025–26 conduct in its Pool segment. That is set out at 2B.3 with the RF-NET-003 test written out, and it is handed to `12` labelled `predecessor_entity`.

## 6. Provenance & Next Data Request

- **Provenance, in one sentence:** of **53** subjects on the Discovery Register, **44 were filing-supplied** (disclosed by nVent in its 10-K, 10-Qs, Exhibit 21, proxy, 8-Ks or press releases), **9 were independently discovered** by this loop (the 22-day former name, the Dublin registered-office cluster, Varsity Brands, Fernweh Group, AZZ Inc., Bain Capital, KKR, Harry Hoffman, and the unverified Pentair founder candidate Murray J. Harpole), and **none was user-supplied** — and of all 53, **zero classify `disclosable-and-omitted`**. A further **31 named hop-1 entities** received the scoped pass only and are listed on the Scope-Boundary Register at row S6.
- **Beneficial-interest scope exclusions, named:** the nine non-employee directors — **Sherry A. Aaholm, Jerry W. Burris, Susan M. Cameron, Michael L. Ducker, Diane Leopold, Danita K. Ostling, Nicola Palmer, Herbert K. Parker** and outgoing director **Greg Scheu** — are excluded from beneficial-interest scope because they are independent non-executive directors with no control stake; nVent's own board affirms all nine non-employee directors are independent with no material relationship. **They were still swept for integrity at Tier C** (three escalated to a full sweep). This line is about beneficial interest only. No nominee directorships exist to exclude.
- **Aggregator conflict kept in scope and flagged (A17-10):** one, named. nVent's investor-relations board page renders Herbert K. Parker's fourth directorship as "**Dauch Corporation**" while the 2026 proxy names "**American Axle & Manufacturing**". Both names were kept in scope and swept; the conflict is resolved on the proxy as the primary document, and **no name was dropped**. A second, benign variance: the same IR page gives Wozniak's age as 60 and the proxy as 61, consistent with a birthday between the two publication dates — recorded, not treated as an identity conflict.
- **The single highest-value next data request:** **the SEC Form 4 filings and Schedule 13D/13G ownership filings for nVent Electric plc.** They are the one input that would let this agent test the two axes it currently cannot — whether any insider sold ahead of an adverse disclosure (A16-20's market-conduct edge, and RF-MKT-001), and whether any 5%-plus holder sits behind a structure the proxy's "no related person transactions" statement does not reach. One EDGAR pull settles both, and it does so for `04` at the same time.

## 7. People & Network Integrity Read

Twenty-one people were swept and twenty grade **Clean**; the twenty-first, Lead Director **Susan M. Cameron**, grades **Minor concerns** because she was non-executive chairman of Tupperware Brands through its 2023 restatement, its disclosed control weaknesses, its going-concern warning and its September-2024 Chapter 11 — a disclosed association on her record, not an allegation against her, and not a live linkage, since both the directorship and the company have ended. On the entity side, twenty-six were swept and the riskiest is **Pentair plc**, nVent's own former parent, which is now a defendant in 2026 securities-fraud class actions over 2025–26 conduct in a Pool business nVent never owned: the RF-NET-003 trigger was tested against it and deliberately **not** fired, because what survives between the two companies is a legacy equity-plan link and an eight-year-old indenture rather than any live control or trading relationship — the counter-reading, and the cap it would carry, are set out in 2B.3 so `99` can decide on facts rather than on a label. The discovery loop ran both phases, reached **hop 2**, and stopped on **`breadth_budget`** with 31 named hop-1 entities and the residual subsidiary block left at scoped depth; the loop's own best catch — a 22-day formation-stage former name and a law-firm registered-office cluster — turned out to be entirely benign, which is a real answer rather than a null one. No §24 Filter 1 signal is open: `01_disqualifier-scan` routed no integrity buzz, and none surfaced here.

What a rational minority holder should conclude: **the people running nVent are, on every public record this engine can reach, clean — no criminal matter, no regulator order, no sanctions match, no disqualification, no undisclosed directorship, no undisclosed related entity, and no related-party transaction reported for 2025** — and the network around them is unusually tidy for an acquisitive industrial: the marks sit inside the group, the lineage is a solvent 2018 spin-off the company describes accurately in its own filings, and every entity that trades with the company is disclosed by it. The two things worth watching are not integrity failures but **bench and continuity**: the company-secretary-equivalent seat falls vacant on 2026-04-01 with no named successor as of the last proxy, the chief accounting officer announced a retirement and reversed it inside ten weeks, and the CFO is fifteen months into the job — a gatekeeper bench in motion, all of it disclosed, none of it adverse, and all of it better read by `05` and `08` than scored here.

# Audit & Assurance Quality — NVT

**Regime (from `00_governance-data-triage`, §5A).** nVent Electric plc is a **US SEC domestic filer** (Form 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K / DEF 14A / 11-K), incorporated in Ireland, tax-resident in the UK, listed on the NYSE, reporting under **US GAAP** in **USD**, fiscal year ending **31 December**. Two consequences run through every row below:

1. **There is no standalone-vs-consolidated split.** A US filer publishes ONE set of consolidated financial statements with ONE auditor's opinion. The "clean standalone / modified consolidated" divergence test has nothing to compare against here — it is answered as Not Applicable (regime), not skipped.
2. **CARO, the MR-3 secretarial audit report, and the SEBI Oct-2019 auditor-exit circular are India-only instruments.** They are genuinely Not Applicable, never "missing data" (CLAUDE.md §27). The local analogues that DO exist — the SOX §404(b) internal-control attestation, Item 9 "Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants", the Item 4.01 auditor-change 8-K, and the cover-page error-correction checkboxes — are read in their place and reported below.

**Evidence binding.** All pool reads went through the frozen extract generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6` (`manifest.json`, `corpus.txt`, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json`). Live `data/NVT/` was not read; `data/NVT/` is a citation label only. Four facts the pool could not answer were retrieved directly from SEC EDGAR and from the audit regulators' own sites and are labelled as such, with dates, in the Sweep Log and Source Log.

**Plainly stated.** Every audit opinion a reader can actually see — FY2022, FY2023, FY2024 on the financial statements, plus FY2024 on internal control — is clean. There is no qualification, no adverse opinion, no disclaimer, no emphasis-of-matter paragraph, and no going-concern language anywhere in the pool. **What a reader cannot see is FY2025**, and that is the honest limit on this section: the most recent audited year, the year in which revenue rose about 29.5% (FY2024A $3,006.1m → FY2025A $3,893.1m, *Capital IQ Income Statement tab — tier-5 vendor, unaudited in this pool*) and a ~$979.6m business was folded in, has no readable auditor's report.

**Restatements (A7-02).** No restatement in five years. The strongest single piece of evidence is not narrative but a regulatory attestation: **both** FY24 10-K cover-page checkboxes — error correction, and restatement requiring a 10D-1 clawback recovery analysis — are unticked. Carry this qualifier with the finding (§3): the Capital IQ Cash Flow and Income Statement tabs label the FY2021 and FY2022 columns **"Restated"**, and that is a **vendor label for the recast of prior periods into discontinued operations** after the Thermal Management sale (agreement 2024-07-31, closed 2025-01-30) — **not** an error correction. `01_disqualifier-scan` named this trap first; it travels intact.

**Clawback.** A recovery policy exists — **"nVent Electric plc Recovery Policy"**, filed as Exhibit 97 and incorporated by reference into the FY24 10-K exhibit index, with matching recoupment clauses in the option, RSU and PSU award agreements referencing Dodd-Frank and its implementing regulations. Because no restatement occurred, no recovery was owed and none was pursued. (`03` owns the policy's design under A6-06; this row only records that it exists and was not needed.)

**Rotation, outgoing and incoming firms named.** There has been **no rotation to name**: Deloitte & Touche LLP in, 2017; Deloitte & Touche LLP still in, 2026. No Item 4.01 auditor-change 8-K exists in nVent's EDGAR 8-K history (checked 2026-09-07). The only firm swap anywhere in the group is Deloitte → **Crowe LLP** at the employee benefit plan, and the outgoing and incoming firms there are **different networks** (Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu → Crowe Global) — the opposite of a same-network affiliate dodge, and at a plan, not the issuer.
