## 4. Economic Independence — Fees (A4-06, A4-07)

| FY | Audit fee | Non-audit fee (incl. network firms) | Non-audit / audit (%) | Prohibited services? | Fee vs peer median | Revenue growth | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2024 | **Not disclosed in pool** | Not disclosed in pool | Not computable | Not testable | Not computable | +12.6% (FY2023 $2,668.9m → FY2024 $3,006.1m, audited) | **Not Applicable (no data)** | FY24 10-K, Item 14 — fees incorporated by reference to the absent 2025 proxy |
| FY2025 | **Not disclosed in pool** | Not disclosed in pool | Not computable | Not testable | Not computable | **+29.5%** (FY2024A $3,006.1m → FY2025A $3,893.1m; CIQ Income Statement tab, tier-5 vendor, unaudited in pool) | **Not Applicable (no data)** | FY2025 10-K absent; FY2026 DEF 14A fee table not extractable (see below) |

**Why this is Not Applicable rather than Red or Green.** The FY24 10-K's Item 14 does not print a single fee figure — it names Deloitte & Touche LLP (PCAOB ID 34) as principal accountant and incorporates the fees by reference to *"Proposal 4 Ratify, by Non-Binding Advisory Vote, the Appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as the Independent Auditor of nVent Electric plc and to Authorize, by Binding Vote, the Audit and Finance Committee of the Board of Directors to Set the Auditor's Remuneration"* in a proxy statement that is not in the pool. Per the partial-data rule, **A4-06 and A4-07 are Not Applicable (no data)**, and the score cap (Audit & assurance quality max 65; Confidence max 80) applies.

**What was checked, so the gap is sized honestly.** Direct retrieval from SEC EDGAR on 2026-09-07 confirms that the disclosure **exists and is public**: the FY2026 DEF 14A (filed 2026-03-31) carries "Fees Paid to Independent Auditors" and an "Audit and Finance Committee Pre-approval Policy" at page 61, and the FY2025 DEF 14A (filed 2025-04-01) carries the same at page 62. Three retrieval attempts on the 2.6MB proxy documents truncated before reaching those pages, so **the fee numbers themselves were not read**. That distinction matters: this is a **pool-collection and retrieval gap, not company opacity** — nVent discloses its auditor fees in the ordinary place a US filer discloses them.

**Two things that ARE established about independence, and one that is not:**
- **Pre-approval structure exists.** The Audit and Finance Committee operates a documented pre-approval policy for auditor services [FY2026 DEF 14A, p.61].
- **Fee-setting authority sits with the committee under shareholder authority**, not with management — the Irish-law binding vote each year authorises the committee to set the auditor's remuneration, and it passed with 0.48% against in 2026. This is structurally stronger than the US norm, where the committee's authority derives from its charter alone.
- **Not established:** the ratio itself, and whether any service prohibited by **SOX §201** (bookkeeping, financial-information-systems design, **appraisal / valuation and fairness opinions**, actuarial, internal-audit outsourcing, management or HR functions, broker-dealer/investment-banking, legal, and unrelated expert services) was rendered. *The regime named here is SOX §201 — not India's Companies Act Sec 144, which does not apply to this filer. Note that valuation work IS a §201 prohibition even though it is not a Sec 144 item; that is directly relevant because the FY2024 Critical Audit Matter is a valuation, on which Deloitte used its **own** fair-value specialists in an audit capacity — the permitted side of the line, not a prohibited service.*

**The untested test that would have mattered most.** A4-07's low-balling trigger — a fee that FALLS while revenue grows more than 20% — is live in exactly this window: revenue rose about **29.5%** in FY2025 while the group bought EPG (~$979.6m) and sold Thermal Management ($1.7bn), a scope change on both sides at once. Whether the audit fee moved with that scope is unknowable from this pool, and no peer-median benchmark can be applied to a fee nobody can see. **Follow-up:** obtain the DEF 14A fee tables for FY2023–FY2025 and test the ratio and the trend against the scope change.

**A4-04 verdict: Green.** No auditor resignation, mid-term or otherwise, in the last three-to-five years. Item 9 of the FY24 10-K reads "None." on changes and disagreements with accountants; no Item 4.01 8-K exists; and the appointment is re-ratified by shareholders each year with negligible dissent. There is no qualification for an auditor to have fled from, because there has been no qualification.

**A4-15 verdict: Green, with one thing to watch.** Building the three-year gatekeeper timeline is what dissolves the open lead the triage handed over. The CFO "change" was not a gatekeeper exit at all — the outgoing CFO stayed at the company as a segment president, the incoming CFO was named 20 days in advance with a full career history, and no auditor, company secretary or internal auditor left in the same window. **No CFO + auditor cluster; no CFO + company secretary cluster; RF-AUD-006 does not fire, and neither does RF-MGT-001 or RF-MGT-002.** The one item worth a follow-up is the **reversed CAO retirement**: an announced retirement, a named successor, then a reversal 18 days before the effective date and 6 days before a $1.75bn acquisition announcement, with the reason given as no more than "has decided to stay." Both the announcement and the reversal were disclosed properly, which is the opposite of concealment — but the chief accounting officer's succession going in and then out inside a quarter, in the middle of the largest deal in the company's history, is a stability question a reader should keep open.

## 7. KAM / CAM Recurrence (A4-10)

| KAM / CAM | Years it appeared | Underlying balance trend | Sector-standard or company-specific? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Acquisitions — valuation of the Trachte acquired customer-relationship intangible asset** ($206.6m, from $687.5m of consideration; multi-period excess earnings method; the judgments called out are the EBIT-margin and revenue-growth forecasts and the discount and customer-attrition rates) | **FY2024 only, in the readable record.** Deloitte deployed its own fair-value specialists and built an independent range for the discount and attrition rates | Goodwill and intangibles were **$4,469.6m on a $7,146.3m balance sheet** at FY2024 (carried forward from `11_capital-allocation-governance`), and the acquisition programme continued after the reporting date — EPG ~$979.6m (closed 2025-05-01) and Maverick Power $1.75bn + up to $550m earn-out (announced 2026-08-24). The balance behind this class of estimate is **growing** | **Company-specific in its subject** (one named deal), **sector-standard in its type** (purchase-price allocation is a routine CAM for an acquisitive industrial) | **Insufficient Data on recurrence** — the 3-year test cannot be run. A US 10-K prints only the current period's CAM, and the FY2022, FY2023 and FY2025 10-Ks are all absent from the pool. One readable CAM is not a recurrence pattern, and stating that KAMs "evolve" would be a claim the evidence cannot carry | FY24 10-K, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, Critical Audit Matter; FY24 10-K Note 5; `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance` |

**The structural point, stated as a watch item rather than a finding.** A company that buys a business a year will keep producing acquired-intangible-valuation CAMs, and the balance those estimates sit on is compounding. That is not the same defect as a recurring revenue-recognition or receivables KAM on a growing balance — a purchase-price allocation is a one-time exercise per deal, and this one was closed out with independent specialist ranges. But if the FY2025 report's CAM is again an acquired-intangible valuation and the FY2026 report's is again the same, the class becomes recurring even though each instance is new. **Follow-up:** read the FY2025 10-K CAM and classify it; if it is purchase-price allocation for a third straight year against a rising intangible balance, re-test A4-10 against the Red band.

## 8. CARO, Internal & Secretarial Audit (A4-08, A4-11)

**Local equivalents applied.** nVent is a US/SEC filer under Irish company law. CARO (the Companies (Auditor's Report) Order) and the MR-3 secretarial audit report are **India-only instruments** with no US or Irish counterpart — they are Not Applicable by regime, never scored as missing (CLAUDE.md §27). The instruments that carry the same function here, and were read in their place, are the SOX §404(b) ICFR attestation, Item 9, the cover-page error/restatement checkboxes, and the CEO/CFO §302 and §906 certifications.

The committee is also the body that **selects and compensates** the auditor, and the FY2024 CAM narrative records that the matter was "communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee" — evidence of a live reporting channel from the engagement team to the committee, not a claim about it | **Green** | FY2025 DEF 14A, Audit and Finance Committee section (EDGAR, 2026-09-07); FY24 10-K, Critical Audit Matter preamble; FY24 10-K Item 14 |

**Note on the standard applied.** On the pool alone this row would have been **Insufficient Data**, not Green and certainly not Red — silence in the disclosures is never proof that a private session was not held (CLAUDE.md §3/§11; the A4-12 band in MODULE_RULES). Direct retrieval of the proxy converted silence into an affirmative disclosure, and the verdict follows the evidence, not the gap.

## 10. Read

The assurance chain here is able and unafraid on every test a reader can actually run: a Big-4 firm in place since the company's incorporation, unqualified opinions on FY2022–FY2024 and on internal control, no restatement in five years attested on the 10-K cover page itself, no auditor resignation and no Item 4.01 8-K ever filed, an audit committee that met eight times and sat in executive session without management at each meeting, and an auditor whose reappointment drew 0.48% of votes against. The gatekeeper lead the triage handed over dissolves on the evidence — the CFO "departure" was a lateral move to a segment presidency with a successor named 20 days ahead, so there is no exit cluster at all.

What cannot be tested is independence in money terms, and that is the weakest link. **The audit-fee ratio is unreadable** — the FY24 10-K routes Item 14 to a proxy nobody collected, and three direct retrievals of the public proxy truncated before the fee table — so the one Enron-shaped question, whether the auditor earns more from consulting than from auditing, has no answer here. It bites hardest because the very period in question is the one where revenue rose about 29.5% while a ~$979.6m business came in and a $1.7bn one went out; a fee that failed to move with that scope is exactly what A4-07 exists to catch, and it is exactly what this pool cannot show. Two smaller gaps sit alongside it: the **FY2025 auditor's report and ICFR scope are absent**, so the first-year control exclusion for the Electrical Products Group is invisible; and the **signing partner is never named**, so the unit of accountability — and the five-year lead-partner rotation the US regime does require — cannot be checked at all.

To trust these numbers more, three documents would do it: the DEF 14A fee tables for FY2023–FY2025 (the ratio and its trend against scope), the FY2025 Form 10-K (the missing opinion, the missing ICFR scope, and the second CAM that would turn one data point into a recurrence test), and the PCAOB Form AP for the nVent engagement (the partner's name, and a partner-level discipline sweep to replace the coverage-limited row).

**Conclusion: mixed — watch the named link (the unreadable audit-fee ratio, and the FY2025 audit report behind it).** Nothing in the readable record is adverse; the reservation is about what is unreadable, not about what was found.

# Related-Party & Group Forensics — NVT

**Company:** nVent Electric plc · Irish-incorporated, NYSE-listed US domestic filer (SEC CIK 1720635) · reporting currency USD · US GAAP · fiscal year = calendar year.
**As-of date:** 2026-09-07. **Latest annual filing in the frozen pool:** FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-12-31, filed 2025-02-18). **Latest interim:** Q2 FY26 10-Q (period ended 2026-06-30).

**Cross-module inputs used.** `07_people-integrity-dossiers.md` (Discovery Register, Section 3 Network Map, Section 3B lineage read, Section 4 A17-08 reconciliation, `entity_network.json`) — read and reconciled below. `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md` — the >25% RPT hard lock is **not tripped** and is not re-adjudicated here. `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` — revenue, PAT and net-debt denominators taken from it, not recomputed.

**Two data facts that shape everything below, stated up front.**
1. **There is no FY2025 Form 10-K in the frozen pool.** The audited annual read (notes, Exhibit 21 subsidiary list, commitments) is FY2024. FY2025 balance-sheet figures come from the comparative column of the two FY2026 10-Qs, which is filing-grade; FY2025 income-statement figures come from the Capital IQ export, which is tier-5 vendor data and labelled as such wherever used.
2. **The proxy statement is not in the frozen pool.** The FY2024 10-K's Item 13 ("Certain Relationships and Related Transactions") is incorporated by reference to the proxy [FY24 10-K, Item 13]. This agent therefore retrieved the DEF 14A filings directly from SEC EDGAR (2026-03-31, 2025-04-01 and 2024-04-02 filings) and cites them as primary filings retrieved outside the pool, with the retrieval date. Every such row is marked. Agent `07` independently read the same 2026 proxy and reports the same sentence, so the two agents corroborate.

---

## 1. RPT Intensity & the Applicable Regime (A5-01)

**Applicable materiality rule, named per period.** nVent is a US-reporting issuer, so **SEC Regulation S-K Item 404(a)** governs proxy-level related-person disclosure in every year read: any transaction over **$120,000** in which the company is a participant and a director, executive officer, 5%-holder or their immediate family has a direct or indirect material interest. The financial-statement note is governed by **ASC 850** (material related-party transactions must be disclosed in the notes). **nVent's own written policy sets a stricter line than the SEC floor — $50,000** — and routes every candidate transaction to the Governance and Sustainability Committee [nVent DEF 14A filed 2026-03-31, "Policies and Procedures Regarding Related Person Transactions", SEC EDGAR, retrieved 2026-09-07]. There was **no regime change across FY2023–FY2025**: the same Item 404(a) $120,000 floor and the same $50,000 company policy applied in all three years. The India LODR Reg 23 graded-slab change of December 2025 is **not applicable** to this issuer and is not used anywhere in this report.

One jurisdictional overlay does apply on top, because nVent is an Irish plc: under Irish company law **a guarantee or security for a loan, quasi-loan or credit transaction to a director or a connected person requires a special resolution of shareholders** (a 75% supermajority) [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4 — Description of Securities, "Voting"]. That is a stronger structural gate on the A5-03 channel than the US default, and no such resolution appears on any AGM ballot in the period read.

**Verdict, A5-01: Green.** Below the 1–5% green band by the maximum possible margin — the value is nil, affirmatively stated, on three separate evidence legs (the audited notes' silence where ASC 850 would speak, the leases note's explicit denial, and the proxy's explicit sentence).

Every band in this section that turns on "promoter" therefore has no subject — which is a real answer, not a data gap, and it is why five of the six A5 channel tests below read Green on structure rather than on measurement.

**Slab-slicing result — the sums actually checked.** Same-counterparty totals were computed per year across every named counterparty in §4 and every party-in-interest row in §2, then compared against the approval slab of **$50,000** (the company's own policy line, stricter than the SEC's $120,000):
- **Related-person counterparties, FY2023 / FY2024 / FY2025: $0 / $0 / $0** summed per counterparty — nothing to slice, and nothing sitting just under the line.
- **Fidelity group, FY2025 (plan-level, ERISA-exempt, paid by the Plan not the company): $139,431** of administrative fees, taken as one summed total rather than as separate fund-level charges. It is **above** the $50,000 policy line on a summed basis — and it is disclosed in full, itemised, labelled exempt, and paid by a different legal person (the Plan) than the issuer. Summing it is exactly the discipline the slab-slicing test demands; the total survives the test on disclosure.
- **Empower Trust Company LLC + Alerus Financial, N.A., FY2025: $8,966** summed — below the line even in aggregate.
No pattern of several deals each landing just under a threshold exists, because there are no deals.

**The aborted-deal sweep, and what it covered.** Board-meeting outcomes and material-event disclosures for a US issuer arrive as Form 8-K, and the frozen pool contains no 8-Ks — so the sweep was run against EDGAR and public announcement records instead, dated in the Sweep Log. It returned **no terminated, withdrawn or abandoned acquisition agreement for nVent in 2024, 2025 or 2026**, and no proposal of any kind involving a director-, officer- or 5%-holder-linked seller. The 2026 proxy adds the forward-looking half of the same test in the company's own words: "**To our knowledge, no related person transactions are currently proposed**" [DEF 14A filed 2026-03-31]. The Satyam-Maytas trigger — a board-approved-then-aborted purchase of a controller's entity — has **no candidate event** here. **A5-09: Green.**

**RF-CAP-004 is tested and not fired, with the reasoning stated.** nVent is unambiguously an **acquisitive** company: five acquisitions in four years, and the pending Maverick deal at $1.75bn plus a $550m earn-out. §24 Filter 4 asks whether that is a value-destructive serial-acquirer pattern, especially debt-funded near or above the company's own value. On this module's evidence it is not: the two largest completed deals were funded with **cash on hand** ($975.4m for EPG, explicitly "available cash on hand" [Q2 FY26 10-Q, MD&A]), leverage on the strict basis **fell** from 3.01× at FY2024 to 1.60× at FY2025 [earnings/01, Table 1], and revenue and absolute EBITDA both rose through the programme. Maverick is to be funded with "a combination of available cash on hand and new debt" [press release 2026-08-24], which is the one item to re-test after close. Deals are **not** the leakage channel here — every seller is a third party — so RF-CAP-004 does not attach on the A5-09 route. The capital-allocation *quality* judgment belongs to `02_capital-allocation-scorecard`, which owns it; this row exists so the two agents cannot disagree about whether the pattern was noticed.

## 8. Group-Structure Map (A11-01)

| Metric | Value | Band | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Layers, listco → deepest entity | **Not disclosed.** SEC Exhibit 21 requires a list of subsidiaries and their jurisdictions; it does **not** require the ownership chain, and nVent's does not give one. *Inference, not from filings:* the entity names imply at least three tiers — nVent Electric plc (Ireland) → the Luxembourg/Netherlands/Swiss holding and finance layer (nVent Finance S.à r.l., nVent International Holding S.à r.l., nVent Global S.à r.l., nVent Holding NL B.V., nVent Finance Group GmbH) → country holdcos (nVent Holdings, Inc., nVent UK Holdings Limited, Schroff Holdings Germany GmbH, Eldon Holding AB) → operating companies | ≤2 Green; >3 Red | **Insufficient Data** — the chain is genuinely not disclosed in this filing regime; the inference points to ≥3 tiers and is labelled as inference | [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 21] |

| Offshore entities without evident purpose | **0 identified.** Four Luxembourg and five Netherlands / five Swiss entities exist and each has a stated function: nVent Finance S.à r.l. is the **named issuer of the senior notes** and Hoffman Schroff Holdings, Inc. is a **named co-guarantor**; the Swiss entities include nVent Services GmbH (the brand proprietor) and the Thermal Europe operating business. No entity sits in a secrecy jurisdiction with no named role | 0 Green | **Green** | [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 21 and Note 10 (Debt)]; [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 10] |
| Entities that only move money | **The finance/holding layer does exactly this, and it is disclosed as doing so**: "nVent Electric plc … has no independent assets or operations unrelated to its investments in consolidated subsidiaries and the guarantees of the Notes"; "nVent Finance's principal source of cash flow … is interest income from its subsidiaries" | 0 Green | **Amber — present, but named, purposed, and consolidated**, not hidden | [FY24 10-K, Note 10 (Debt) — Guarantor disclosure]; [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 10] |
| Perimeter change since the last audited list | The FY2025 Exhibit 21 is **absent from the pool**. The Form 11-K names **eight** entities that became participating employers on 2026-01-01 — nVent Enclosures System – Chattanooga LLC, Central Electric Manufacturing Company LLC, The Calvert Company LLC, Critical Power Equipment & Solutions, Inc., CGIT Systems LLC, nVent Enclosures Systems LLC, Powergrid Solutions LLC, Atkinson Industries LLC — plus WASP Critical Power Solutions, i.e. the acquired EPG entities. The Thermal entities left on 2025-01-30 | — | **Amber (coverage)** — the current perimeter is partly reconstructed, not read from an audited list | [FY25 Form 11-K, Note 1 — Subsequent Events and plan participation]; [FY24 10-K, Note 6] |

**What each layer is FOR, one line each.**
- **nVent Electric plc (Ireland)** — the listed parent and note guarantor; holds investments in subsidiaries and, on its own statement, nothing else.
- **The Luxembourg / Netherlands finance layer (nVent Finance S.à r.l., nVent Global S.à r.l., nVent International Holding S.à r.l., nVent Luxembourg S.à r.l., nVent Finance NL B.V., nVent Holding NL B.V.)** — issues the group's senior notes and on-lends the proceeds to the operating companies; that on-lending is the $1,592.1m receivable in §9.
- **The Swiss layer (nVent Services GmbH, nVent Services Holding GmbH, nVent Finance Group GmbH, nVent Thermal Europe GmbH, Hoffman Schroff GmbH)** — holds the brand estate and, before the divestiture, the European Thermal business.
- **The country holdcos (nVent Holdings, Inc., nVent International Holdings, Inc., nVent UK Holdings Limited, Schroff Holdings Germany GmbH, Eldon Holding AB, Hoffman Schroff Holdings, Inc.)** — hold the local operating stacks and, in one case, co-guarantee the notes.
- **The acquisition stacks (ERICO ×11, Hoffman/Schroff ×12, ILSCO ×6, ECM ×5, Trachte ×5, CIS Global ×6, Eldon ×10, Warrior/Parkline ×7)** — each acquired brand family arrived with its own legal entities, which is where most of the 137 count comes from.
- **The operating companies in 33 jurisdictions** — local statutory entities required to employ people, hold licences, and invoice locally.

**The A11-01 judgment, stated rather than mechanically banded.** 137 entities is above the registry's >100 red line. It is not, on this evidence, the IL&FS pattern the line exists to catch: debt does **not** sit where ratings cannot reach — it sits at one named issuer (nVent Finance S.à r.l.) guaranteed by the listed parent, and the filings say in terms that "**there are no significant restrictions on the ability of nVent Electric plc to obtain funds from its subsidiaries by dividend or loan**" and "**none of the assets of nVent Electric plc or its subsidiaries represents restricted net assets pursuant to the guidelines established by the Securities and Exchange Commission**" [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 10 (Debt)]. Entity count tracks the acquisition history and the country footprint one-for-one. The honest verdict is **Amber**: above the numeric line, with visible purpose for every layer, and with the ownership chain undisclosed so a reader cannot independently verify the depth.

## 9. Cash & Funding Topology (A11-02, A11-03)

**Matched-basis rule (CLAUDE.md §15).** Every ratio below names the basis on both sides. All cash figures are **period-end balances** from the same MD&A sentence in the same filing, so numerator and denominator are measured the same way and the ratios are matched without qualification. No peak, no cap, no maximum-daily-balance figure is used anywhere in this section — so no mismatched ratio is published and no monitoring threshold rests on one.

| Question | Raw value | Basis (both sides) | Matched ratio | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where does consolidated cash sit (parent vs subs)? | The listed parent holds essentially none: "nVent Electric plc … **has no independent assets or operations unrelated to its investments in consolidated subsidiaries** and the guarantees of the Notes". Cash sits at the operating subsidiaries | Qualitative filing statement; no split disclosed | n/a — the split is not disclosed | **Amber** — normal for a holding-company structure, but the parent-vs-subsidiary cash split is genuinely not quantified in any filing read | [FY24 10-K, Note 10]; [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 10] |
| Cash held where repatriation is limited | 2024-12-31: **$53.2m of $131.2m**. 2026-03-31: **$75.1m of $190.0m**. 2026-06-30: **$79.6m of $256.0m** | Both sides = **period-end cash balance**, same sentence, same filing | **40.5%** → **39.5%** → **31.1%** — matched, and **falling** | **Amber — sizeable but shrinking, and disclosed to the dollar every quarter** | [FY24 10-K, MD&A Liquidity]; [Q1 FY26 10-Q, MD&A Liquidity]; [Q2 FY26 10-Q, MD&A Liquidity] |
| Share held with a related **finance company** or treasury vehicle | **$0.0m held with any entity outside the consolidated group.** The group's treasury vehicle, nVent Finance S.à r.l., is a **100%-owned consolidated Luxembourg subsidiary** — not an affiliated non-consolidated finance company | n/a | **0.0%** external | **Green** | [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 21 and Note 10] |
| Parent borrowing while subs hold the cash? | **Yes in form, and explicitly de-risked in substance.** The notes are issued by nVent Finance S.à r.l. and guaranteed by nVent Electric plc, while cash sits at operating subsidiaries. The filings then state: "**There are no significant restrictions on the ability of nVent Electric plc to obtain funds from its subsidiaries by dividend or loan. None of the assets … represents restricted net assets pursuant to the guidelines established by the Securities and Exchange Commission**" | Both statements are as of the same balance-sheet date | n/a — a legal-restriction test, not a ratio | **Green, with the contradiction adjudicated below** | [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 10 (Debt)] |
| ICDs to group entities — amount, rate, tenor | **$1,592.1m** of Obligor Group noncurrent assets due **from non-guarantor subsidiaries**, against Obligor Group noncurrent assets of $1,599.9m. Rate and tenor **not disclosed** — the balances are eliminated on consolidation and the summarized Obligor Group table does not price them | Both sides = **period-end** balances at 2026-06-30, from the same table | **99.5%** of Obligor Group noncurrent assets are intercompany receivables — matched | **Green on leakage** (every counterparty is a 100%-owned consolidated subsidiary, so nothing leaves the group); **Amber on visibility** (rate and tenor undisclosed) | [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 10 — Obligor Group table, footnote 2]; [Q1 FY26 10-Q, Note 8 — same figure] |
| Evergreen / rolled-over ICDs? | The $1,592.1m receivable is **identical to the cent** at 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 — a flat balance across two quarters, consistent with a standing internal funding line rather than a rolling short-term deposit | Both sides = period-end, one quarter apart | Change = **$0.0m / 0.0%** | **Amber — recorded, not adverse.** Standing intra-group funding of a bond issuer's on-lending is the intended mechanics of the structure, not an evergreen advance to an outsider | [Q1 FY26 10-Q, Note 8]; [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 10] |

**Adjudicating the number that disagrees (CLAUDE.md §3).** Two statements in the same filings point different ways and both belong in the record. The debt note says there are "no significant restrictions" on the parent getting funds from subsidiaries and no restricted net assets under SEC guidelines. The MD&A says $79.6m of the $256.0m cash balance "is held in certain countries in which the ability to repatriate is limited due to local regulations or significant potential tax consequences." They are not in conflict once the tests are named: the debt note answers the **SEC Rule 4-08(e) restricted-net-assets** test, which is about legal restrictions on dividends and loans; the MD&A answers a **practical and tax-cost** question. Both are true. The conservative read is the MD&A's: roughly **31% of period-end cash is not freely movable without local-regulatory friction or a tax charge**, and that share should be treated as the working figure, not the debt note's zero.

**No related financial counterparty exists, so the extra facts that row would require do not arise.** The company's own equity interest in its treasury vehicle is 100%; nVent Finance S.à r.l. is not a regulated financial institution and no approved cap, utilisation, or independent-director review of a related-finance-company exposure is disclosed, because there is no such exposure. Recording that explicitly is the point: the exposure is nil, and it is nil for a structural reason (the treasury vehicle is inside the consolidation), not because a disclosure is missing.

**Monitoring threshold, stated on a basis measurable again next quarter.** Repatriation-limited cash as a share of **period-end** cash, both figures from the same MD&A liquidity sentence: 40.5% (2024-12-31) → 39.5% (2026-03-31) → **31.1% (2026-06-30)**. The same two numbers appear in the same sentence every quarter, so this ratio can be re-measured identically at the next 10-Q. **A11-02: Amber. A11-03: Green on leakage, Amber on visibility.**

The two do not compete and share no marks. **Does the listco transact with it, or with anyone who controls it?** **No.** What survives is administration of legacy equity awards under "earlier Pentair stock incentive plans that are now outstanding under the 2018 Plan" and nVent's and Pentair's shared status as parties to the March-2018 indenture — no trading relationship, no control, no fee | **$0.0m flows between them.** Nothing to price | **Green — checked, and the answer is that nothing flows** | [FY24 10-K, Item 1 — separation history]; [FY24 10-K, Note 16 (Share-Based Compensation) — legacy Pentair plans]; [FY24 10-K, Exhibits 4.1 and 4.2 — 2018 indenture parties]; [07, Sections 2B.3 and 3B] |

**Why the predecessor read matters here even though it comes back clean.** `07`'s Section 3B establishes that nVent's history claims ("roots trace back to the acquisition of Federal-Hoffman Corporation in 1988") reconcile to a **2017-05-30 incorporation** through a named, dated, disclosed spin-off — a pro-rata distribution to Pentair's own shareholders, one nVent share for every Pentair share, completed 2018-04-30 [FY24 10-K, Item 1]. That is continuity through a formal disclosed process, not assets moved to an insider. The one live fact worth carrying — Pentair is a defendant in 2026 securities-fraud class actions over 2025–26 conduct in its **Pool** segment, a business nVent never owned — is a `12`/`07` matter, carries no flow between the two companies, and is **not** a leakage finding here. **A11-04: Not Applicable on the promoter limb (no controller); Green on the lineage limb (checked, nothing flows).**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A11-05** | Material subs' financials visible & audited; structure stable | **Visibility is partial and regime-limited.** US GAAP consolidates; the SEC does not require stand-alone subsidiary financials, and none are published. That is deal activity with full disclosure, not churn used to obscure. **Below-threshold associates: two, and both are tiny** — **Iceotope Group Limited at 5.2%** and **Torgoterm AD at 19%**, both named on Exhibit 21 with their percentages footnoted. Naming a 5.2% holding on a subsidiary exhibit is **more** disclosure than the rule requires, which is the opposite of the pattern this test hunts | stable perimeter / engineered below thresholds | **Green on the associate limb; Amber on churn** | [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 21, footnote: "Iceotope is 5.2% owned. Torgoterm AD is 19% owned"]; [Q2 FY26 10-Q, Notes 5 and 6] |
| **A11-06** | Independent-director seat on every unlisted material subsidiary's board; secretarial audit of material subs | **Not Applicable (regime).** SEBI LODR Reg 24(1) and the secretarial-audit requirement are Indian rules; nVent is a US-reporting Irish plc and neither applies. The functionally comparable US/Irish protections — an all-independent audit committee overseeing the whole consolidation, Section 302/906 certifications by the CEO and CFO covering all subsidiaries, and an unqualified ICFR audit — are **in place** | Reg 24(1) bands (India) | **Not Applicable (regime — Indian rule, non-Indian issuer); the comparable US/Irish protections are present** | [FY24 10-K, Item 9A — Controls and Procedures, disclosure controls concluded effective]; [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 23] |

The **Irish** equivalent is stronger in one specific respect and was checked: Irish company law requires a **special resolution** for a guarantee or security in a credit transaction with a director or connected person, for an off-market purchase of shares, and for a scheme of arrangement. The **$1.7bn Thermal Management divestiture** — roughly 25% of FY2024 total assets — was executed **without a shareholder vote**, which is lawful for a US-reporting Irish plc where the sale is not substantially all of the undertaking, and which is a genuine difference from the Indian regime | Reg 24(5)-(6) bands (India) | **Not Applicable (regime); the divestiture-without-a-vote fact is recorded because a reader comparing regimes should see it** | [FY24 10-K, Exhibit 4 — Description of Securities, matters requiring special resolutions]; [FY24 10-K, Note 6 (Discontinued Operations)] |

## 14. Read

**Value moving to a controller or a related party: $0.0m a year, 0.0% of PAT, in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025** — and the finding rests on three independent legs rather than one convenient sentence: the audited statements carry no ASC 850 note where a material flow would force one, the leases note explicitly denies any related-party lease, and the proxy states in terms "we had no related person transactions during 2025" against a self-imposed **$50,000** threshold that is stricter than the SEC's own $120,000 line. There is no controller to leak to — the largest holder is Vanguard at 5.24%, filed passive — so the whole promoter-channel apparatus (royalty, promoter vendor, promoter customer, sibling private company, insider on both sides of a trade) has no subject, and the brand estate that would otherwise be the obvious channel sits **inside** the consolidation at nVent Services GmbH at a zero external rate.

**The single largest channel, if one ever opens, is the group's own plumbing rather than any counterparty:** $1,592.1m of intercompany funding flowing from the Luxembourg note issuer down to non-guarantor subsidiaries — 99.5% of the Obligor Group's noncurrent assets, unchanged to the cent across two quarters, with rate and tenor undisclosed. Every counterparty on that line is a 100%-owned consolidated subsidiary, so nothing leaves the group; it is a visibility item, not a leakage item, and it is the one place a future related-party transaction would be hardest to see.

**Would the structure let leakage hide?** Partly. 137 named entities across 33 jurisdictions is above the >100 line, the ownership chain between them is not disclosed in this filing regime, no material subsidiary publishes its own numbers, roughly 31% of period-end cash sits where repatriation is limited by local rules or tax cost, and the perimeter moved twice in eighteen months ($1.7bn out, $979.6m in, $1.75bn pending). Set against that: the debt sits at one named issuer guaranteed by the listed parent with a published Obligor Group table, there are no variable interest entities and no unconsolidated special-purpose entities at all, the captive insurer is consolidated and named, and even a 5.2% shareholding is disclosed on an exhibit that does not require it.

**The one disclosure that would settle the biggest open question: the FY2025 Form 10-K Exhibit 21** — the audited subsidiary list as of 2025-12-31. It is the only document that would show the post-divestiture, post-EPG group perimeter as management and the auditor actually certify it, rather than reconstructed from a benefit-plan filing; it would confirm whether the Russian entity is still in the group; and it would give the entity count the next run should be judging, instead of a count that is eighteen months stale.

No VIE, no SPE, no unconsolidated structured entity; the captive insurer and the Luxembourg finance vehicle are both named and consolidated. | **Total** | **14** | **100** | |

**Reading the score.** 0 = no leakage risk found on a FULL read; 100 = leakage proven. **14/100** means: on a read that reached the audited annual notes, two interim filings, the benefit-plan filing, three proxy statements retrieved from EDGAR, the AGM voting results, the 13G ownership filings and `07`'s 53-subject network, **no value was found leaving minority shareholders through any related-party channel**, and the residual risk is about structural visibility — undisclosed layer depth, undisclosed intercompany pricing, and an entity count above the numeric line — rather than about conduct. Each checklist item contributes to exactly one component; nothing is double-counted.

**Score caps considered.**
- The **"No related-party note / RPT disclosure" cap (RPT & leakage risk floor 40)** was examined and **does NOT apply**. The rule exists for a pool where the RPT position is unknown. Here the position is affirmatively **known and nil** from three independent evidence legs, including the company's own explicit sentence and an audited note set where ASC 850 would have compelled a note. Marking a proven nil as "unknown, therefore floored at 40" would be a bad-extraction error in the opposite direction from the one the rule guards against. The partial-data rule's *disclosure* limb is separately recorded at finding 09-029 as an **Amber on pool coverage**, which is where it belongs.
- **RF-CAP-004** tested and not fired on the A5-09 route (deals are not the leakage channel; all sellers third-party) — see finding 09-014. The capital-allocation-quality question is `02`'s.
- **RF-NET-003** — `07` left one judgment visible for `99`: whether the residual nVent↔Pentair link is "live". **From this module's angle the answer is unambiguous: $0.0m flows between the two companies**, so whatever `99` decides about the exposure grade, it does not change the leakage read here.
- No cap from `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` — no hard disqualifier flagged.

# Contingent Liabilities & Commitments — NVT

**Company:** nVent Electric plc (NYSE: NVT). **Jurisdiction / regime:** US SEC domestic filer (Irish-incorporated plc) — the contingency note is the 10-K "Commitments and Contingencies" note plus Item 3 (Legal Proceedings), not an Ind AS Schedule III note [`FY24 10-K, Note 18`; `FY24 10-K, Item 3`]. **Reporting standard:** US GAAP. **Reporting currency: USD, in millions.** **Fiscal year ends 31 December.** **Latest balance-sheet date: 30 June 2026** [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets`].

**Evidence binding.** Frozen generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6`. Live `data/NVT/` was not read; `data/NVT/…` is a citation label only.

### Four framing points before the tables

1. **`balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md` exists and was read.** Its quantified exposures — the $102.0m of bonds/LCs/guarantees, the $550.0m Maverick earnout cap, the $1,066.1m mixed-basis maximum, the 26.7%-of-equity ratio — are taken as given and cited to it. **This report does not recompute them.** What is added on top is the governance lens this module owns: whether the disclosure is honest, how each item moved year by year, whether probable losses are provided or parked, and the A7a items `05` does not cover (indirect tax, statutory dues, regulator demands, recourse financing, capital commitments, derivatives).
2. **There is no "total contingent liabilities" line anywhere.** A US GAAP filer is not required to publish one, and nVent does not. So the A7a-01 headline is built by this agent from the itemised disclosures, and the build is printed so a reader can rebuild it (CLAUDE.md §15). Three different totals are given because three different bases are defensible, and each is labelled.
3. **The FY2025 Form 10-K is absent from this pool** — the Q2 FY26 10-Q cross-refers to it by name ("legal proceedings previously disclosed in Item 3 of our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K") [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Part II Item 1`], so the audited FY2025 contingency note and FY2025 Item 3 exist but cannot be read here. Annual-note depth in this pool is therefore **FY2024 (Note 18, with FY2023 comparatives), plus the FY2022–FY2024 unrecognized-tax-benefit roll-forward, plus two 2026 interim notes.** A contingency note DOES exist, so the MODULE_RULES "no contingent-liability note" floor is not applied; a reduced-depth confidence cap is (see §11).
4. **This company has no promoter and no controlling shareholder.** nVent is a widely held plc. Every guarantee in the pool runs between 100%-owned group entities. RF-RPT-003 does not fire and there is nothing to cross-route to `09` (A5-03) on guarantees — stated so the silence is not mistaken for an unchecked box.

## 1. Headline Exposure (A7a-01)

**Reporting currency USD, millions. Period: 30 June 2026, except where a line is explicitly post-balance-sheet or stale.** Totals A and B are built by this agent from the itemised disclosures; total C is taken verbatim from `balance-sheet-survival/05` and is NOT recomputed here.

**The build (so the totals can be rebuilt):**
- Bonds, letters of credit and bank guarantees, face value at 30-Jun-2026: **102.0** [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15`]
- Contractual purchase obligations (raw materials): **66.7 for calendar 2025 only** — a stale one-year figure; the 2026 equivalent lives in the absent FY2025 10-K [`FY24 10-K, MD&A, "Material contractual cash requirements"`]
- Maverick Power earnout cap: **up to 550.0**, arising from a definitive agreement signed **24-Aug-2026** — **after** the 30-Jun-2026 balance-sheet date [`nVent news release "nVent to Acquire Maverick Power", 2026-08-24`]

Maximum / gross exposure — taken verbatim from `balance-sheet-survival/05`, not recomputed** (mixed basis: undiscounted leases, gross pension/OPEB, gross UTBs, LC face value, stale purchase commitment, post-BS earnout cap) | **1,066.1** | Total equity = 3,986.9 | **26.7%** *(`05`'s own figure)*; **12.9% excluding the earnout** *(`05`'s own figure)* | >25% → Red on the stated basis | **Amber — the basis, not the number, is what disqualifies a clean Red**: over half this total is recognized leases and pensions that already sit on the balance sheet and pay out over 5–12 years, so it is not a contingent-liability total in the A7a sense | `balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md`, §4 Build B |
| **Total commitments (separate line, as A7a requires)** — firm Maverick purchase price, post-balance-sheet | **1,750.0** | Net worth = 3,986.9 [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Balance Sheets`] | **43.89%** | Not a contingency — a firm, funded commitment | **Amber (scale)** — committed, bridge-financed, closing conditions only | `nVent news release, 2026-08-24`; funding already carried in `balance-sheet-survival/01`, §5A |
| **Total commitments — contracted capital expenditure** | **Not separately disclosed** — no contracted-capex line exists in any pool document | Net worth = 3,986.9 | n/a | Nil-vs-undisclosed rule: **not separately disclosed**, therefore not Green | **Amber** | `FY24 10-K, MD&A, "Material contractual cash requirements"` — lists debt, interest, leases and raw-material purchase obligations, and nothing for capex |

**How A7a-01 is graded, stated plainly.** On the balance sheet as it stood at 30 June 2026, nVent's disclosed contingent exposure is **$168.7m, or 4.23% of the $3,986.9m equity base — inside the Green band.** Add the signed-but-unclosed Maverick earnout and it becomes **$718.7m, 18.03% of net worth (Amber) and 120.12% of $598.3m of LTM profit (Red on the profit limb)**. Applying the conservative default (CLAUDE.md §4), **the item is graded Amber overall and RF-FIN-003 fires** — contingent liability above 5% of net worth.

**What that flag does and does not mean.** The $550.0m driving it is a performance earnout on 2027 and 2028 results at a business nVent has agreed to buy but does not yet own; it becomes payable only in the state of the world where the acquired business hits its numbers, and management's own words point toward paying it — returns are "significantly better if the potential additional considerations are paid" [`nVent news release, 2026-08-24`]. It is not a tax demand, not a judgment, not an adjudicated loss, and not a related-party obligation. **It is also not yet a disclosure failure:** the agreement was signed 24-Aug-2026 and the most recent nVent filing in this pool is the Q2 FY26 10-Q filed 31-Jul-2026, so no filing has yet come due in which it should have appeared. Materiality is graded **High, not Critical**, because the Materiality Thresholds table reserves Critical for adjudicated or adversarial exposure, and this is a commercial purchase-price term.

The mirror-image test applies instead, and it is the finding of this section: **the disclosure text stayed word-for-word identical across three filings while the one number in it moved 9.5-fold.** The bonds/LC/guarantee paragraph in the Q2 FY26 10-Q is the same paragraph as in the FY24 10-K, character for character apart from the dates and the two figures [compare `FY24 10-K, Note 18` with `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15`]. ᵃ **Label-change caveat.** The FY24 10-K roll-forward is headed "gross unrecognized tax benefits" and ends at 11.7; the 10-Qs use the phrase "the liability for uncertain tax positions was $9.4 million and $10.3 million". The two labels are treated here as the same measure because they occupy the same balance-sheet lines and the series is continuous, but the wording differs and the 10-Q gives no roll-forward. Flagged, not smoothed over.

**Nothing vanished, and nothing crystallized.** Every item that appears in the FY24 10-K note appears again in the FY26 interim notes, or is an annual-only disclosure that a 10-Q is not required to repeat. The "Other matters" litigation paragraph in `FY24 10-K, Note 18` is absent from `Q1/Q2 FY26 Note 15`, but its substance is carried by `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Part II Item 1`, which states there have been "no material developments" with respect to the proceedings disclosed in the FY2025 10-K — a relocation, not a disappearance. **No contingency in any period converted into a real loss or a provision.** The one movement out of a contingency account went the other way — $12.5m released INTO income. **RF-CL-003 (repeated crystallization) therefore does not fire.**

**RF-CL-001 fires** on the bonds/LC/guarantee line: 10.7 → 75.7 is a 7.08x year-on-year rise, comfortably past the A7a-02 red band, with no item-specific narrative.

**The explanation the company never gave, supplied here and labelled.** nVent completed the acquisition of Avail Infrastructure Solutions' enclosures, switchgear and bus-systems businesses (the "Electrical Products Group") on **1 May 2025** for approximately **$979.6m in cash** [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 5`]. That is a project-and-backlog business selling to power utilities and data centres — exactly the kind of work that requires performance bonds. The FY2025 jump in bond and LC face value is chronologically consistent with that acquisition, and with revenue rising 46.2% over the LTM period [`earnings/01_historical-financials`, §2]. **Inference, not from filings** — nVent nowhere links the two, and does not disclose whether it assumed existing Avail instruments or posted new ones. **The mechanism is benign; the silence is the finding.**

## 9. Provided vs Only-Disclosed (A7a-14)

**The test, stated plainly.** Under US GAAP (ASC 450) a loss that is *probable* and estimable must be booked as a cost now; one that is only *reasonably possible* is disclosed but not booked. The governance question is whether the label matches the actual record, not whether management asserts it does.

| Dispute / claim | Classified as (probable / possible) | Appeal record says | Provision held | Candor verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **Unrecognized tax benefits** | **Probable and estimable — booked** | **No loss at any level in five disclosed years.** Settlements with authorities: nil FY2024, 0.2 FY2023, 2.3 FY2022. Balance fell every year: 15.6 → 13.4 → 13.9 → 11.7 → 10.3 → 9.4 | **9.4** booked at 30-Jun-2026, plus **2.0** penalties and **1.4** interest | **Green — honest and conservative.** The company books a liability for positions it has not lost, and the balance shrinks through statute expiry rather than through defeats | `FY24 10-K, income-tax note`; `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 11` |
| **General litigation** (commercial, product liability, asbestos, patent, employment) | **"Unlikely" to be material, with a "remote possibility" of a material adverse ruling** — the company's exact words | **There is no appeal record to test the label against.** Not one adverse ruling, interim order, settlement or judgment is disclosed in any period, and `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Part II Item 1` reports "no material developments" | **Not disclosed** — no aggregate reserve in any period | **Amber.** The label is not contradicted by anything, so it cannot be called evasive; but **the split is never quantified, so a reader cannot check it.** A7a-14's green band requires "the split stated" — it is not | `FY24 10-K, Item 3`; `FY24 10-K, Note 18`; `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Part II Item 1` |
| **Environmental clean-ups / PRP** | **Probable and estimable portions accrued site-by-site**; the rest neither probable nor estimable | No adverse determination disclosed | **"Not material" — accrued but never sized** | **Amber.** The methodology is textbook-correct and openly stated; the number is withheld, and the company itself warns actual liabilities "will exceed the amount of our current reserves" | `FY24 10-K, Item 3 — Environmental matters` |
| **Product / service warranty** | Accrued on historical claim experience | n/a | **"Not material" — never sized**, four consecutive periods | **Amber** | `FY24 10-K, Note 18`; `Q1/Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15` |
| **Bonds, LCs and bank guarantees ($102.0m face)** | **Only-disclosed.** The accounting policy is stated — "We recognize, at the inception of a guarantee, a liability for the fair value of the obligation undertaken in issuing the guarantee" — but **no liability amount is given at any date** | No draw, call or non-performance event disclosed in any period | **$0 booked against $102.0m of face value** | **Amber.** For performance bonds a nil fair-value liability is normal when no non-performance is expected; **but the policy sentence promises a number and the note never delivers one, at any date, while the face value rose 9.5-fold** | `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15`; `FY24 10-K, Note 18` |
| **Disposition indemnities** | **Only-disclosed**, expressly not estimable | "Historically, we have not made significant payments for these indemnifications" | Nil | **Amber** — open-ended by admission, but the admission itself is candid and the historical record supports it | `FY24 10-K, Note 18`; `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15` |
| **The $12.5m guarantee liability released in FY2024** | Was probable (booked), then **de-recognised into income** | No forum, no counterparty, no explanation of what changed | **Now nil** | **Amber.** A provision going the *right* way is the opposite of the RF-CL-002 pattern — but a $12.5m credit to profit (**5.19% of $240.8m of continuing-operations net income**) explained in one MD&A sentence, with no note, is thin | `FY24 10-K, MD&A "Other expense (income)"`; `FY24 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows` |

**RF-CL-002 does NOT fire.** That flag requires large probable losses carried as "possible" through **serial appeal losses**, unprovided. nVent has lost nothing, anywhere, in any year disclosed in this pool: no adverse ruling, no confirmed demand, no dismissed appeal. Judged against the actual record rather than against management's assertion, **the probable/possible labels are not contradicted by a single data point.** The candor problem here is the opposite one — **nVent quantifies almost nothing, so most of its labels cannot be independently checked at all.** That is a completeness failing, not a provisioning failing, and it is graded as such.

## 11. Read

**nVent's disclosed off-P&L exposure at the balance-sheet date is $168.7m — 4.23% of a $3,986.9m equity base [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets`] — and there is not one adverse ruling, confirmed tax demand, dismissed appeal, regulator penalty, related-party guarantee or recourse receivable financing anywhere in five years of disclosure.** Add the $550.0m Maverick Power earnout signed on 24 August 2026 and the figure becomes $718.7m, 18.03% of net worth and 120.12% of $598.3m of LTM profit [`CIQ → Income Statement, LTM Jun-30-2026`], which fires RF-FIN-003 — but that item is a performance earnout on a business nVent does not yet own, payable only if it hits its 2027–2028 numbers, and no filing has yet come due in which it should have been disclosed.

**The single worst item is not a dispute at all — it is the one number nVent does publish.** Bonds, letters of credit and bank guarantees went 10.5 → 10.7 → 75.7 → 82.6 → 102.0 across December 2023, December 2024, December 2025, March 2026 and June 2026: **a 7.08x rise in FY2025 and a further 34.7% in six months, carried at $0 of booked liability, described by the same unchanged paragraph in every filing.** The lead finding of this report is the mirror image of the flat-total trap: **the disclosure text stayed still while the number moved 9.5-fold.** The most plausible cause is benign and sits elsewhere in the same filings — the $979.6m Electrical Products Group acquisition closed 1 May 2025 brought in a switchgear and bus-systems project business that posts performance bonds [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 5`] — but nVent never connects the two, and that inference is this agent's, not the company's. RF-CL-001 fires on the trend.

**On provisioning, management provides rather than parks — but it quantifies almost nothing.** The unrecognized-tax-benefit book is fully booked at $9.4m (0.24% of net worth), falls every single year, comes with a complete line-by-line roll-forward, and has lost nothing at any level in Germany, India or the U.S. state audits it discloses; that is honest and testable. Against it: **no aggregate litigation reserve in any period, an environmental reserve and a warranty accrual described only as "not material", asbestos named with no claim count and no reserve, a Tonka Bay captive whose reserves are never disclosed, indemnities the company says cannot be estimated, and a $12.5m guarantee liability released straight into FY2024 income — 5.19% of continuing-operations profit — on a single MD&A sentence.** RF-CL-002 and RF-CL-003 do not fire, because nothing has been lost and nothing has crystallized; the failing is completeness, not candor about defeats.

**What a rational minority holder should watch next, in order:** (1) whether the bonds/LC line keeps compounding past $102.0m and whether the FY2026 10-K finally splits performance bonds from financial standby LCs and gives a fair-value liability, as its own stated policy promises; (2) the Maverick earnout — whether the Q3/Q4 FY26 filings disclose it, how it is measured, and whether any part is booked as contingent consideration on closing; (3) whether the approximately $25.8m IEEPA tariff reimbursement recognised in Q2 FY26 profit is ever characterised as final or contestable, because right now it sits in income with no disclosed legal status at all; and (4) the FY2025 10-K, which is absent from this pool and is where the audited FY2025 contingency note and Item 3 would resolve most of what is marked Insufficient Data above.

**Partial-data statement.** A contingency note exists and was read (`FY24 10-K, Note 18`; `Q1 FY26 10-Q, Note 15`; `Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note 15`), so the MODULE_RULES "no contingent-liability note" floor is **not** applied. The **FY2025 Form 10-K is absent from this pool**, so annual-note depth is one full year plus comparatives rather than the 3–5 years this agent's workflow requires; the movement table is built from four balance-sheet dates for the quantified lines and three fiscal years for the tax roll-forward. Confidence is capped accordingly and the affected rows are marked Insufficient Data rather than assumed.

# Accounting Forensics — NVT

**Company:** nVent Electric plc (NYSE: NVT). **Jurisdiction / regime:** US SEC domestic filer, Irish-incorporated. **Reporting standard:** US GAAP. **Currency: USD, in millions except per-share.** **Fiscal year ends 31 December.**

**Evidence binding.** All reads went through the frozen extract generation `6db32848…1aecd1e6` (`manifest.json`, `corpus.txt`, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json` and its `extract` references). Live `data/NVT/` and `analyses/NVT_2026-09-07/_pool_extracts/` were NOT read; `data/NVT/…` below is a citation label only. `NOSTRA_CONTINUATION_RUN_ROOT=analyses/NVT_2026-09-07`, so `balance-sheet-survival/01` was resolved inside that exact root and no prior run was searched.

**Plain-English glossary for the technical terms used below (§21).** **CFO** = cash from operations, the cash the business actually collected from trading, $501.0m in FY2024. **EBITDA** = operating profit before the non-cash charges for wearing out plant and writing down acquired intangibles, $675.6m in FY2024. **Accruals** = the part of reported profit that has not yet turned into cash. **M-score** (Beneish) = an 8-input statistical screen for earnings manipulation; NVT computes at **−2.67**, and more negative is cleaner. **F-score** (Dechow) = a misstatement-probability screen scaled so 1.00 is the average listed company; NVT computes at **1.92**. **RSST accruals** = the total accrual across working capital, long-lived operating items and financial assets, **2.23%** of average assets here. **Soft assets** = the share of the balance sheet that is neither cash nor plant — i.e. the part built on estimates — **92.9%** here. **Effective tax rate (ETR)** = tax charge ÷ pre-tax profit, **43.9%** in FY2024. **Net debt (strict basis, §15)** = total borrowings − cash, **$1,236.4m** at 30-Jun-2026.

## 2. Beneish M-Score (A8-14) — computed with python3, computation shown

**Primary computation: t = FY2024, t−1 = FY2023, every input from the FY2024 Form 10-K.**

| Component | Value FY2024 | Non-manipulator mean | Manipulator zone | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| DSRI (receivables outrunning sales) | **0.8933** | 1.031 | ≥1.465 | Clear — receivables *fell* relative to sales |
| GMI (gross margin deteriorating) | **1.0016** | 1.014 | ≥1.193 | Clear — gross margin flat at 40.2% vs 40.3% |
| AQI (asset quality softening) | **1.0148** | 1.039 | ≥1.254 | Clear |
| SGI (sales growth pressure) | **1.1263** | 1.134 | ≥1.607 | Clear — +12.6% growth, below the average non-manipulator |
| DEPI (depreciation rate slowing) | **0.9353** | 1.001 | ≥1.077 | Clear — the depreciation rate *accelerated* |
| SGAI (overhead vs sales) | **0.9812** | 1.054 | not banded (negative weight in M) | Overheads grew slower than sales |
| LVGI (leverage rising) | **1.0758** | 1.037 | ≥1.111 | Clear, but the closest component to its line — Trachte debt |
| TATA (accruals vs assets) | **−0.0386** | 0.018 | ≥0.031 | Clear by a wide margin — cash exceeded reported profit |

Composite, term by term as printed by the computation:

`M = −4.84 + 0.920(0.8933) + 0.528(1.0016) + 0.404(1.0148) + 0.892(1.1263) + 0.115(0.9353) − 0.172(0.9812) − 0.327(1.0758) + 4.679(−0.0386)`
`  = −4.84 + 0.8218 + 0.5288 + 0.4100 + 1.0047 + 0.1076 − 0.1688 − 0.3518 − 0.1808 = ` **−2.6684**

*Basis check:* recomputing AQI with every held-for-sale line stripped from both years gives AQI = 1.0312 and **M = −2.6618** — the verdict does not move.

| Composite / rule | Value | Green band | Amber band | Red band | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| M-score, FY2024 (filing basis) | **−2.67** | < −2.22, no component in zone | −2.22 to −1.78 | > −1.78 | **Green** |
| Components in manipulator zone, FY2024 | **0 of 7 banded** | 0 | 1–2 (Amber) | ≥3 | **Green** |

**Corroboration on the most recent year, tier-5 vendor basis (Capital IQ workbook, FY2025 vs FY2024).** The FY2025 10-K is not in the pool, so this is a vendor-sourced read, not a filing-sourced one, and it is reported as corroboration only.

| Component | Value FY2025 (vendor) | Manipulator zone | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|
| DSRI | **1.2486** | ≥1.465 | Elevated but clear |
| GMI | 1.0659 | ≥1.193 | Clear |
| AQI | 0.9344 | ≥1.254 | Clear |
| SGI | **1.2951** | ≥1.607 | Clear |
| DEPI | 1.0332 | ≥1.077 | Clear |
| SGAI | 0.9541 | not banded | — |
| LVGI | 0.8585 | ≥1.111 | Clear — leverage *fell* |
| TATA (continuing-ops NI $428.5m vs continuing-ops CFO $649.0m) | **−0.0322** | ≥0.031 | Clear |
| **M-score, FY2025 (vendor basis)** | **−2.07** | — | **Amber (−2.22 to −1.78), 0 of 7 components in zone** |

**Re-checking the two drivers, as the Amber band requires.** The FY2025 Amber is carried by DSRI 1.2486 and SGI 1.2951 — receivables per dollar of sales up ~25%, on sales up 29.5%. Both trace to one disclosed event: nVent bought the Electrical Products Group on 1-May-2025 for $979.6m and the completed purchase price allocation put **$97.7m of acquired accounts receivable** on the balance sheet at that date, while only eight months of the matching revenue landed in the FY2025 denominator [S3, Q2 FY26 10-Q, Note on Acquisitions]. `earnings/06` re-measured days-sales-outstanding against annualised latest-quarter revenue, which removes exactly that lag, and got **57.4 days (Dec-24) → 59.3 (Dec-25) → 60.1 (Jun-26)** — +3.3% then +1.3%, well inside its own 10% flag [S6, §3]. The Amber is an acquisition artefact, not a collections signal.

**One arithmetic trap worth naming, because it flips the answer.** If FY2025 TATA is computed on the **total-company** basis — net income of $710.2m, which includes the $281.7m gain on the Thermal Management disposal, against reported CFO of $465.2m, which is *reduced* by $183.8m of operating cash that left through discontinued operations — TATA becomes **+0.0358, inside the manipulator zone**, and M rises to **−1.75, above Beneish's cutoff**. That reading is wrong on both ends of the ratio: it charges a non-operating disposal gain to the numerator and a disposal tax payment to the denominator. Beneish specifies net income from **continuing** operations, and the matched continuing-operations pair (−$220.5m of accruals, TATA −0.0322) is the one used above. Anyone quoting a Beneish score above the cutoff for nVent's FY2025 has almost certainly made this mismatch.

## 3. Dechow F-Score & Accrual Battery (A8-17, A8-18) — computed with python3, computation shown

**Primary: FY2024. Inputs from the FY2024 10-K except `ΔCASH_SALES` and `ΔROA`, which need the 31-Dec-2022 balance sheet and are vendor-sourced.**

Working, as printed:
- `WC` (working capital) 454.8 → 494.0, **ΔWC = +39.2**
- `NCO` (non-current operating) 4,288.4 → 4,767.4, **ΔNCO = +479.0** (Trachte goodwill and intangibles)
- `FIN` (financial assets less debt) −1,780.7 → −2,155.0, **ΔFIN = −374.3** (the debt that paid for Trachte)
- sum **+143.9** ÷ average total assets 6,448.3 = **RSST 2.23%**
- `pred = −7.893 + 0.790(0.02232) + 2.518(0.00045) + 1.191(0.00002) + 1.979(0.92886) + 0.171(0.11098) − 0.932(−0.05106) + 1.029(1) = −4.94044`
- `probability = e^(−4.94044) / (1 + e^(−4.94044)) = 0.007101` → **F = 0.007101 ÷ 0.0037 = 1.919**

| Test | Value FY2024 | Green band | Red band | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| **Dechow F-score** (1.00 = average company) | **1.92** | <1.00 | ≥1.85 (substantial; ≥2.45 high) | **Red — band tripped** | computed above from [S1] + [S4] |
| RSST accruals / average assets | **2.23%** | ≤3% | ≥10% | **Green** | [S1, Balance Sheets p.41] |
| Soft assets % of total assets | **92.89%** (FY2023 91.89% → rising +1.0pp) | <50% | >65% and rising | **Red — band tripped** | [S1, p.41] |
| Δ receivables / average assets | **0.045%** | <2% | ≥5% with no acquisition explaining it | **Green** | [S1, p.41] |
| Δ inventory / average assets | **0.002%** | <2% | ≥5% with no acquisition explaining it | **Green** | [S1, p.41] |
| ΔROA (return on assets) | **−5.11pp** (10.25% → 5.15%) | — | rising ROA is the manipulation direction | Green — ROA *fell* | [S1, p.40]; [S4] for the Dec-2022 asset base |
| A8-18 — issuance in a flagged year | **$500.0m of long-term debt + $3.4m of employee shares issued in FY2024, a year in which the F composite is ≥1.85 but TATA is −0.0386** | none while flagged | issued while F ≥1.85 **or** TATA ≥0.031 (RF-ACC-004) | **Amber — see below** | [S1, p.42] |

**Sensitivity on the two vendor-dependent inputs.** Setting `ΔCASH_SALES` and `ΔROA` to zero gives **F = 1.80** — Amber, not Red. So the vendor-sourced inputs move the composite by 0.12 and sit on either side of the 1.85 line. The composite's placement is therefore not robust to that one basis choice, and this is stated rather than rounded away.

**Decomposition — what actually carries the 1.92.** The computation was re-run with terms switched off:

| Configuration | F-score |
|---|---:|
| Every accrual input at nVent's actual value, but soft assets = 0 and no issuance | **0.11** |
| Soft assets and the issuance dummy at nVent's values, every accrual input = 0 | **1.76** |
| Soft assets alone (no issuance) | **0.63** |
| A company with every input at zero and no issuance (the model's floor) | **0.10** |

**Read that table before reading the headline.** nVent's *accrual* content — the part of the model that measures profit booked ahead of cash — scores **0.11, about one-tenth of an average company**. The entire trip over 1.85 comes from two structural terms: a balance sheet that is 92.9% soft assets (weight 1.979, contributing +1.838) and a binary dummy for having issued any security at all (weight 1.029). A company with perfectly clean accruals that is intangible-heavy and issues a bond scores ~1.76 before it books a single dollar of anything. That is the model behaving as specified, not a finding about nVent.

**What the soft-asset number does mean.** It is not nothing. At 31-Dec-2024, goodwill of $2,221.8m plus net intangibles of $1,587.0m is **$3,808.8m — 56.6% of total assets and 117.6% of the $3,237.6m of shareholders' equity** [S1, p.41]. Add $1,276.1m of assets held for sale and the non-cash, non-plant share reaches 92.9%. Concretely: most of what nVent's balance sheet says it owns is management's estimate of the future cash flows of businesses it bought, tested annually for impairment — and Deloitte's single Critical Audit Matter for FY2024 was precisely that class of estimate (the $206.6m Trachte customer-relationship intangible, valued on a multi-period excess-earnings model with management-set margin, growth, discount and attrition assumptions) [S1, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, 18-Feb-2025]. That is an impairment and valuation exposure, and it belongs in the risk register. It is not evidence that revenue or profit is fabricated, and the accrual half of this same battery says the opposite.

**Corroboration, FY2025, tier-5 vendor basis:** **F = 1.91**, also above the 1.85 line, on RSST 6.01% (Amber, between the 3% and 10% lines), ΔREC 4.80%, ΔINV 1.64%, soft assets **88.07% — falling** from 92.89%, ΔROA +5.31pp, ISSUE = 1 ($275.0m of long-term debt drawn) [S4]. The ΔREC of 4.80% sits just under its 5% Red line, and the band's own carve-out applies: stripping the $97.7m of receivables acquired with EPG takes it to **3.36%** [S3, Note on Acquisitions]. The one input that got worse — RSST 6.01% — is the EPG purchase accounting itself: $975.7m of cash acquisitions adding goodwill and intangibles to `ΔNCO` [S4, CIQ Cash Flow, `Cash Acquisitions`].

**A8-18 graded Amber, and why not Red.** The letter of the Red band is met — securities were issued in a year whose F composite is ≥1.85. The band's stated purpose is "books dressed for a raise," and every piece of evidence points the other way: TATA is **−0.0386** (cash exceeded reported profit by $260.2m, the opposite of the flagged direction), CFO/PAT was **2.08×**, cash taxes paid rose to $120.2m, and the $500.0m issue is disclosed acquisition financing for Trachte, a deal whose purchase accounting Deloitte examined as its Critical Audit Matter. The trigger is also partly circular here: the issuance dummy is itself one of the two terms that pushes F over 1.85. Graded **Amber**, with the divergence stated rather than resolved silently. **RF-ACC-004 is not emitted.** It would be emitted if a future year showed issuance alongside a positive TATA or a materially higher RSST.

## 4. Cash Authenticity (A8-19)

| Test | Value | Band | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|

## 12. Forensics Read

**The accrual evidence says these books are clean, and it says so on every measure that matters.** The Beneish M-score computed from the FY2024 10-K is **−2.67 with zero of seven components in the manipulator zone** — receivables fell relative to sales, gross margin was flat, the depreciation rate accelerated, and total accruals were **negative $260.2m** (cash exceeded reported profit). CFO/PAT has run 0.92–2.08× for five years, CFO/EBITDA 69–79% for four, cash taxes paid rose 37.7% while revenue rose 31.0%, the $2.5bn backlog management quotes is the same number the 10-Q discloses as a contractual ASC 606 performance obligation, and the effective tax rate in the last audited year was **43.9%, eighteen points above statutory** — fabricated profit does not pay $120.2m of cash tax at above the statutory rate.

**The one number that trips a red band is the Dechow F-score at 1.92, and the decomposition matters more than the headline.** Re-running the model with terms switched off shows nVent's *accrual* content scores **0.11 — about a tenth of an average company**; the entire trip over 1.85 comes from two structural terms, a balance sheet that is 92.9% soft assets and a binary dummy for having issued any security at all, which together produce ~1.76 before a single dollar is booked. Set the two vendor-dependent inputs to zero and F falls to 1.80, below the line. So RF-ACC-001 is recorded honestly, and it is equally honestly reported as a model artefact of an intangible-heavy acquirer rather than a manipulation signal. **The Score Cap Rules floor does not apply** — it requires RF-ACC-001 with ≥3 Beneish manipulator-zone components (nVent has zero) or a cash-authenticity failure (none).

**The real finding underneath that artefact is worth keeping.** Goodwill plus intangibles of $3,808.8m is **117.6% of shareholders' equity**, tangible book value is **negative $571.2m**, and Deloitte's single Critical Audit Matter was exactly this class of estimate. Most of what this balance sheet says nVent owns is management's forecast of what four acquired businesses will earn, and the Maverick Power deal will add more. That is an impairment and valuation exposure for the risk register — not a revenue-recognition one. The three softer signals sit alongside it: bad-debt coverage has fallen from 2.93% to 1.69% of receivables while the book doubled (small, ~2% of profit, but moving the wrong way); "one-off" restructuring and acquisition costs recur every single year; and leverage touched the 3.00× Red line at FY2024, was rescued by a divestiture rather than by repayment, and is heading back to ~2.4× on the next deal — a capital-allocation question for `02`, not an accounting one.

**What a rational minority holder should conclude, and what should keep them honest.** On the evidence available, nVent's reported earnings are confirmed by its cash, its revenue is confirmed by its tax and its collections, its order book is contractual, and its auditor gave a clean opinion on both the accounts and the internal controls. The binding limitation is not the company's — it is the pool's: **the entire primary battery runs on a 20-month-old FY2024 Form 10-K, because the FY2025 10-K (filed 17-Feb-2026) was never collected.** The FY2025 corroboration is tier-5 vendor data, and on that basis the M-score drifts into Amber at −2.07, driven by an acquisition's opening receivables. Collect the FY2025 10-K and re-run both batteries before anyone treats this Green as current.

**Score Cap Rules — explicit statement for the synthesis.** RF-ACC-001 is triggered on the Dechow composite, but the MODULE_RULES cap row requires **"RF-ACC-001 with ≥3 manipulator-zone components, or RF-ACC-002."** nVent has **zero** Beneish components in the manipulator zone in both computed years, and RF-ACC-002 (cash authenticity) does not fire. **Therefore the Accounting-Forensics risk floor of 70 and the Governance risk floor of 60 do NOT apply.** The score of 29/100 stands on its evidence rows. Per that same cap row, this finding is routed to `earnings/06` for cross-check in the synthesis — and `earnings/06`'s independent accrual-flag table triggered one of six rows (deferred revenue, the mildest), which is consistent with this read.

**Confidence limitation carried to the synthesis (not a Score Cap row, but it belongs in the verdict).** The primary battery runs on a **20-month-old** FY2024 Form 10-K because the FY2025 10-K, filed 17-Feb-2026, was not collected into this pool. Every FY2025 figure above is tier-5 vendor corroboration. This is a data-collection gap, not a company disclosure failure, and it caps confidence in the currency — not the direction — of this read.

# Regulatory, Legal & Compliance — NVT

**Run type:** full sweep, 2026-09-07. `NOSTRA_CONTINUATION_RUN_ROOT` is set (`analyses/NVT_2026-09-07`), so no prior-dated `management-governance` folder was globbed, searched or read, and the only cross-module inputs used are the ones inside that exact root. This is a first-run company sweep, not a delta-refresh.

**Coverage headline — the sweep RAN.** SEC EDGAR (filing index, submissions, full-text UPLOAD/CORRESP), the SEC staff comment-letter correspondence itself, CourtListener/RECAP federal dockets, OpenSanctions' consolidated sanctions/PEP/MDB-debarment screen, Good Jobs First Violation Tracker, Fitch's rating action as reported, the company's own SEC-filed FWP naming its agency ratings, the 2026 DEF 14A, and dated adverse-media batteries were all reachable and were used. Five sources refused automated reads and are recorded as **coverage notes, never as evidence of absence**: `spglobal.com` ratings article (403), `violationtracker.goodjobsfirst.org` record-detail page (403, though the parent summary was obtained via the indexed page), `dockets.justia.com` (403), `nvent.com/about-nvent/EthicsandCompliance` (403), and PACER itself (paid — the Vertiv complaint could not be read). Nothing below is a filings-only profile presented as a clearance.

**Jurisdiction & regime (from `00_governance-data-triage`, §5A).** US/SEC **domestic filer** — Form 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K / DEF 14A / Form 4 / 11-K, Commission file **001-38265**, CIK **1720635**. Issuer incorporated in **Ireland** (CRO **605257**), UK tax-resident, principal executive offices London, US management office Minneapolis. **One listing exchange: the New York Stock Exchange, ticker NVT**, listed 2018-05-01. US GAAP, USD in millions, fiscal year ends 31 December. All documents English — no translation required and **no language-based gap is recorded** (CLAUDE.md §27). India/SEBI instruments (SEBI orders, NSE/BSE quarterly fine files, PIT/SAST disclosures, wilful-defaulter lists) are **genuinely Not Applicable** to this regime and are never scored as missing data.

**Net-worth denominator used for every materiality test below:** total equity **$3,986.9m** at 2026-06-30 [`Q2 FY26 10-Q`, consolidated balance sheet].

**Disqualifier deference (Hard Rule — reported verbatim, not re-adjudicated).** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`, item 6 "Active regulatory enforcement action on financial reporting", answered **N**, verbatim: *"No SEC investigation, subpoena, Wells notice, consent order, DOJ matter or civil penalty appears anywhere in the corpus (zero hits on each term)… The latest filing says 'There have been no material developments with respect to the legal proceedings previously disclosed'."* Its §3 Verdict-Lock Signal reads verbatim: *"No verdict-lock. The synthesizer is free to score this business on its merits; nothing in this scan overrides other scores."* This module does not re-decide that lock. It owns the spectrum below it, and that spectrum is what follows.
