## 2. Compliance Hygiene (A9-06, A7-01)

### Exchange-fine register — 8 quarters, ALL exchanges

**Regime note (Hard Rule — bands never fire against a structure the regime dictates).** NVT is listed on **one** exchange, the NYSE. The NYSE regime has **no quarterly listing-fine file** of the kind SEBI LODR requires of NSE and BSE; continued-listing enforcement runs through **Section 802 non-compliance notifications** (which a US issuer must disclose by press release and 8-K), the annual CEO certification, and ultimately a Form 25 delisting. So this item is answered on the axes the regime actually has. Recording "no NYSE quarterly fine file" as missing data would be the §27 twin of marking a non-US company's data missing for want of a 10-K.

| Quarter | Exchange | Fine / non-compliance item | Amount | Reason | Source |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Q3 2024 through Q2 2026 (8 consecutive quarters) | **NYSE (sole listing)** | **None found.** No Section 802.01 non-compliance notification, no compliance plan, no late-filing delinquency notice, no suspension notice, no Form 25 or 25-NSE. The security has traded continuously since 2018-05-01 | $0 | — | Web: SEC EDGAR submissions and filing index, CIK 1720635, retrieved 2026-09-07 (no Form 25/25-NSE, no 8-K disclosing a listing deficiency); Web: NYSE-scoped non-compliance query, 2026-09-07, 0 attributable results |
| Same 8 quarters | NSE / BSE / any other exchange | **Not Applicable — nVent is listed on no other exchange.** The India/SEBI quarterly fine register is not an instrument of this regime | — | — | `FY24 10-K` and `Q2 FY26 10-Q` cover pages, "Securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b)": Ordinary Shares, NYSE, ticker NVT — one line only |

**A9-06 verdict: Green.** Nil across eight quarters on the only exchange the company lists on, established from the exchange-enforcement axes that exist in this regime rather than from an absent India-style fine file.

### Filing timeliness — 12 quarters (and beyond)

Deadlines applied are the US large-accelerated-filer statutory clocks: **10-K within 60 days of fiscal-year end; 10-Q within 40 days of quarter end**; Form 8-K within four business days of the triggering event.

| Signal | Raw value | Green band | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Results filed on time (last 12 quarters, Q3 2023 → Q2 2026) | **12 / 12 on time.** 10-Qs: 2023-10-27 (Q3'23, 27 days), 2024-05-03 (32), 2024-08-06 (37), 2024-11-01 (32), 2025-05-02 (31), 2025-08-01 (32), 2025-10-31 (31), 2026-05-01 (31), 2026-07-31 (31). 10-Ks: 2024-02-20 (FY23, 51 days), 2025-02-18 (FY24, 49), **2026-02-17 (FY25, 48)** — every one inside the 40-day / 60-day clocks, with the widest 10-Q margin at 3 days to spare and the tightest 10-K margin at 9 days | 12/12 on time | **Green** | Web: SEC EDGAR filing index, CIK 1720635, forms 10-K/10-Q, retrieved 2026-09-07 |

| Material-event clock (US: Form 8-K within 4 business days; India Reg 30 clocks are **Not Applicable** to this regime) | **28 Form 8-Ks filed 2025-01-01 → 2026-09-07**, an active stream including Item 5.02 officer events on 2025-07-17 (Lammers retirement notified 2025-07-11 effective 2026-04-01; Leopold appointment), the CAO retirement announced 2026-06-11 and its reversal on 2026-08-14. **No 8-K Item 4.02 (non-reliance on previously issued financials) and no Item 4.01 (auditor change) was found.** No chronic lateness identified | No chronic lateness | **Green** | `07` Sweep Log, SEC EDGAR 8-K listing rows, 2026-09-07; Web: SEC EDGAR, CIK 1720635, 2026-09-07 |
| Exchange clarification requests / nudges | **None found** from the NYSE. **But two SEC staff comment letters did land** — 2024-07-26 and 2024-09-03, with the company's response filed 2024-08-08 | None | **Amber** — the regulator, not the exchange, and a review rather than a nudge, but it is the same species of signal and it is not nil | SEC UPLOAD 2024-07-26 / 2024-09-03; nVent CORRESP 2024-08-08 |
| Rumour verification (≤24h where mandated) | **Not Applicable** — no rumour-verification obligation exists in the US/SEC regime; this is a SEBI LODR instrument | — | **Not Applicable (regime)** | `00_governance-data-triage`, §5A |
| **Disclosure COMPLETENESS (the second half of A7-01)** | **Three staff comments, all sustained by the company.** An "Other" category was being included in consolidated reportable-segment totals when it is not a reportable segment; a non-GAAP measure (**consolidated segment income**) was presented **without a reconciliation to the comparable GAAP measure and without stating how management uses it**; and non-GAAP measures were not clearly labelled as non-GAAP. All three were corrected in the 2024-08-06 filings and the earnings release of the same date | No regulator-required correction to how results are presented | **Amber** | nVent CORRESP 2024-08-08 (`0001720635-24-000051`), quoted verbatim in Section 1 |

**A7-01 verdict: Amber.** Timeliness is unambiguously Green — twelve consecutive quarters on time, three annual reports on time, and not one late-filing notification in eight years as a public company. Completeness is not. The measure the SEC made the company stop presenting on a consolidated basis without a reconciliation — **segment income** — is the same measure `00_governance-data-triage` records the CEO uses *"for setting incentive compensation targets"*, and it is the same measure `business-model/12_red-flags-sweep` scored at 55/100 (inverted) for excluding the amortisation the company's own acquisitions create. Those qualifiers travel: `12_red-flags-sweep` graded it a **disclosed item, not an integrity finding**, and that is how it is carried here too. What this row adds is that the presentation was not merely aggressive by an analyst's lights — the SEC's own staff required it changed. **No RF-REG-002:** RF-REG-002 fires on delayed results or delayed material disclosure, and neither occurred.

**A14-03 verdict: Green.** A top-tier bank consortium consistent with the company's size, and then some: **nothing in the corporate debt stack is secured, and nothing is pledged** [`balance-sheet-survival/01`, §1]. The only "secured debt" a data vendor shows is $140.5m of operating-lease liabilities secured by the leased assets themselves. There is no obscure lender, no high-cost lender, no asset-backed or receivables-factoring reliance, and — the test that actually matters — **no lender flight mid-cycle**: in the last fifteen months the company added a $600m committed unsecured revolver, upgraded its bondholders' guarantee package, and secured a bridge commitment from a global bank for its largest-ever deal. Good banks leaving is information; good banks arriving is information too. ## 8. Litigation-Register Reconciliation (A9-10)

**The company's own account, first.** Item 3 of the FY24 10-K discloses litigation **by CATEGORY, not by case**: *"We have been made parties to a number of actions filed or have been given notice of potential claims relating to the conduct of our business, including those pertaining to commercial disputes, product liability, asbestos, environmental, safety and health, patent infringement and employment matters"*, with the assessment that *"a material impact on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows from any such future claims or potential claims is unlikely"*. Note 18 (FY24) and Note 15 (Q2 FY26) add: *"We are subject to disputes, administrative proceedings and other claims arising out of the normal conduct of our business… On the basis of information currently available, management does not believe that existing proceedings and claims will have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements."* The most recent filing says: *"There have been no material developments with respect to the legal proceedings previously disclosed in Item 3 of our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K"* [`Q2 FY26 10-Q, Part II Item 1`]. **Item 103 of Regulation S-K permits exactly this treatment for ordinary routine litigation incidental to the business** — so a case being unnamed is not by itself an omission; the test is whether a MATERIAL case is missing.

This table is coverage only — `10_contingent-liabilities-and-commitments` owns every amount.

## 9. Read

**Clean record, machinery real — with two named soft spots.** After a logged sweep of SEC enforcement, DOJ, federal dockets, the consolidated sanctions and debarment screen, the aggregated US regulatory-penalty database and both rating agencies the company actually engages, the public record adds nothing adverse to nVent's self-portrait: no enforcement action, no investigation, no forensic audit, no rating downgrade or non-cooperation tag, no listing deficiency, no insider-trading order, no sanctions match, and twelve consecutive quarters of filings inside the statutory clock with not one late-filing notification in eight years as a public company. The compliance machinery is more than ornamental — a board-adopted code, a third-party helpline with an explicit non-retaliation clause, an insider-trading policy that names the General Counsel as owner of the trading window and bars hedging and pledging, and a lender group moving toward the company rather than away from it.

**The single worst legal/regulatory fact is not a case — it is that the SEC's own staff had to make this company reconcile a non-GAAP measure it was publishing without a reconciliation.** In 2024 the Division of Corporation Finance told nVent that "Other" did not belong in its reportable-segment totals, that consolidated **segment income** needed a GAAP reconciliation and a stated management use, and that its non-GAAP measures needed labelling as such. nVent fixed all three. That is a small event with a long shadow, because segment income is the measure `00_governance-data-triage` records the CEO uses *"for setting incentive compensation targets"* — and it travels with its qualifier: `business-model/12_red-flags-sweep` graded that a **disclosed item, not an integrity finding**, and nothing here upgrades it.

**Nothing in this module belongs in front of the synthesis as a cap.** No red flag fired; the Non-Negotiable Gate is untouched by anything found here; `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`'s "no verdict-lock" stands unchallenged. Two things go forward as watch items rather than findings: the **Russian subsidiary**, whose current group status and Russian-language record are both unswept and which no post-divestiture Exhibit 21 in this pool can settle; and the **agencies' verdict on Maverick Power**, announced fourteen days before this run, which takes pro-forma net leverage to roughly 2.43x against a Fitch expectation of *"below 2.5x"* — the closest thing to a live rating question this company has.
